records.title: Strategy & Operations - Director and Service Line Leader - Quality
records.description:
Impact Advisors, LLC is a nationally recognized healthcare management consulting firm delivering Best in KLAS advisory, implementation, and optimization services. We are driven by a commitment to exceed client expectations and are proud to be a trusted partner to many of the nation's leading healthcare organizations. Our mission to drive patient-centered, value-driven outcomes has earned us prestigious industry accolades. To learn more about us, visit www.impact-advisors.com

**Job Overview**

Impact Advisors is seeking a dynamic and motivated Director-level healthcare leader with deep experience in healthcare quality performance, clinical documentation integrity, hospital quality ratings, and patient safety improvement. This role is responsible for delivery and business development for new and existing client relationships. You will partner with provider organizations to assess current quality and clinical documentation performance, identify improvement opportunities, and develop actionable strategies related to healthcare quality ratings, CMS Star scores, Leapfrog Safety Grade, Case Mix Index and accurate DRG documentation. Healthcare consulting experience is preferred, but candidates must have direct hospital-based experience in these areas.

**Responsibilities**

* **Sales:** Maintaining and leading $3.5M - $5.0M in annual sales for quality and clinical documentation engagements
* **Oversee client engagements as the client-facing Director**
* **Manage 6-8 full-time employees and 3-5 contractors at a time across 3-5 quality projects**
* **Interpret complex quality analytic analysis and conduct analysis independently**
* **Independently lead Assessments for quality and CDI performance**
* **Mentor project teams and lead business development for the quality service line**
* **Develop methodology internally to use for ongoing client engagements as the solutions evolve / grow**

**Qualifications**

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, public health, nursing, business, or a related field required; master’s degree preferred.
* **Experience:** Significant experience in a hospital or health system setting related to healthcare quality ratings, CMS scores, Leapfrog, and safety ratings is required. Experience operating at the consulting Director level is strongly preferred. Healthcare consulting experience and client-facing engagement leadership are preferred, but not required.
* **Preferred credentials:** Relevant industry certifications or clinical credentials are a plus.
* **Healthcare quality and safety expertise:** Deep knowledge of quality measurement methodologies, ratings programs, patient safety frameworks, and performance improvement strategies.

* **Strategic consulting and analytics:** Strong ability to interpret complex healthcare data, synthesize insights, communicate recommendations to executive stakeholders, and drive measurable results in hospital operations or consulting environments.

* **Leadership and client relationship management:** Proven ability to lead teams, manage senior client relationships, influence decision-making, and support business growth in a consulting environment.

* **Technology:** Epic technical background and experience with Epic reporting and provider documentation workflows is preferred (Inpatient ClinDoc, Orders, Progress Notes Templates, OurPractice Advisories, SmartText, etc.)

For salaried positions, this role may also be eligible for an annual performance bonus. Additional benefits and perks may also be available, depending on the position and employment terms. This range reflects consideration of several factors, including skills, experience, training, certifications, and organizational needs.

**Our People and Culture**

At Impact Advisors, we cultivate a caring, fun, honest, and autonomous work environment. Our success stems from our associates' dedication and a shared mission to create a “Positive Impact.” We embrace diversity and inclusion, fostering an environment where all employees feel valued and empowered.

**Join Impact Advisors and make a real difference in healthcare.**

records.title: Senior Director, GMP Quality Assurance (Commercial)
records.description:
At Kailera, we are bold, authentic and committed to our mission of developing therapies that give people the power to transform their lives and elevate their overall health. Rooted in an entrepreneurial spirit and a team-oriented culture, we are working together to advance Kailera's mission to advance novel therapies for obesity and related conditions.
 
 
We are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes collaboration, integrity, and excellence. As we expand, we seek the most talented individuals with diverse backgrounds, cultures, perspectives, and experiences to join our team.

**What You'll Do:**

Kailera is preparing to bring its therapies to patients, and the Senior Director, GMP Quality Assurance will lead the quality strategy that gets us there. Reporting to the Head of Quality Assurance, you will be accountable for GMP Quality across drug substance, drug product, packaging/labeling, testing, stability, and product release as Kailera moves from late-stage clinical supply to commercial manufacturing and launch. You will develop and execute the commercial GMP Quality strategy, build the quality systems and team needed for a compliant and reliable commercial supply chain, and serve as a trusted quality leader with Technical Operations, Regulatory, Supply Chain, and our network of contract manufacturers and testing laboratories.

 

*Required location: Waltham, MA (hub-based, onsite 3-4 days per week) OR Remote (home-based, onsite at a hub 1 week every other month).*

 

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop and execute the commercial GMP Quality strategy and roadmap, aligned with company and functional objectives, to support registration, launch, and lifecycle supply of Kailera products
* Be accountable for the performance and results of the GMP Quality function, including key quality initiatives, goals, and product assets
* Evolve the Kailera Quality Management System from clinical phase to commercial readiness, including change control, deviations/CAPA, complaints, product quality reviews, supplier management, training, and data integrity
* Define GMP quality metrics and KPIs for Quality Management Review, and use trends to anticipate risks and drive continuous improvement across the manufacturing network
* Advise senior leadership on quality risks, compliance trade-offs, and changes in the global regulatory environment, translating external trends into Kailera's quality strategy
* Lead the quality aspects of commercial readiness, including oversight of process performance qualification (PPQ), process and analytical method validation, commercial specifications, and stability programs
* Lead pre-approval and pre-license inspection (PAI/PLI) readiness across Kailera and contract manufacturing sites; host or support health authority inspections and drive timely, effective responses and commitments
* Partner with Regulatory CMC to ensure commercial manufacturing and controls are consistent with marketing applications; provide QA review of CMC sections of regulatory filings, post-approval supplements, and variations
* Establish and oversee commercial batch record review and lot disposition, ensuring final disposition complies with approved registrations and supporting QP certification for EU supply
* Build post-market quality processes, including product complaint handling, regulatory reporting (e.g., Field Alert Reports), recalls, and annual product quality reviews.
* Oversee quality requirements for commercial packaging, labeling, artwork control, and serialization (DSCSA and other market requirements)
* Ensure Good Distribution Practice (GDP) compliance for commercial distribution, including qualification of third-party logistics providers, temperature excursion management, and returns
* Where applicable, integrate combination product and device quality requirements (e.g., 21 CFR Part 4) for drug-device presentations
* Develop and lead risk-based quality oversight of CDMOs, contract testing laboratories, and other GMP suppliers, including qualification, audits, and performance management.
* Negotiate and maintain commercial Quality Agreements and ensure adherence by Kailera and its partners
* Use independent judgment to resolve highly complex or novel quality issues, such as major deviations, OOS investigations, and supply disruptions, balancing patient safety, compliance, and supply continuity
* Direct cross-functional, multidisciplinary teams across Technical Operations, Supply Chain, Regulatory, and external partners to resolve quality events and implement improvements
* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing GMP Quality team as Kailera scales to commercial operations, including organizational design, hiring, and succession planning
* Drive followership by leading with trust, understanding, and adaptability; coach managers and team members, recognize contributions, and foster a culture of quality, accountability, and psychological safety
* Manage GMP Quality budget and resources, including the use of external consultants and auditors

 

**Required Qualifications:**

* 12+ years of GMP experience in the FDA-regulated pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry (or 10+ years with an advanced degree), including significant experience supporting commercial products
* Demonstrated success leading quality activities for product registration and commercial launch, including PPQ and PAI/PLI readiness
* 5+ years of people leadership experience, including building and developing teams
* Expert knowledge of cGMP and GDP requirements, including 21 CFR Parts 210, 211, and 11, EudraLex Volume 4 (including Annex 16), and ICH Q7, Q9, and Q10; working knowledge of 21 CFR Part 4 and DSCSA preferred
* Track record of successfully hosting or supporting FDA, EMA, and/or other health authority inspections
* Extensive experience leading quality oversight of CDMOs and contract laboratories, including audits and Quality Agreements
* Proficient in Veeva QualityDocs and Veeva QMS or a comparable electronic quality system
* Recognized expertise in GMP quality, with the judgment to give clear, risk-based quality advice that balances compliance with business needs
* Exceptional communication skills; tailors messages to executives, cross-functional partners, contract manufacturers, and health authorities, and explains the rationale behind decisions to build buy-in
* Proven ability to guide teams through complex change and ambiguity, anticipate problems before they escalate, and keep work focused on defined outcomes in a fast-paced, growing company
* Builds trusting relationships internally and externally, and navigates conflict through open dialogue and collaboration
* Brings creative, practical solutions to complex problems and encourages others to take calculated risks that challenge the status quo while maintaining compliance

 

**Education:**

* BA or BS degree in a scientific discipline required; advanced degree preferred

**For Full Time Roles:** This range represents the company's good-faith estimate of the salary at the time of posting. Actual pay may vary based on experience, skills, qualifications, location, and internal equity. We also offer comprehensive health coverage, flexible time off, paid holidays, and a year-end shutdown. Enjoy a monthly wellness stipend, generous 401(k) match, tuition reimbursement, commuter benefits, disability and life insurance, plus annual bonus opportunities and equity grants—because your well-being and future matter to us.

**EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY INFORMATION:**

Kailera Therapeutics, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer that does not discriminate on the basis of actual or perceived race (including traits historically associated with race, such as hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, creed, religion (including religious dress and grooming practices), national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, age (40 and over), sex or gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, pregnancy-related conditions, and lactation), gender identity or expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, marital status, military service and veteran status, physical or mental disability, genetic information, reproductive health decisions, domestic victim status, political affiliation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws and ordinances.

*E-Verify:*

Kailera Therapeutics, Inc. uses E-Verify to confirm the identity and employment eligibility of all new hires.

records.title: Administrative Director of Inpatient Quality and Operations, Department of Medicine

postedPay.title: Administrative Director of Inpatient Quality and Operations, Department of Medicine

records.description:
Department Overview:

The Department of Medicine (DoM) at OHSU is comprised of a diverse community of faculty, staff, clinicians, researchers, educators, and learners dedicated to advancing patient care, education, and research across ten divisions.

The Director of Inpatient Quality and Operations provides strategic leadership, operational oversight, quality management, and performance improvement support for inpatient clinical services across the Department of Medicine's ten specialty divisions and care sites. Reporting to the Vice Chair of Clinical Practice and partnering closely with the Vice Chair for Administration, this position serves as the Department's primary administrative leader for inpatient quality, patient safety, operational performance, and clinical effectiveness initiatives.

Function/Duties of Position:

Working collaboratively with DoM and OHSU Health quality leaders, division leadership, hospital operations, finance, revenue cycle, informatics, care management, nursing leadership, clinical documentation teams, and physician leaders, the Director advances the Department's inpatient quality, operational, clinical, and financial goals through the design, implementation, and oversight of standardized processes, performance improvement efforts, operational reporting, and strategic initiatives.

Emphasis is placed on quality programing and outcomes, patient safety, clinical documentation integrity, coding accuracy, revenue cycle performance, operational efficiency, provider productivity, inpatient capacity management, and growth planning across all Department of Medicine inpatient services. The Director supports a broad portfolio of inpatient programs spanning multiple clinical specialties and care settings.

This position functions within a highly matrixed environment and serves as a key liaison between departmental leadership and enterprise partners, ensuring alignment with OHSU Health strategic priorities, quality objectives, and high-reliability organizational principles.

**Inpatient Quality and Operations Leadership and Oversight**

* Work in direct partnership with the DoM Vice Chair of Clinical Practice, DoM Associate Vice Chair of Inpatient Services, Healthcare quality leaders, and other institutional leaders to oversee and coordinate quality-focused inpatient care across Department of Medicine divisions.
* Provide strategic administrative leadership and operational oversight for Department of Medicine inpatient programs and services.
* Serve as the Department's primary administrative leader for inpatient quality, patient safety, operational performance, and performance improvement initiatives.
* Partner with division heads, section heads, medical directors, healthcare administrators, quality leaders, and physician leaders to identify and address operational and quality barriers affecting patient safety, access, efficiency, provider experience, and clinical outcomes.
* Shape and implement standardized inpatient quality, safety, and operational best practices across medicine specialties.
* Coordinate departmental quality improvement initiatives focused on reducing medical errors, serious safety events, healthcare-associated infections, hospital-acquired conditions, avoidable readmissions, preventable complications, and patient harm.
* Lead administrative efforts related to inpatient quality programs, patient safety activities, inpatient capacity management, patient flow, consult services, discharge efficiency, care coordination, and service-line optimization.
* Support departmental participation in mortality reviews, safety event reviews, quality committees, accreditation activities, regulatory preparedness efforts, and institutional quality initiatives.
* Establish and maintain departmental quality and operational governance structures, including scorecards, dashboards, performance reviews, and accountability processes.
* Partner with healthcare quality teams to identify opportunities for improvement and coordinate development of corrective action plans.
* Serve as the primary administrative liaison between Department of Medicine leadership, inpatient programs, Healthcare quality teams, and hospital operations leadership.
* Monitor operational, quality, and patient safety performance measures and drive action planning to improve outcomes.
* Facilitate multidisciplinary teams and stakeholder groups responsible for advancing inpatient quality, safety, throughput, and operational effectiveness.

**Revenue Cycle, Billing, Coding, and Clinical Documentation Integrity**

* Serve as the Department's operational lead for inpatient professional revenue cycle performance.
* Partner with Revenue Cycle, Professional Coding, Clinical Documentation Integrity (CDI), Finance, Compliance, and physician leaders to improve revenue capture, reimbursement, and operational performance.
* Evaluate and improve inpatient provider documentation practices, coding accuracy, charge capture processes, and billing workflows.
* Lead provider education efforts related to documentation requirements, coding regulations, payer expectations, reimbursement methodologies, and compliance standards.
* Monitor inpatient professional fee performance, wRVU generation, Case Mix Index (CMI), coding trends, denials, reimbursement outcomes, and documentation quality measures.
* Develop dashboards and performance reporting tools that support transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Identify specialty-specific opportunities for revenue optimization, operational efficiency, and documentation improvement.

**Performance Improvement and Strategic Initiatives**

* Lead complex inpatient operational and quality improvement initiatives utilizing Lean, process improvement, project management, and change management methodologies.
* Design and implement department-wide initiatives focused on improving quality outcomes, patient safety, throughput, provider experience, financial performance, and operational consistency.
* Conduct workflow analyses and redesign efforts to eliminate inefficiencies, reduce variation in care delivery, and improve service performance.
* Collaborate with Quality, Analytics, Finance, Informatics, and Operations teams to establish measurable goals and monitor outcomes.
* Develop project charters, implementation plans, success metrics, and performance benchmarks for strategic initiatives.
* Support departmental strategic planning activities and implementation of enterprise priorities related to inpatient growth, quality, and operational excellence.
* Advance high-reliability organization principles and support compliance with accreditation and regulatory requirements.

**Data Analytics, Reporting, and Financial Performance**

* Develop and maintain operational, financial, quality, patient safety, and utilization reporting structures for departmental and divisional leadership.
* Establish and maintain comprehensive inpatient quality scorecards and dashboards.
* Monitor and analyze key performance indicators including:
 + Analyze trends in inpatient volumes, utilization, consult activity, throughput, revenue cycle performance, patient outcomes, and quality metrics.
 + Translate complex operational and quality data into actionable recommendations for leaders.
 + Benchmark Department performance against institutional, regional, and national metrics when available.
 + Support financial forecasting, business case development, and investment planning for inpatient growth initiatives.

**Stakeholder Engagement and Committee Leadership**

* Represent the Department of Medicine on institutional committees related to quality, patient safety, inpatient operations, revenue cycle, clinical documentation, care management, patient flow, and performance improvement.
* Build collaborative partnerships with hospital administrators, nursing leaders, physicians, quality teams, informatics, finance, and operational stakeholders.
* Provide subject matter expertise regarding inpatient quality, safety, operational performance, workflow redesign, and professional revenue optimization.
* Lead communication, stakeholder engagement, and change management activities for major inpatient initiatives.
* Support development of a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, patient safety, and operational excellence throughout Department of Medicine inpatient programs.

Required Qualifications:

**Education**

Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business, finance, or a related field is required. Master’s degree may substitute for one (1) year of experience.

**Experience**

* Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in clinical operations or healthcare administration, with at least two (2) years in a formal leadership role.
* Experience supporting inpatient hospital operations, quality improvement, patient safety, healthcare finance, revenue cycle, or operational excellence initiatives.
* Experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives within healthcare organizations.
* Experience working collaboratively with physician leaders, nursing leadership, and hospital operational teams.
* Experience developing performance metrics, scorecards, dashboards, and operational improvement plans.

**Competencies**

* Strong knowledge of inpatient healthcare operations and physician practice management.
* Strong knowledge of healthcare quality improvement, patient safety, performance measurement, and high-reliability organizational principles.
* Knowledge of inpatient reimbursement methodologies, documentation requirements, clinical coding, and revenue cycle practices.
* Knowledge of regulatory, accreditation, and quality reporting requirements affecting inpatient healthcare delivery.
* Advanced analytical, reporting, and data interpretation skills.
* Demonstrated ability to develop quality scorecards, operational dashboards, and executive-level performance reporting.
* Ability to analyze complex clinical, operational, financial, and quality data and translate findings into actionable improvement strategies.
* Demonstrated ability to manage large-scale operational and performance improvement initiatives across multiple clinical specialties.
* Experience leading multidisciplinary efforts focused on reducing medical errors, improving patient outcomes, and advancing a culture of safety.
* Excellent communication, facilitation, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
* Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes without direct authority.
* Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, Epic, reporting platforms, and healthcare analytics tools.
* Strong financial acumen, strategic planning, and business case development capabilities.

Preferred Qualifications:

**Education**

Master’s Degree in Health Care Administration, Business, Public Health or Nursing; or Bachelor’s degree with equivalent combination of education, experience and training.

**Experience**

* Eight or more years of progressively responsible healthcare operations, quality, or performance improvement experience.
* Academic medical center experience.
* Experience with inpatient physician billing and professional fee revenue cycle.
* Experience with quality reporting, patient safety programs, accreditation activities, and regulatory readiness.
* Experience with Epic reporting, provider productivity analysis, CDI initiatives, and coding optimization.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or process improvement certification or training.
* Matrix leadership experience.

**Competencies**

Demonstrated ability to leverage advanced analytics, financial modeling, forecasting tools, artificial intelligence-enabled technologies, and other data-driven methodologies to improve operational efficiency, inform strategic decision-making, optimize resource allocation, and support sustainable program growth.

Additional Details:

Professional office environment; may include occasional travel to affiliate and partner sites. In-person work schedule expected, with limited telework acceptable.

Operates in an environment with frequent interruptions, multiple competing priorities, and extensive interaction with faculty, staff, trainees, and institutional partners.

Physical location: Marquam Hill (primary)

Why apply to OHSU?: **We are Oregon's only public academic health center.** In addition to caring for patients, we lead groundbreaking research. We also train the next generation of health care professionals. As Portland's largest employer, we give you opportunities to learn and advance in a system of hospitals and clinics across Oregon and Southwest Washington. **All are welcome.** OHSU welcomes people of all ages, ethnicities, genders, national origins, religions and sexual orientations. We are striving to build an anti-racist, multicultural institution and encourage people with diverse backgrounds to apply. To request reasonable accommodation, contact askhr@ohsu.edu

records.title: DIRECTOR OF QUALITY AND RISK MANAGEMENT

postedPay.title: DIRECTOR OF QUALITY AND RISK MANAGEMENT

records.description:
**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Director of Quality and Risk Management is responsible for providing strategic leadership, oversight, and direction for both the Quality Management and Risk Management programs within the organization. This role develops, implements, and monitors a hospital-wide, data-driven quality improvement program designed to enhance patient outcomes, reduce medical errors, and minimize risks to patients, staff, visitors, and property. The Director ensures compliance with regulatory requirements (e.g., The Joint Commission (TJC), Title 22, Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS), and other applicable standards) and fosters a culture of continuous quality improvement and patient safety throughout the organization.

**ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS / RESPONSIBILITIES**

***Quality Management & Performance Improvement***

* Develop and Implement Quality Programs:

* Design, implement, and monitor a comprehensive, hospital-wide quality management and performance improvement program.
* Direct the collection, measurement, and analysis of quality data to identify trends and drive process improvements.
* Education and Training:

* Provide in-service education and training to clinical and administrative staff on quality improvement methodologies, regulatory standards, and data management.
* Serve as a subject matter expert and resource on quality improvement initiatives and continuous quality improvement (CQI) processes.
* Compliance and Reporting:

* Monitor compliance with TJC, Title 22, CMS, and other regulatory standards.
* Oversee the accuracy and timeliness of quality data submissions and reports for internal and external stakeholders.

***Risk Management***

* Manage Risk Programs:

* Oversee the organization’s Risk Management Program by developing and implementing strategies to identify, assess, and mitigate risks to patients, staff, visitors, and property.
* Coordinate the investigation and reporting of incidents, patient/visitor complaints, and potential liability events.
* Incident and Claims Management:

* Maintain and oversee the hospital-wide occurrence reporting system.
* Direct the investigation and documentation of incidents and claims, ensuring that trends are identified and appropriate corrective actions are taken.
* Serve as the primary liaison with internal departments, legal counsel, and external agencies regarding risk management issues and claim defense.
* Evidence Preservation and Litigation Support:

* Safeguard materials obtained during root cause analyses and ensure proper documentation and preservation of evidence.
* Negotiate settlements for minor claims within administrative authority and coordinate litigation support activities when necessary.

***Leadership & Strategic Integration***

* Cross-Functional Collaboration:

* Work closely with senior leadership, clinical staff, and departmental managers to integrate quality and risk management initiatives across the organization.
* Chair or participate in committees (e.g., Patient Safety/Risk Committee) to promote a unified approach to quality and risk management.
* Staff Development:

* Mentor and coach quality and risk management staff to foster professional growth and enhance departmental performance.
* Lead the development of rapid-cycle improvement teams and task forces to address quality and risk-related issues.
* Continuous Improvement:

* Actively participate in continuous quality improvement (CQI) initiatives and contribute to the overall strategic direction of the organization
* Support human resources and performance improvement efforts through active participation in team conferences, staff meetings, and orientation programs.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* General:
* The role primarily involves office work with extended periods of sitting, as well as occasional standing and walking.
* Manual Tasks:

* Frequent use of hands for typing, data entry, and document handling.
* Occasional lifting of light items up to 10–25 pounds may be required.
* Vision:
* No special vision requirements beyond standard capabilities.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

* The position is based in a typical office/hospital environment with standard ambient noise levels.
* Occasional exposure to areas with moderate activity levels.
* Reasonable accommodations may be made to permit qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

**Education:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Nursing or a healthcare-related field is required.
* Master’s Degree is preferred.

**Experience:**

* A minimum of five (5) years of quality and/or risk management experience in an acute care hospital setting is required.
* At least two (2) years of supervisory or administrative management experience is preferred.
* Experience in risk investigation, claims management, and regulatory compliance is highly desirable.

**Licenses/Certificates:**

* Certified Professional Healthcare Quality (CPHQ) is required or must be obtained within one year of hire.
* Other risk management or quality certifications are a plus.

**Skills and Abilities:**

* Demonstrated leadership and management skills with the ability to motivate teams, delegate responsibilities, and drive organizational change.
* In-depth knowledge of regulatory requirements including TJC, Title 22, CMS, and applicable local and federal regulations.
* Strong analytical skills with experience in data collection, performance measurement, statistical analysis, and quality management information systems.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and familiarity with healthcare information systems and databases.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills with proven ability to negotiate and resolve complex issues.

records.description:
**Quality/Risk Director Career Opportunity**

**Highly regarded and valued for your Quality/Risk Director expertise** 
Are you seeking a career that not only utilizes your skills but also aligns with your personal values, providing a profound sense of belonging and the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in patients' lives? Look no further than Encompass Health, the nation's leader in in-patient rehabilitation care. As a Quality/Risk Director, you will oversee a hospital-wide quality management program, collaborating with various stakeholders to monitor and enhance the quality of patient care services. Join a team that values collaboration, support, and inclusivity, and embark on a rewarding career close to home and close to your heart, complete with access to cutting-edge equipment and technology and a comprehensive benefits package from day one.

**A Glimpse into Our World** 
At Encompass Health, you'll experience the difference the moment you become a part of our team. Being at Encompass Health means aligning with a rapidly growing national inpatient rehabilitation leader. We take pride in the growth opportunities we offer and how our team unites for the greater good of our patients. Our achievements include being named one of the "World's Most Admired Companies" and receiving the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® Award, among other accolades, which is nothing short of amazing.

**Starting Perks and Benefits** 
At Encompass Health, we are committed to creating a supportive, inclusive, and caring environment where you can thrive. From **day one,** you will have access to:

* Affordable medical, dental, and vision plans for both full-time and part-time employees and their families.
* Generous paid time off that accrues over time.
* Opportunities for tuition reimbursement and continuing education.
* Company-matching 401(k) and employee stock purchase plans.
* Flexible spending and health savings accounts.
* A vibrant community of individuals passionate about the work they do!

**Become the Quality/Risk Director you've always aspired to be**

* Ensure compliance with regulatory agencies, accrediting bodies, corporate and hospital policies, and procedures. Develop, implement, and maintain quality assessment and improvement programs.
* Assess compliance with federal, state, and industry regulatory and accreditation standards, facilitating processes to remediate and/or maintain compliance. Provide organizational education related to regulations and standards and coordinate local, state, federal, and accreditation surveys.
* Use a variety of applications (including, but not limited to, PatCom, UDS, ORYX, and Press Ganey) to identify improvement opportunities, generate reports, research issues, identify resources, and access external databases.
* Ensure the update and maintenance of hospital plans, including the Provision of Care/Scope of Services, Leadership, Information Management, Utilization Review, Infection Control, and Patient Safety plans. Oversee risk management activities, including completion of incident reports, notice of potential claims, corrective action planning, and incident reporting to the Corporate Risk Manager.
* Coordinate the review, development, and implementation of hospital policies.
* .Communicate and collaborate with other departments to coordinate care and promptly resolve patient concerns or complaints.
* Celebrate the accomplishments and successes of our dedicated employees along the way.

**Qualifications**

* A bachelor's degree in healthcare or a related field is preferred.
* License or Certification as required by state regulations.
* Experience in Quality and/or Risk Management, including primary responsibility for performance improvement activities, regulatory compliance, conflict resolution, leadership, and risk management activities.

**The Encompass Health Way**

We proudly set the standard in care by leading with empathy, doing what's right, focusing on the positive, and standing stronger together. Encompass Health is a trusted leader in post-acute care with over 150 nationwide locations and a team of 36,000 exceptional individuals and growing!

At Encompass Health, we celebrate and welcome diversity in our inclusive culture. We provide equal employment opportunities regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, national origin, color, creed, age, mental or physical disability, or any other protected classification.

records.description:
Req ID: 11315

**Working Location: District Columbia, Washington; Massachusetts, Westborough; Pennsylvania, Center Valley**

**Workplace Flexibility: Remote**

 

***For more than 100 years, Olympus has focused on making people’s lives healthier, safer and more fulfilling.***

Every day, we live by our philosophy, True to Life, by advancing medical technologies and elevating the standard of patient care so people everywhere can fulfill their desires, dreams, and lives.

Our five Core Values empower us to achieve Our Purpose:

**Patient Focus, Integrity, Innovation, Impact and Empathy.**

 

Learn more about Life at Olympus: https://www.olympusamerica.com/careers.

**Job Description**
-------------------

Senior Director, Regulatory & Quality Counsel, Global, reports to the VP, Regulatory & Quality Counsel, Global, and serves as a strategic legal partner to the Company's global Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, and Medical Safety organizations. This role provides expert legal counsel on the full spectrum of medical device regulatory, quality, compliance, enforcement, and commercialization matters across the product lifecycle, including emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), software as a medical device (SaMD), digital health, and connected medical devices products.

Senior Director, Regulatory & Quality Counsel, Global will independently manage significant legal projects, advise leadership on complex regulatory risks, support interactions with FDA and global health authorities, lead legal support for regulatory inspections and enforcement actions, and provide strategic guidance on remediation programs, product development, commercialization, and global compliance initiatives. The role also provides leadership and oversight to other attorneys supporting the Global QARA organization.

This role covers multiple jurisdictions across the Americas, as well as other key business centers located in Japan, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, China, Asia Pacific.

**Job Duties**
--------------

* Strategic QARA Legal Support
 
 + Act as a strategic legal partner to Global Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs teams and business clients, providing practical, risk-based legal advice on regulatory, quality, compliance, and enforcement matters.
 + Provide day-to-day legal counseling to internal stakeholders on regulatory and quality matters affecting the development, manufacture, distribution, promotion, and post-market management of medical devices to support compliance with global medical device regulations.
* Global Regulatory Compliance
 
 + Counsel the business on all aspects of medical device regulation throughout the product lifecycle, including research and development, clinical activities, regulatory submissions, commercialization, post-market surveillance, quality systems compliance, and lifecycle management.
 + Assist business teams in obtaining FDA and other global regulatory clearances, approvals, registrations, licenses, and certifications necessary to market medical device products.
 + Support compliance with post-market regulatory requirements, including reporting obligations, field actions, recalls, and corrective actions.
 + Draft, review, and provide legal guidance regarding policies, procedures, quality system documentation, guidance documents, product manuals, training materials, and governance documents.
* Inspections, Enforcement, and Remediation
 
 + Advise the business regarding FDA inspections and inspections conducted by global regulatory authorities, including Notified Bodies, Health Canada, MHRA, PMDA, TGA, ANVISA, and other competent authorities.
 + Support inspection readiness activities, inspection management, inspector interactions, document production, escalation processes, and post-inspection response strategies. Provide legal advice regarding inspectional observations (e.g., Form 483 observations), warning letters, import alerts, recalls, detentions and import restrictions, regulatory investigations, and other enforcement actions by FDA and global health authorities. Advise and assist in drafting responses to inspectional observations, regulatory inquiries, Warning Letters, and other enforcement communications.
 + Provide strategic legal oversight for remediation and quality-system improvement programs arising from FDA or other regulatory authority findings.
* Import and Export Compliance
 
 + Advise on FDA and global medical device import and export requirements. Provide legal support regarding import-for-export requirements, import alerts, detentions, product admissibility issues, global distribution and supply chain activities, and resolution of import restrictions and enforcement actions.

**Job Qualifications**
----------------------

**Required:**

* Minimum of 10 years of legal experience supporting FDA-regulated medical device companies.
* Combination of in-house counsel, law firm, and/or regulatory agency experience, including FDA experience.
* Significant experience advising medical device businesses on regulatory, quality, compliance, and enforcement matters.
* Demonstrated experience counseling senior leadership regarding global recalls, FDA inspections, Form 483 observations, Warning Letters, Import Alerts, and other enforcement actions.
* Experience leading or advising on complex remediation programs arising from FDA or other regulatory authority findings.
* Experience supporting inspections and interactions with FDA and global regulatory authorities.
* Experience advising on medical device import/export requirements and regulatory trade compliance issues.
* Experience managing complex cross-functional legal and compliance initiatives in a global environment.
* Deep expertise in medical device regulatory and quality law.
* Strong understanding of FDA medical device requirements and global regulatory frameworks.
* Strong understanding of enforcement trends and evolving regulatory requirements affecting digital health and AI-enabled medical devices.
* Excellent judgment and ability to provide practical, business-oriented legal advice in complex situations.
* Strong leadership, communication, negotiation, and collaboration skills.
* Proven ability to influence executive leadership and effectively manage multiple high-priority matters simultaneously.
* Ability to operate successfully in a fast-paced, highly regulated, global environment.
* Flexibility to work across global time zones, including early morning or evening calls in support of a large, global, matrixed organization.
* Travel up to 15% of time is anticipated.
 

**Preferred:**

* Experience supporting Class I, II, and III medical devices.
* Experience advising on Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), Software in a Medical Device (SiMD), connected medical devices, digital health platforms, mobile medical applications, remote monitoring technologies, and AI/ML-enabled medical devices.
* Experience with EU MDR, UK MDR, ISO 13485, and other global medical device regulatory frameworks.
* Experience managing external regulatory counsel and consultants.

**Why join Olympus?**

We offer a holistic employee experience supporting personal and professional well-being through meaningful work, equitable offerings, and a connected culture.

 

**Equitable Offerings you can count on:**

* Competitive salaries, annual bonus and 401(k)\* with company match
* Comprehensive medical, dental, vision coverage effective on start date
* 24/7 Employee Assistance Program
* Free live and on-demand Wellbeing Programs
* Generous Paid Vacation and Sick Time
* Paid Parental Leave and Adoption Assistance\*
* 12 Paid Holidays
* On-Site Child Daycare, Café, Fitness Center\*\*

**Connected Culture you can embrace:**

* Work-life integrated culture that supports an employee centric mindset
* Offers onsite, hybrid and field work environments
* Paid volunteering and charitable donation/match programs
* Employee Resource Groups
* Dedicated Training Resources and Learning & Development Programs
* Paid Educational Assistance

* US Only

\*\*Center Valley, PA and Westborough, MA

 

**Are you ready to be a part of our team?**

Learn more about our benefits and incentives: https://www.olympusamerica.com/careers/benefits-perks.

 

The anticipated base pay range for this full-time position is $224,401.00 - $359,041.00 / year, plus potential for annual bonus (subject to plan eligibility and other requirements). This pay range represents the National Average of the range, and may vary depending on the location of the individual.

 

Olympus considers a variety of factors when determining actual compensation for this position, including level of experience, working location, and relevant education and certifications.

 

At Olympus, we are committed to Our Purpose of making people’s lives healthier, safer and more fulfilling. As a global medical technology company, we partner with healthcare professionals to provide best-in-class solutions and services for early detection, diagnosis and minimally invasive treatment, aiming to improve patient outcomes by elevating the standard of care in targeted disease states.

 

For more than 100 years, Olympus has pursued a goal of contributing to society by producing products designed with the purpose of delivering optimal outcomes for its customers around the world.

 

Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, Olympus employs more than 31,000 employees worldwide in nearly 40 countries and regions. Olympus Corporation of the Americas, a wholly owned subsidiary of Olympus Corporation, is headquartered in Center Valley, Pennsylvania, USA, and employs more than 5,200 employees throughout locations in North and South America. For more information, visit www.olympusamerica.com.

 

**You Belong at Olympus**

We are deeply committed to fostering a respectful, fair, and welcoming workplace for all individuals, perspectives, and lifestyles. We believe in fostering a non-discriminatory, inclusive work environment where everyone feels a sense of belonging, in full compliance with legal standards. Empathy and unity are core to our company culture, empowering employees to contribute fully and flourish. We warmly encourage all who wish to bring their talents to Olympus to apply.

 

***Applicants Requesting Accommodations:*** Olympus is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Olympus will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations for the hiring process. If reasonable accommodation is needed, please contact OCAAccommodations@olympus.com. If your disability impairs your ability to email, you may call our HR Compliance Manager at 1-888-Olympus (1-888-659-6787).

 

**Let’s realize your potential, together.**

It is the policy of Olympus to extend equal employment and advancement opportunity to all applicants and employees without regard to race, color, national origin (including language use restrictions), citizenship status, religious creed (including dress and grooming practices), age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, medical conditions related to pregnancy, childbirth and/or breastfeeding), gender, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, marital status, disability (physical or mental) and/or a medical condition, genetic information, ancestry, veteran status or service in the uniformed services, and any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

records.title: Director, AI Quality, Evaluation & Observability Engineering

postedPay.title: Director, AI Quality, Evaluation & Observability Engineering

records.description:
### **Why Patients Need You**

Pfizer's Commercial organization is putting GenAI and AI agents into work that shapes how medicines reach patients, from content creation and review to field and customer engagement. If we can't show that these systems are accurate, safe and behaving as intended, they don't belong in production. You will build the engineering capability that lets Pfizer prove it, before release and every day after.

### **What You Will Achieve**

You will own the evaluation and observability capability for AI solutions across the Commercial portfolio, and you will be accountable for the Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards: the metrics, thresholds and technical criteria that inform production-readiness and ongoing monitoring decisions. You will build shared tooling, datasets and metrics that let product teams measure quality, safety and performance consistently, catch regressions before release, and detect drift and failures in production. You will set your team's priorities and decide where its engineering capacity goes across the portfolio. Success means teams evaluate through your platform by default, release decisions rest on evidence, and production AI issues are caught by monitoring before users or auditors find them.

### **How You Will Achieve It**

* Build and run a shared evaluation platform for GenAI and agentic solutions. It covers offline test suites, regression testing in CI/CD, LLM-as-judge and rubric-based scoring, and structured human review workflows.
* Set the Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards, including metrics for accuracy, groundedness, hallucination, safety, bias, robustness and task success and the minimum monitoring every production AI solution must have. Calibrate automated scoring against expert human judgment and publish the agreement rates.
* Partner with commercial technology leaders to create and govern golden datasets and test sets with domain experts (e.g., medical, legal and regulatory reviewers), including versioning, data lineage and handling of sensitive data.
* Implement production observability for AI systems, including tracing of prompts, retrievals, tool calls and agent steps, plus monitoring of quality, drift, latency, cost and guardrail activity, with alerting and incident response.
* Evaluate technical and model quality, with business outcomes and value measured separately.
* Set the evaluation thresholds and technical production-readiness criteria that feed release gates run by SDLC Standards & Governance, and give a clear pass, conditional or fail assessment against them, so go-live decisions rely on measured results rather than demos.
* Partner with Responsible AI, Legal, Privacy, Cybersecurity and Compliance to turn policy requirements into measurable tests and auditable evidence, including support for AI-related audits and regulatory inquiries.
* Run adversarial and red-team testing (e.g., prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage) with Cybersecurity, and feed the findings back into evaluation suites.
* Evaluate models and vendors objectively when teams select or upgrade foundation models, AI platforms or third-party AI products in partnership with Strategic Partnerships and contracting, so vendor decisions stay joined up.
* Report quality and reliability trends across the AI portfolio to senior Digital and Commercial leadership.
* Set priorities for the AI quality and observability team and allocate its engineering capacity against portfolio needs, based on risk, release timing and business impact. Make the trade-offs visible and escalate when demand exceeds capacity.
* Lead and develop a team of AI quality and observability engineers that will evolve over time, and coach product and vendor teams, including third-party and offshore partners, to own their evaluations using shared tooling.

### **Decision Rights & Escalation**

* **Decides:** Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards, metrics, thresholds and minimum monitoring requirements; the technical readiness assessment for each release; team priorities and capacity allocation; evaluation tooling and platform design within enterprise architecture standards.
* **Informs:** Release go/no-go decisions made through SDLC stage gates and product ownership; model, platform and vendor selection decisions led with Strategic Partnerships and contracting.
* **Escalates to the Commercial AI Portfolio Lead when:** a team wants to release a solution that does not meet agreed thresholds (risk acceptance); a production issue creates patient-safety, compliance or reputational exposure; demand for evaluation support exceeds team capacity across priority programs; or Responsible AI, Legal or Cybersecurity cannot agree on how a requirement becomes a test.

### **Qualifications**

**Must-Have**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering or a related field.
* 8+ years of experience in software, ML or data engineering, including 3+ years building evaluation, testing or monitoring for ML or GenAI systems in production.
* Hands-on experience designing LLM evaluations, including rubric and LLM-as-judge methods, human evaluation design, and statistically sound comparison of model or prompt versions.
* Experience instrumenting production systems for observability (tracing, metrics, logging, alerting) and running incident response.
* Strong Python skills and experience integrating automated testing into CI/CD pipelines.
* Experience leading engineering teams and influencing product teams across a matrix without direct authority.
* Ability to explain evaluation results and their limits plainly to non-technical leaders.

**Nice-to-Have**

* Master's degree or PhD in a quantitative field.
* Experience with LLM evaluation and observability tooling (e.g., OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, Arize, Weights & Biases, MLflow, Ragas, Promptfoo).
* Experience evaluating RAG systems and multi-step AI agents, including tool use and MCP-based integrations.
* Familiarity with AI risk and regulatory frameworks (e.g., NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001).
* Experience with AI red-teaming or adversarial testing.
* Pharmaceutical or life sciences experience, ideally with Commercial, promotional review, medical or other regulated content.

Candidate demonstrates a breadth of diverse leadership experiences and capabilities including: the ability to influence and collaborate with peers, develop and coach others, oversee and guide the work of other colleagues to achieve meaningful outcomes and create business impact.

**Other Job Details:**

* Last Date to Apply for Job: **December 7, 2026.**
* Ability to travel based on business needs
* This position is hybrid and requires working onsite 2 to 3 days per week

 
The annual base salary for this position ranges from $189,200.00 to $315,400.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 22.5% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States. 
This role is posted in multiple locations. If you are applying for the role in an secondary job posting location where pay transparency regulations apply, your Talent Advisor will share the local pay information with you during the first interview.

Relocation assistance may be available based on business needs and/or eligibility.

**Sunshine Act**

Pfizer reports payments and other transfers of value to health care providers as required by federal and state transparency laws and implementing regulations. These laws and regulations require Pfizer to provide government agencies with information such as a health care provider’s name, address and the type of payments or other value received, generally for public disclosure. Subject to further legal review and statutory or regulatory clarification, which Pfizer intends to pursue, reimbursement of recruiting expenses for licensed physicians may constitute a reportable transfer of value under the federal transparency law commonly known as the Sunshine Act. Therefore, if you are a licensed physician who incurs recruiting expenses as a result of interviewing with Pfizer that we pay or reimburse, your name, address and the amount of payments made currently will be reported to the government. If you have questions regarding this matter, please do not hesitate to contact your Talent Acquisition representative.

**EEO & Employment Eligibility**

Pfizer is committed to equal opportunity in the terms and conditions of employment for all employees and job applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity or gender expression, national origin, disability or veteran status. Pfizer also complies with all applicable national, state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment as well as work authorization and employment eligibility verification requirements of the Immigration and Nationality Act and IRCA. Pfizer is an E-Verify employer. This position requires permanent work authorization in the United States.

Pfizer endeavors to make www.pfizer.com/careers accessible to all users. If you would like to contact us regarding the accessibility of our website or need assistance completing the application process and/or interviewing, please email disabilityrecruitment@pfizer.com. This is to be used solely for accommodation requests with respect to the accessibility of our website, online application process and/or interviewing. Requests for any other reason will not be returned.

To learn more about acceptable and prohibited uses of AI during the recruitment process, please review our candidate AI-use guidelines available on Pfizer Careers.

records.title: Managing Director, Enterprise Quality
records.description:
We are hiring a Managing Director, Enterprise Quality to join our Enterprise Risk Adjustment, Quality & Affordability team at BCBST!

In this role, reporting to the VP of Enterprise Risk Adjustment, Quality and Affordability, you will provide enterprise leadership and strategic direction for Quality ratings, with accountability for establishing and executing the enterprise Quality strategy and driving measurable performance across key programs and outcomes. You will lead and integrate quality efforts across Medicare, Commercial and Medicaid products, including MA Stars, HEDIS, CAHPS/HOS, clinical quality, pharmacy, member experience, provider performance, data and analytics. You’ll establish clear governance and accountability, evaluate performance and the effectiveness of interventions, and partner across the organization to remove barriers, align priorities, and drive sustained improvement in enterprise Quality performance.

To be successful in this role, you’ll bring significant healthcare quality leadership experience and a track record of leading at the enterprise level. You’ll be a strong candidate if you have led complex Quality functions and are comfortable operating in a highly visible leadership role that requires influence across multiple areas of the organization.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Own and direct the enterprise Quality strategy, establishing priorities, objectives, and performance expectations across lines of business and key Quality domains, including Stars, HEDIS, CAHPS/HOS, Appeals, clinical quality, member experience, provider performance, and other priority Quality areas.
* Establish and lead enterprise Quality governance and performance management, ensuring clear accountability among Quality leaders, Measure Champions, and cross-functional stakeholders for achievement of established goals and performance outcomes.
* Monitor enterprise Quality performance and intervention effectiveness, using data and analytics to identify emerging risks, performance gaps, and opportunities; ensure interventions are achieving required results and drive timely corrective action and escalation when performance is off track.
* Lead and integrate Quality efforts across the enterprise, partnering with Clinical Operations, Pharmacy, Provider and Network organizations, Customer Service, Member Experience and Outreach, Risk Adjustment, IT/Data, and other functions to align priorities, resolve cross-functional barriers, and coordinate Quality activities that extend beyond the formal Quality organization.
* Provide strategic oversight for clinical and service quality improvement, regulatory readiness, and accreditation, ensuring Quality programs and practices align with applicable CMS, NCQA, URAC, and other regulatory and accreditation requirements.
* Direct enterprise strategies to improve provider Quality performance, including collaboration on provider engagement, value-based care, performance improvement, incentive programs, and other initiatives designed to improve clinical and Quality outcomes.
* Lead, develop, and align Quality leaders and teams, establishing clear expectations and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement while ensuring the organization has the appropriate expertise, resources, and capabilities to achieve Quality objectives.
* Serve as a leader and advocate for Quality, communicating performance, risks, priorities, and recommendations to executive leadership and other key stakeholders and influencing decisions necessary to advance enterprise Quality outcomes.

**Job Qualifications**

Education

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business administration, public health, health sciences, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience, required. Equivalent experience is defined as four years of professional work experience in a corporate or healthcare environment.

Experience

* 10 years - Experience in healthcare, health insurance, Quality, performance improvement, or a related field required.
* 5 years - Progressive leadership experience, including responsibility for leading leaders and/or complex, cross-functional teams required.
* Significant experience leading healthcare Quality strategy, performance improvement, or Quality management programs required.
* Experience with healthcare Quality measurement and performance programs, including Medicare Advantage, Stars, HEDIS, CAHPS/HOS, or similar programs required.

Skills/Certifications

* Extensive knowledge of healthcare Quality measurement, performance improvement, and industry practices, including Stars, HEDIS, CAHPS/HOS, clinical quality, and provider performance.
* Strong knowledge of applicable healthcare regulatory and accreditation requirements, including CMS, NCQA, and URAC.
* Strong strategic planning, analytical, and performance management skills with the ability to translate complex data and performance trends into actionable strategies.
* Demonstrated ability to establish accountability and drive results across complex, cross-functional environments, including areas outside of direct reporting authority.

**Number of Openings Available**

1

**Worker Type:**

Employee

**Company:**

postedPay.title: Senior Director, Architecture & Quality – Connectivity Firmware

records.description:
**About Marvell**

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.

**Your Team, Your Impact**

Marvell's Connectivity firmware organization delivers firmware for our connectivity and optics product lines. This role owns the full Architecture & Quality function for that portfolio. Architecture and quality operate as one integrated group, a shared resource to every firmware team and not a gate in front of them. 
 
You will set the technical architecture direction for the portfolio and hold the quality bar across it, treating the two as a single end-to-end responsibility. Architecture shapes what can be verified, and quality is how we prove it, from requirements through release and into the field. You will be accountable for how architecture decisions are made, how firmware is verified and released, and how well the firmware, hardware and systems teams work together. You will lead a global team of senior technical leaders and are expected to build depth in a function that is currently concentrated in a few people.

**What You Can Expect**

This is one function, not two. Architecture decisions set what can be tested, and quality findings feed straight back into architecture. You will own the full lifecycle from requirements and design through verification, release and field support.

**Architecture that is built to be verified**

* Product and systems architecture across the Connectivity firmware portfolio: reference architectures, standards, design reviews and technical decision records, each with testability and observability designed in.
* Product hardware interlink: the architectural contract between hardware and firmware, covering requirements, interface definition, bring-up readiness and silicon-to-firmware feedback loops, with validation criteria agreed up front.
* CMIS and optics architecture: firmware architecture for CMIS-based modules and optics products, including spec compliance, feature roadmap and interoperability, tied directly to conformance and interop test plans.
* Architecture governance that scales: lightweight review processes, clear ownership and reusable components, so teams move faster instead of waiting on reviews.

**Quality as an end-to-end discipline**

* Quality strategy that starts at requirements and architecture review, not at test execution: shift-left practices, requirements quality and design-for-test standards owned jointly with the architects.
* Software Quality Assurance (SQA) strategy and execution: test strategy, automation, regression coverage, release qualification and defect trends.
* Release readiness and quality gates for all firmware releases, with clear exit criteria and a straight, data-backed go/no-go recommendation.
* Quality metrics and reporting to Engineering leadership, Product Management and customer-facing teams.

**Closing the loop**

* Customer-escape and defect analysis that traces root causes back to architecture, interfaces and process, and turns the learning into updated patterns, standards and test coverage.
* A single set of metrics and quality signals shared across architecture, interlink, optics and SQA, so design risk and test findings are managed in one view.

**Organization**

* Lead and develop a global organization (30+).
* Grow and retain senior technical talent, and manage the pipeline, hiring, succession and career paths for architects and quality engineers.
* Build a collaborative partnership with Firmware, Hardware, Systems, Product and Program Management, and with the Optics and telemetry teams.
* Own the function's budget, headcount plan, requisitions and tooling or lab investments.

**Your Team**

You will lead a small team of senior leaders and architects who together cover the function end to end, with architecture and quality responsibilities intentionally overlapping:

* Software quality assurance and release qualification.
* Hardware and firmware interlink.
* Optics and module architecture.
* Product and systems architecture.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Set a multi-year architecture and quality roadmap aligned with product and customer priorities, and drive it across engineering teams that do not report to you.
* Make and communicate hard trade-offs between schedule, scope and quality, and own the release recommendation.
* Raise the architecture bar: consistent patterns, reuse across product lines, and early detection of design risk before it becomes schedule risk.
* Shift quality left: embed test, automation and requirements quality earlier in the lifecycle, and invest in CI/CD, simulation, emulation and lab infrastructure.
* Represent Architecture & Quality in executive reviews and in technical engagements with key customers and standards bodies.
* Keep the function independent and credible: escalate quality risks directly and transparently, including when the news is unwelcome.
* Build the next layer of leadership so the function does not depend on any one person, and set clear delegation across the architecture and SQA leads.
* Manage a distributed team across time zones with clear rituals, ownership and handoffs.

**What We're Looking For**

* BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related field.
* 15+ years in embedded firmware or systems software for semiconductor, networking or optical products, including 8+ years leading managers or senior technical leaders.
* Track record owning both architecture and quality outcomes for shipping firmware products at scale.
* Deep working knowledge of firmware architecture for connectivity or optics products, with direct experience in HW/FW co-design and silicon bring-up.
* Hands-on experience with test strategy and automation, release qualification and quality metrics for complex, customer-deployed products.
* Experience leading globally distributed teams across multiple sites and cultures, including offshore QA/SQA organizations.
* Proven executive communication: able to present risk, trade-offs and recommendations to VP-level and customer audiences.

**Preferred Experience**

* Experience with CMIS and optical module firmware (for example 400G/800G and coherent or pluggable optics), and related industry standards and interoperability programs.
* Familiarity with Ethernet PHY, retimer, DSP or SerDes firmware, and with security features such as MACsec.
* Experience with secure firmware update, recovery and lifecycle practices.
* Background building or transforming an SQA organization, including automation and CI/CD maturity.
* Experience in a matrixed, platform-style organization where architecture is a shared service.

**Expected Base Pay Range (USD)**

218,850 - 327,800, $ per annum

The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.

This role is eligible to participate in Marvell's bonus and equity plans, including a new hire equity grant and annual equity refreshers, ensuring you are rewarded for your contributions and remain invested in the company's long-term success.

**Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements**

Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. Our offerings are built around four key pillars: financial well-being, family support, mental and physical health, and recognition. Highlights include an employee stock purchase plan with a 2-year look back, family support programs to help balance work and home life, robust mental health resources to prioritize emotional well-being, and a recognition and service awards to celebrate contributions and milestones. We look forward to sharing more with you during the interview process.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

Any applicant who requires a reasonable accommodation during the selection process should contact Marvell HR Helpdesk at TAOps@marvell.com.

**Interview Integrity**

To support fair and authentic hiring practices, candidates are not permitted to use AI tools (such as transcription apps, real-time answer generators like ChatGPT or Copilot, or automated note-taking bots) during interviews.

These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. Use of AI tools without prior instruction from the interviewer will result in disqualification from the hiring process.

**This position may require access to technology and/or software subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). As such, applicants must be eligible to access export-controlled information as defined under applicable law. Marvell may be required to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce and/or the U.S. Department of State. Except for U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), all applicants may be subject to an export license review process prior to employment.**
