records.title: Director, Quality Systems & Digital Quality
records.description:
Cambridge, MA

Development – Quality Assurance /

Full-Time /

Hybrid

 

*Scholar Rock is delivering muscle-targeted breakthroughs to transform the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and other rare neuromuscular diseases where muscle atrophy remains a critical unmet need.*

*As a global leader in myostatin biology, a field focused on proteins that regulate muscle mass, the biopharmaceutical company is named for the visual resemblance of a scholar rock to protein structures. Our commitment to unlock fundamentally different treatment approaches is powered by broad application of a proprietary platform, which has developed novel monoclonal antibodies to modulate protein growth factors with extraordinary selectivity. Scholar Rock works every day to create new possibilities for patients through its highly innovative anti-myostatin program, including opportunities in additional rare neuromuscular diseases. Learn more about our neuromuscular franchise at* ***ScholarRock.com*** *and follow @ScholarRock on X and on LinkedIn.*

 

**Summary of Position:**

Scholar Rock is seeking an experienced, hands-on Director, Quality Systems & Digital Quality. Reporting to the Sr Director, Global Quality Systems & Compliance, this leader is an integral part of Scholar Rock’s Quality Management System (QMS) and the GxP computerized systems and data that support it, across our commercial and early-phase pipeline. Because Scholar Rock outsources all GMP manufacturing, testing, and distribution to qualified contract organizations, this role will build and sustain a lean, risk-based, phase-appropriate QMS that meets US (FDA), EU (EMA/EU GMP), and Japan (MHLW/PMDA) requirements, ensuring that Scholar Rock’s own systems are inspection-ready and that the GxP data generated on our behalf by contract partners is reliable, complete, and traceable.

### **Position Responsibilities**

***Quality Management System***

* Partner with Quality process owners to ensure GxP digital systems effectively support QMS processes, enabling efficient, compliant, and scalable operations aligned with Scholar Rock’s evolving business needs.
* Track a focused set of key QMS performance indicators and present them in periodic quality management reviews.

 

***Digital Systems & Computer Software Assurance***

* Provide Quality oversight of Scholar Rock’s GxP computerized systems (largely cloud/SaaS, e.g., eQMS, document and training management, ERP and other GxP-relevant platforms), ensuring compliance with 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11, and Japan’s ER/ES guideline.
* Lead and execute GxP system enhancements and continuous improvement initiatives, partnering with business process owners to define requirements, evaluate solutions, manage implementation, and ensure effective adoption of new functionality.
* Establish and apply a risk-based computerized system validation and assurance approach consistent with applicable GxP regulatory requirements, leveraging GAMP 5 principles, relevant FDA guidance, and vendor documentation to ensure appropriate assurance while minimizing redundant testing.
* Oversee the GxP computerized system lifecycle, including risk-based validation and assurance, change control, periodic reviews, access management, audit trail controls, data retention, and system retirement. Ensure appropriate validation deliverables, testing, and documented evidence are established and maintained throughout the system lifecycle.
* Partner with IT and business owners on system selection, implementation, upgrades, and vendor releases so that new digital capabilities are adopted with right-sized assurance.
* Support qualification of computerized system suppliers (e.g., SaaS, software, and IT service providers), including risk-based vendor assessments and audits, and the Part 11/Annex 11 and data integrity provisions of their quality agreements; qualification of GMP manufacturing and testing suppliers remains with other Quality functions.
* Monitor evolving expectations, including the revision of EU GMP Annex 11 and emerging guidance on AI in GxP settings, and advise on practical, compliant adoption of digital and AI-enabled tools.
* Support the implementation of AI-enabled tools in GxP processes (e.g., document drafting and review, deviation and complaint trending, AI features within eQMS and other platforms), defining risk-based assurance, human oversight, and data integrity controls proportionate to each tool’s intended use and impact on product quality and patient safety.
* Partner with IT, Legal, and business owners to establish lightweight governance for AI use in GxP activities, including an inventory of AI applications, acceptable-use expectations, training, and ongoing performance monitoring.
* Lead the development and execution of a risk-based digital Quality roadmap, prioritizing system enhancements and improvements based on business needs, compliance requirements, and operational efficiencies.
* Partner with Quality process owners and cross-functional stakeholders to identify improvement opportunities, translate business needs into functional requirements, and implement scalable digital solutions.
* Drive the end-to-end implementation of GxP system enhancements, including requirements definition, risk assessments, configuration, testing, validation documentation, deployment, and post-implementation support.
* Establish efficient processes for managing system changes, including vendor releases, impact assessments, regression testing, and maintaining systems in a validated state.
* Provide hands-on leadership and technical guidance for Veeva eQMS, eDMS, and other GxP platforms, ensuring effective system functionality, integration, and continuous improvement.
* Establish clear system ownership, governance, and accountability across Quality, IT, and business functions, including responsibilities for system administration, validation, user access, and ongoing lifecycle management.
* Support regulatory inspections and audits involving computerized systems, electronic records, electronic signatures, and data integrity, including preparation of supporting documentation and remediation of identified gaps.
* Drive effective adoption of new digital capabilities through stakeholder engagement, training, change management, and ongoing evaluation of system effectiveness.
* Establish and maintain effective governance for GxP system enhancements and vendor releases, including change prioritization, impact assessments, testing strategies, implementation planning, and post-deployment monitoring.

 

***Data Integrity & Data Governance***

* Lead the development and ongoing governance of Scholar Rock’s GxP data integrity program, establishing risk-based expectations, controls, and oversight mechanisms in partnership with business process owners and applicable Quality functions.
* Define a lightweight data governance model with clear data ownership and stewardship for GxP data across Quality, Regulatory, Technical Operations, and Clinical.
* Extend data integrity oversight to contract organizations through quality agreement requirements, data integrity–focused audit criteria, and review of partner-generated data (e.g., batch records, CoAs, stability, deviations).
* Establish governance and controls for GxP-relevant master data, partnering with designated data owners to ensure data accuracy, consistency, integrity, and appropriate alignment across internal systems, contract partners, and regulatory information.
* Lead data integrity risk assessments and drive timely, proportionate remediation of gaps.

 

***Inspection Readiness & Regulatory Support***

* Lead inspection readiness for the QMS, computerized systems, and data integrity controls, and support health authority inspections of Scholar Rock and its contract partners.
* Contribute to regulatory submissions and responses, such as annual reports, IND/CTA updates, and marketing applications in the US, EU, and Japan.
* Maintain awareness of regulatory changes in the US, EU, and Japan and translate them into practical, minimal-necessary updates to the QMS.

 

***Leadership & Partnership***

* Act as the subject matter expert and coach for colleagues across Quality and partner functions on QMS, computerized system, and data integrity topics.
* Collaborate with the Head of Global Quality and Quality leadership, IT, Regulatory, Technical Operations, and Clinical to align quality systems with corporate goals and regulatory obligations.
* Champion a culture of quality, accountability, and data integrity, and serve as a change agent for simplification and digitization of the QMS.

### **Candidate Requirements**

* BS/MS degree in a scientific, engineering, or information systems discipline.
* 12+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical/biotech industry, with 5+ years leading Quality systems, computerized system compliance, or related programs; biologics experience preferred.
* Deep understanding of GxP and Quality System requirements (US, EU, and Japan) for biologics development and commercial products, including ICH Q9(R1) and Q10.
* Demonstrated expertise in 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11, risk-based CSA/GAMP 5, and global data integrity expectations, including qualification of computerized system and SaaS suppliers.
* Familiarity with AI/ML-enabled tools in regulated environments and with emerging health authority expectations for AI use in GxP activities.
* Experience in a virtual or outsourced model, including oversight of quality systems and data integrity at CDMOs and contract testing laboratories.
* Experience leading or supporting regulatory inspections and interfacing with global health authorities.
* Proven ability to design lean, simple processes and to make pragmatic, risk-based decisions on what is required versus nice to have.
* Highly proactive, decisive, and capable of independently managing key initiatives as a hands-on individual contributor.
* Collaborative leader who builds quality culture and capability across teams through influence, coaching, and knowledge sharing.
* Excellent communication skills and ability to influence across functions and with external partners.

$200,000 - $260,000 a year

records.title: Director, Quality Assurance Operations
records.description:
**Director, Quality Assurance Operations**

At Vericel Corporation, we are pioneers in advanced cell therapies for sports medicine and severe burn care, transforming patient lives through cutting-edge regenerative medicine. Our commitment to innovation, patient-centered focus, and scientific excellence drives us to develop groundbreaking treatments including MACI (knee cartilage repair), Epicel and Nexobrid (burn care).

**Position Summary**

The Director of Quality Operations is responsible for the strategic leadership and performance of Quality Assurance Operations, Document Control, and Supplier Quality Management. This role provides oversight of product disposition and release, labeling and documentation controls, deviations, CAPAs, product complaints, supplier quality management, tech transfer activities, controlled documentation, and internal audits. The Director translates business objectives and quality risks into operational strategies, resource plans, and measurable outcomes. This position develops organizational capability through effective leadership, succession planning, and talent development while driving cross-functional collaboration and continuous improvement. The Director exercises independent, risk-based decision-making within delegated authority to ensure compliance, operational excellence, and sustained product quality.

**Schedule:** This position is onsite Monday through Friday at our Burlington office, with one day per week at our Cambridge office.

**Essential Functions:**

**Quality Operations and Department Management**

* Provide strategic oversight and accountability for product disposition and release, deviations, CAPAs, complaints, supplier quality management, documentation controls, labeling review, and internal audit programs and tech transfer activities; ensure activities are executed in compliance with regulatory requirements and business objectives.
* Establish department strategy and annual operating plans aligned with organizational priorities, quality objectives, and risk management principles; determine resource, staffing, and budget requirements to support business growth and compliance commitments.
* Serve as the Quality Operations representative in cross-functional governance, planning, and decision-making forums involving Manufacturing, Regulatory Affairs, Technical Operations, Product Development, and Project Management.
* Make and oversee complex quality decisions within delegated authority using scientific rationale, regulatory requirements, and risk-based assessments; escalate significant compliance or product quality risks with recommended mitigation strategies.
* Develop, implement, and maintain departmental policies, procedures, standards, and governance processes to ensure consistent and effective execution across all areas of responsibility.
* Ensure continuous inspection readiness; lead departmental support for regulatory inspections, customer audits, and internal audits, and ensure timely completion of all commitments and corrective actions.

**Continuous Improvement and Quality Metrics**

* Lead a portfolio of strategic, cross-functional quality improvement initiatives designed to enhance compliance, strengthen quality systems, improve operational efficiency, reduce deviation recurrence, and increase right-first-time performance.
* Establish measurable objectives, success criteria, timelines, and effectiveness metrics for improvement initiatives; monitor progress and ensure sustainable implementation of results.
* Analyze performance trends, quality metrics, audit findings, and CAPA effectiveness data to identify systemic risks, prioritize resources, and drive data-informed decision making.
* Partner with Quality leadership to establish performance indicators and business reviews that ensure accountability and continuous improvement.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Staff Management and Leadership Development**

* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Quality Operations organization through effective organizational design, workforce planning, talent acquisition, and succession planning.
* Develop leadership capability through coaching, mentoring, performance feedback, and individualized development plans; cultivate future leaders and ensure organizational readiness for key roles.
* Delegate authority and accountability appropriately while maintaining oversight of critical quality and business outcomes.
* Foster a culture of engagement, collaboration, continuous learning, and accountability that supports both employee growth and organizational objectives.
* Provide ongoing coaching and performance management, including recognition, corrective action, and career development guidance as appropriate.

**Performance Management and Accountability**

* Establish and communicate clear goals, priorities, performance expectations, and timelines; hold leaders and employees accountable for achieving results in accordance with company values and quality standards.
* Maintain effective communication through regular leadership meetings, team meetings, one-on-one discussions, and skip-level engagements.
* Address performance concerns promptly through documented coaching, performance improvement planning, and follow-up actions to ensure sustained improvement and accountability.
* Promote transparency, collaboration, and decision-making discipline across the department to support operational effectiveness and employee engagement.

**Qualifications, Education, & Experience:**

**Basic Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree with a minimum of 14 years of experience in a biotech or pharmaceutical regulated industry (minimum of 10 years in Quality/8 years directly related to management of personnel). Prior leadership experience required.
* Master’s degree with a minimum of 12 years of experience in the life sciences regulated industry (minimum of 10 years in Quality/8 years directly related to management of quality personnel). Prior leadership experience required.
* Strong working knowledge of ICH, FDA, ISO, and cGMP regulations.
* Excellent technical writing and presentation skills.
* Strong leadership and personnel development experience
* Excellent communication skills at organization, team, and individual levels.
* Demonstrated experience leading Quality Operations functions within a regulated GMP environment.
* Proven ability to lead regulatory inspections and manage interactions with FDA and other regulatory authorities.
* Experience developing and leading managers and building succession pipelines within a Quality organization.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Medical device, biotechnology, cell and gene therapy, or combination product experience strongly preferred.
* Proficient in Auditing, both internal and vendor.
* Prior International experience.

**Working Conditions & Physical Demands:**

* Ability to lift up to 30 lbs.
* Ability to travel if required.
* Must be able to support holiday coverage.
* Must be able to gown into the CNC areas when required

**Why Vericel?**

* **Mission-Driven Work:** Help bring potentially life-enhancing cell therapies to patients with serious medical conditions.
* **Innovative Products:** Work with a first-in-class therapy backed by clinical success and provider trust.
* **Career Growth:** Be a part of a growing organization with opportunities to expand your impact.
* **Collaborative Culture:** Join a supportive, cross-functional team that values passion, integrity, and excellence.

The salary range Vericel reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for this position at the time of this posting is $206,000 - $225,000 annually.

The actual salary offered will be determined based on factors such as the candidate’s qualifications, experience, and skills. Bonus, incentive pay, equity and benefits may be provided in addition to the base compensation listed above.

In accordance with Massachusetts law, Vericel provides the pay range that it reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for a particular and specific employment position at the time of posting or offer. This range is subject to change based on business needs, market conditions, and individual qualifications. Employees and applicants may request the pay range for their position or for a position to which they are applying. Retaliation for making such a request is strictly prohibited.

**EEO Statement**

*All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to their race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, or protected veteran status and will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability. Vericel Corporation is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer.*

*Vericel Corporation is VEVRAA federal contractor and desires priority referrals of protected veterans for job openings at all locations within the state.*

records.description:
Division Department: Therapeutics | Quality

Position Title: Director of Quality (Head of Quality)

Reports To: Corporate Head of Quality (proposed; final reporting structure to be confirmed)

Salary - $225-250,000 based on experience

**PharmaLogic is expanding our therapeutics business line. Our therapeutics business, Agilera, is the** **world’s only cGMP-compliant CDMO currently manufacturing and distributing commercial radiopharmaceutical therapeutics across more than 30 countries. In this role,** **you will have the opportunity to work as part of a unique environment that is involved in the entire value chain, from the preclinical phase to the commercial production and distribution of radiopharmaceuticals.**

**Role Summary:**

The Director of Quality serves as the Head of Quality for PharmaLogic’s newly acquired therapeutics business, leading the quality organization and establishing the systems, capabilities, and culture needed for reliable GMP manufacturing. This leader is accountable for the pharmaceutical quality system and Quality oversight of sterile therapeutic drug manufacturing, testing, and release under applicable 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211 requirements. As a member of the site leadership team, the Director partners with Operations, Technical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, and corporate Quality to support clinical supply, technology transfer, commercialization, and growth. The role requires independent judgment, visible leadership on the manufacturing floor, and the ability to translate quality requirements into practical execution while protecting patient safety and product quality.

**Job Responsibilities and Duties:**

**Quality Leadership and Governance**

Lead the Quality function, including Quality Assurance and oversight of Quality Control and microbiology activities within the assigned organizational scope. Set strategy, staffing, budgets, objectives, and development plans; build a capable team with clear accountability.

Maintain the Quality unit’s independent authority to approve or reject materials and drug products, including outsourced products; approve quality-impacting procedures and specifications; and ensure documented responsibilities and appropriate escalation to corporate Quality and executive leadership.

Own batch disposition through authorized Quality personnel. Ensure production and laboratory records, deviations, and required test results receive appropriate review before release. Place materials or product on hold and stop affected operations when quality or compliance concerns warrant.

**Quality Systems and Sterile Manufacturing**

Establish and continuously improve systems for deviations, investigations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, document control, training, complaints, product quality reviews, and quality risk management. Require scientifically sound root-cause analysis and verification of CAPA effectiveness.

Provide Quality oversight of aseptic processing and contamination control, including cleanrooms, environmental and personnel monitoring, gowning qualification, aseptic process simulations, sterilization, disinfection, and container closure integrity, as applicable.

Oversee laboratory controls, specifications, analytical method validation and transfer, stability programs, and investigations of out-of-specification and out-of-trend results. Ensure complete, accurate, traceable data and effective controls for electronic records and computerized systems.

Approve qualification and validation strategies, protocols, and reports for facilities, utilities, equipment, manufacturing processes, cleaning, and computerized systems. Ensure a documented lifecycle approach and continued process verification.

**Manufacturing Readiness and External Partners**

Lead Quality readiness for new products, technology transfers, process scale-up, and commercial launches. Establish clear acceptance criteria and readiness decisions with Development, Manufacturing, Engineering, and Regulatory Affairs.

Serve as the primary site Quality representative for FDA inspections and customer audits. Lead inspection preparation, responses, and commitments; maintain sustained readiness and timely, effective remediation.

Manage supplier qualification, contract laboratory and manufacturer oversight, audits, and quality agreements. Define responsibilities with CDMO customers and ensure outsourced activities meet agreed quality requirements.

**Acquisition Integration and Regulatory Partnership**

Lead the acquisition Quality integration plan: assess inherited systems and commitments, prioritize gaps by risk, align governance and procedures with corporate standards, and manage changes without disrupting compliant product supply.

Partner with Regulatory Affairs on manufacturing and quality content for filings, change assessments, and regulatory commitments. Lead quality defect assessments and support recalls, field actions, and required notifications with designated functions.

For radiopharmaceutical therapeutics, oversee appropriate controls for isotope and precursor quality, radiochemical testing, time-sensitive manufacturing and disposition, and stability. Partner with Radiation Safety and EHS on safe, compliant execution.

**Quality Performance and Continuous Improvement**

Present quality performance and material risks to site and corporate leadership. Use management reviews and meaningful metrics to improve investigation quality, CAPA effectiveness, release reliability, training, and inspection readiness.

**Job Requirements, Skills and Education:**

**Required Qualifications**

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, microbiology, pharmacy, engineering, or a related scientific discipline.

Typically, 10 or more years of progressive pharmaceutical Quality experience, including at least 5 years leading teams or major Quality programs in a GMP manufacturing environment.

Demonstrated Quality leadership in sterile injectable manufacturing, with substantial knowledge of aseptic processing, contamination control, laboratory controls, validation, and data integrity.

**Strong working knowledge of 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211, applicable electronic records requirements, and relevant FDA guidance and ICH quality principles.**

Experience leading regulatory inspections, complex investigations, remediation, and batch disposition, with sound scientific judgment and the ability to defend quality decisions.

Experience supporting technology transfer, clinical or commercial manufacturing, and cross-functional delivery of significant quality or operational improvements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

Experience with therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals or radioligand therapies; CDMO operations and pharmaceutical customer partnerships; and commercial launch or preapproval inspection readiness.

Experience integrating an acquisition, building or transforming a quality organization, and implementing electronic quality management systems. Advanced scientific degree or relevant professional certification.

**Leadership and Working Expectations**

A visible, hands-on leader who develops people, communicates clearly, and holds teams accountable. Able to challenge decisions constructively, escalate risks promptly, and make timely decisions under pressure. Regular onsite presence in manufacturing and laboratory areas, compliance with required gowning and safety practices, and availability for critical quality events are expected. Travel requirements will be defined for the role. Essential functions may be performed with reasonable accommodation.

Come join our winning team and begin a fulfilling career with us by applying today. 
 
PharmaLogic is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status, or any other protected class.

**Benefits Include:**

401(k) retirement benefit program

Medical

Dental care

Disability insurance

Employee assistance program

Life insurance

On-site parking

Paid time off

Vision care

**Job Description :**

**Your Job:**

 

The Director of Quality is responsible for the overall operations of quality management throughout the Medical Center. Ensures that the hospital's policies and practices as related to patient care are within appropriate guidelines as designated by all State and Federal agencies as well as certifying agencies. Facilitates the hospital's JCAHO compliance and survey readiness. Acts as a resource to members of the management team in reference to legal guidelines for Patient Care Services.

 
 

**Your Job Requirements:**

 

* Bachelor's degree in health profession required; Master's or equivalent experience preferred

* Certification as a case manager and/or CPHQ (Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality) preferred

* Three to five years experience related to areas of risk, case management, and/or process improvement with a minimum of two years in management

* Extensive knowledge of State, Federal and regulatory guidelines/standards as they relate to the patient care services and medical staff services

 
 

**Your Job Responsibilities:**

 

* Responsible for the overall strategic planning and implementation of a comprehensive quality management program including the education and compliance component.

* Serves as a resource to the Board of Directors, Administration, managers, medical STAFF employees related to quality issues.

* Serves as the liaison for the Texas Department of Health (TDH) related to quality issues that may arise.

* Oversees State, Federal and accrediting compliance. Serves as a resource for national trends, regulatory updates, survey/site visit readiness related to compliance.

* Incorporates the customer satisfaction surveys and data from the Guest Relation Representative to establish trends to be utilized for action plan development.

* Collaborates with the manger/directors to improve customer satisfaction.

* Responsible for the resource management program including utilization review and case management.

records.description:
Overview:

**Hospital Name: Ohiohealth Rehabilitation Hospital** 
**Joint venture/Partnership/Affiliation with Select Medical** 
**Position:** **Director of Quality Management** 
**Location: Dublin, OH**

* Bonus incentives
* Extensive onboarding and training program
* Customizable health insurance packages

**Who We Are**

Our inpatient rehabilitation hospital is committed to providing exceptional and compassionate care to best address the medical, physical, emotional, and vocational challenges for individuals with brain injuries, spinal cord injuries, neurological disorders, orthopedic issues, amputation, and multiple traumas

Responsibilities:

Coordinates the Medical Quality Management and Performance Improvement activities to measurably enhance the quality, process and cost effectiveness of patient and customer services rendered. Coordinates the Performance Improvement and Patient Safety programs in accordance with the guidelines and regulatory requirements of Federal and State regulations on a hospital-wide basis. Oversees operations of the Infection Control and Employee Health Programs. Develops and Reviews policies and procedures to ensure compliance with all regulatory and accrediting standards. Collects data to monitor compliance and/or trends.

 

* Institutes and monitors the Hospital’s CQI Processes, utilizing data analysis measuring tools. Oversight/coordination of operations of the Infection Control & Employee Health Program based upon hospital size and configuration.
* Assists with the design and compliance of quality processes/activities in the areas of clinical/medical staff PI for all applicable clinical/medical TJC /CARF/DOH standards. Assists with all assigned activities to assure that the hospital maintains accreditation, certification and licensure. Assumes leadership with the Joint Commission and DOH as well as other regulatory agencies with regard to CQI activities.
* Serves as a resource for all departments within the facility to provide guidance on designing, implementing, analyzing and reporting on Quality Improvement.
* Assists clinical areas in developing criteria, monitoring and reporting mechanisms and action documentation related to the hospital’s CQI program.
* Performs basic chart review activities with appropriate staff for outcome utilization, infection control and medical CQI indicators. Analyzes results of chart review activities with appropriate staff and confers with department staff on any case requiring special attention.
* Prepares analysis of significant PI findings pertaining to adverse drug reactions, drug usage evaluation, medical management of acute transfers and other CQI indicators.

Qualifications:

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Registered Nurse with valid state license. Legacy employees may exist with other clinical licensure.
* Requires experience in at least one of the core areas of responsibility: Quality, Survey Readiness, Risk Management, Infection Control, Employee Health and Education
* Demonstrates familiarity with accrediting standards, including TJC and CARF preferred.

**Preferred Experience**

* Previous experience in Quality Improvement, with Statistical Process Control experience and computer skills preferred.
* Demonstrates familiarity with accrediting standards, including JCAHO and CARF preferred.
* Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ) preferred

Additional Data:

* Start Strong: Extensive and thorough orientation program to ensure a smooth transition into our setting
* Recharge & Refresh: Generous PTO and Paid Sick Time for full-time team members to maintain a healthy work-life balance
* Your Health Matters: Comprehensive medical/RX, health, vision, employee assistance program (EAP) and dental plan offerings for full-time team members
* Invest in Your Future: Company-matching 401(k) retirement plan, as well as life and disability protection for full-time team members
* Your Impact Matters: Join a team of over 44,000 committed to providing exceptional patient care

*Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disabled/Veterans*

records.title: Director, Central Quality Audit, Pharmacovigilance
records.description:
**Job Description Summary**
===========================

Managing, ensuring and improving capabilities to comply with external standards and regulations. Interprets internal and external business challenges and recommends best practices to improve products, processes or services. Stays informed of industry trends that may influence work. 
 
GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

**Job Description**
===================

**Roles and Responsibilities**

* Own the Pharmacovigilance (PV) Audit Program: Develop, implement, and maintain the global PV audit strategy, ensuring alignment with regulatory expectations (e.g., EMA, FDA, MHRA, PMDA) and industry best practices.
* Manage Audit Operations: Oversee scheduling, planning, execution, reporting, and follow-up for PV audits, including internal audits and audits of service providers and affiliates. Fully participate in the audit program; actively owning and executing PV audits.
* Risk Identification and Communication: Identify high-risk compliance issues, escalate findings, and provide actionable recommendations to senior leadership.
* Regulatory Inspection Support: Prepare for and support PV-related health authority inspections, including back-room management and post-inspection follow-up.
* Metrics and Reporting: Define and track PV audit KPIs, ensuring visibility of compliance risks and trends to leadership.
* System Ownership: Manage audit-related modules within the electronic Quality Management System (eQMS), including support of configuration, UAT, and documentation.
* Team Leadership: Lead and develop a team of 3–5 auditors, providing coaching, mentorship, and performance management.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with PV Operations, Quality, and Regulatory teams to ensure audit outcomes drive continuous improvement.
* Strategic Influence: Contribute to policy development and influence PV compliance strategy across the organization.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum 5 years of people leadership experience, including team development and performance management.
* Qualified Lead Auditor with active certification.
* Master’s degree and 5+ years in pharmacovigilance or pharmaceutical industry; or Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years relevant experience.
* Minimum of 5 years’ experience driving Global programs to resolve quality compliance issues (directly).
* Experience with Pharmaceutical QMS requirements and regulatory requirements including but not limited to cGMP, GDP, GPvP, GCP and GLP.

**Desired Characteristics**

* Experience with Medical Device QMS requirements and regulatory requirements including but not limited to FDA CFR 21 820 and ISO 13485.
* Prior Veeva and TrackWise Digital experience a plus.
* Prior health authority experience a plus.
* IRCA, ASQ (CQE, CQA, etc.) and/or Lean Certification a plus (green belt, black belt).
* Extensive experience in the Medica Device and Pharmaceutical industry.
* Understanding of product quality improvement using tools such as Six Sigma, DFR.
* Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems.
* Exceptional conflict-resolution skills.
* Ability to interface with top organizational leadership and internal and external customers, responding in a professional manner.
* Demonstrated ability to lead programs / projects. Ability to prioritize and drive multiple programs.
* Ability to energize others by building a connection with the team through personal involvement and trust, providing feedback and coaching to develop others, and accountability of actions.
* Strong oral and written communication skills in English.
* Integrity: Accepting and adhering to high ethical, moral, and personal values in decisions, communications, actions, and when dealing with others.
* Ability to travel globally up to 15%.

We expect all employees to live and breathe our behaviors: to act with humility and build trust; lead with transparency; deliver with focus, and drive ownership –always with unyielding integrity.

Our total rewards are designed to unlock your ambition by giving you the boost and flexibility you need to turn your ideas into world-changing realities. Our salary and benefits are everything you’d expect from an organization with global strength and scale, and you’ll be surrounded by career opportunities in a culture that fosters care, collaboration and support.

We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job opening. For U.S. based positions only, the pay range for this position is $142,400.00-$213,600.00 Annual. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the pay range and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. The specific compensation offered to a candidate may be influenced by a variety of factors including skills, qualifications, experience and location. In addition, this position may also be eligible to earn performance based incentive compensation, which may include cash bonus(es) and/or long term incentives (LTI). GE HealthCare offers a competitive benefits package, including not but limited to medical, dental, vision, paid time off, a 401(k) plan with employee and company contribution opportunities, life, disability, and accident insurance, and tuition reimbursement.

**Additional Information**
==========================

GE HealthCare offers a great work environment, professional development, challenging careers, and competitive compensation. GE HealthCare is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

GE HealthCare will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States for this opening. Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen (as applicable).

While GE HealthCare does not currently require U.S. employees to be vaccinated against COVID-19, some GE HealthCare customers have vaccination mandates that may apply to certain GE HealthCare employees.

**Relocation Assistance Provided:** No

Application Deadline: December 21, 2026

records.title: Director of Quality
records.description:
**SUMMARY**

Leads enterprise clinical quality, patient safety, regulatory compliance, and performance improvement initiatives to improve outcomes, drive operational excellence, and support strategic growth. Partners with clinical and operational leaders to establish quality standards, oversee governance and accreditation activities, implement data-driven improvement strategies, and advance innovative quality solutions that enhance organizational and client success.

**GENERAL HOURS OF WORK:** Monday through Friday (with occasional night and weekend involvement)

 

**REPORTS TO:** Chief Operating Officer

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

*Clinical Quality Leadership*

* Leads accreditation readiness, regulatory compliance, quality reporting, and corrective action planning activities.
* Leads the development and execution of enterprise-wide clinical quality, patient safety, and performance improvement strategies.
* Partners with physician and operational leaders to establish quality goals, drive accountability, and improve clinical outcomes.
* Coordinates and oversees quality improvement initiatives across all clinical programs and service lines.
* Monitors, analyzes, and reports quality performance metrics, benchmarks, and outcome trends to identify improvement opportunities.
* Maintains quality policies, procedures, governance structures, and documentation standards.
* Supports clinical governance, risk management, peer review, and professional practice evaluation processes.
* Facilitates physician quality committees and multidisciplinary improvement teams.
* Promotes a culture of continuous improvement, evidence-based practice, and provider accountability for quality outcomes.

*Performance Improvement & Operational Excellence*

* Identifies workflow variation, standardization opportunities, and best practices to improve outcomes and operational performance.
* Implements and sustains process improvement efforts that reduce variation, improve reliability, and enhance patient experience.
* Partners with operational leaders to improve patient experience, clinical performance, and organizational effectiveness.

*Strategic Quality Engagement*

* Develops and executes Avel's enterprise quality and clinical transformation strategy.
* Designs and operationalizes scalable quality improvement services, frameworks, and methodologies for customers.
* Establishes quality and outcomes measurement as key components of Avel's value proposition and market differentiation.
* Serves as a trusted advisor to clients on quality strategy, patient safety, outcome improvement, and regulatory excellence.
* Identifies emerging healthcare quality trends and incorporate best practices and innovation into Avel solutions.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university in Health Care field required.

* Master's degree in healthcare or business administration preferred
* 10+ years of experience in medical staff office functions, quality, compliance, risk management and performance improvement required.

**ABOUT AVEL eCARE**

Avel eCare is a nationally recognized leader in virtual health, operating one of the most extensive virtual healthcare networks in the world. Based in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, Avel partners with more than 650 health systems, rural hospitals, clinics, and facilities to deliver innovative telehealth solutions. Our services span Behavioral Health, Critical Care, Emergency, Hospitalist, Pharmacy, Specialty Clinic, Senior Care, and School Health — impacting nearly two million patients annually.

For three decades, Avel has been at the forefront of healthcare innovation, developing telehealth solutions that reduce costs, save time, and remove barriers to quality care. Join our mission-driven team and help reshape the future of healthcare.

**MISSION**

"We transform access to high-quality healthcare for people and communities through integrated virtual solutions."

**VISION**

"Setting the standard for healthcare delivery by creating the nation’s most trusted Virtual Health System, through innovation and partnership."

records.title: Director, Quality
records.description:
At Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense Company (EBAD), we believe that our strengths are built on our most important resource - our people. Join EBAD and you'll be a part of a team who creates cutting edge technology that will blast us into the future. No other company can match the innovative energetic solutions that we provide. At EBAD you will actively contribute to successful missions putting men, women and satellites into space, and protecting our armed service men and women around the world. If this is the culture and work environment you are seeking, then EBAD is the place for you!

**Job Description**

**Location:** Simsbury, CT

**Reports to:** VP of Operations

**Industry:** Aerospace & Defense

**Experience Level:** Director (15+ years)

**Shape the Future. Deliver Excellence. Achieve Zero Failure.**

At **Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense (EBAD),** we’ve been innovating for nearly **200 years,** delivering mission-critical technologies that protect lives and advance exploration. As we prepare to double in size over the next 3–5 years, we’re investing in our people and culture to support this transformation.

We’re seeking a dynamic **Director of Quality** to lead a complex, multi-site quality organization and drive performance at scale. Based at our headquarters in Simsbury, Connecticut, this role is critical to ensure the highest levels of product integrity, compliance, and customer trust across a rapidly growing business. This is not just about maintaining standards but about building a future-state vision for quality that enables growth, safeguards mission success, and strengthens EBAD’s reputation as a trusted partner.

**The Opportunity:**

EBAD’s customers depend on us to deliver our products with zero failure in mission-critical environments. The Director of Quality will be responsible for developing and executing a strategic Quality Management System (QMS) while leading quality operations across multiple sites. This leader will be tasked with driving measurable quality improvement, while also championing a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

This is an exciting opportunity for a leader to make an immediate impact by providing direction, driving the strategy for the business, and developing a problem-solving culture.

**Core Competencies for Success:**

* **Quality & Compliance Leadership:** Proven success leading complex, multi-site quality organizations in aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability industries, with expertise in zero-failure mission environments.

* **Continuous Improvement & Performance:** Skilled in EBOS, Lean, and Kaizen practices with the ability to drive metrics-based improvement and systemic problem-solving.
* **Team Development & Leadership:** Demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and build strong teams while fostering engagement and accountability.
* **Collaboration & Influence:** Strong cross-functional partnership with credibility to influence senior leadership, customers, and suppliers.
* **Resilience & Adaptability:** Able to manage ambiguity, drive change, and motivate teams in a fast-scaling environment.

**The Candidate We Are Looking For:**

* BS in an engineering discipline (MS preferred)
* Minimum 10 years of experience in high-mix, low-volume operations and manufacturing environment
* Proven success leading complex, multi-site quality organizations in aerospace, defense, or other mission-critical industries
* Demonstrated expertise in leading audits and managing compliance across regulatory bodies, customers, and suppliers, with deep knowledge of standards such as AS9100, ISO9001, and DoD requirements
* Proven ability to enhance customer quality by partnering closely with engineering, operations, and supply chain teams to consistently meet customer demand
* Strong record of measurable quality improvements
* Skilled in continuous improvement, performance metrics, and problem-solving through EBOS, Lean, and Kaizen practices
* Track record of building and developing strong teams, fostering high engagement, and driving accountability

**A Defining Leadership Opportunity:**

* **Legacy:** Join a privately held, 188-year-old business that takes a long-term approach, free from the short-term pressures of quarterly-driven reporting.
* **Impact:** Lead a mission-critical function where zero failure is the standard and success is business-defining.
* **Partnership:** Work directly with the BU President, senior leadership, and enterprise HR leaders in a highly influential role at the intersection of people and business strategy.
* **Culture of Excellence:** Help shape a culture that values people, integrity, and mission-driven excellence, driven by a Kaizen mindset and a commitment to quality and continuous improvement.

**Ready to Make a Difference?**

If you’re a proven quality engineering leader with the vision, discipline, and drive to achieve zero failure in a complex and growing business, this is your opportunity.

**Compensation and Rewards:**

We recognize that world-class leaders deliver world-class impact, and we reward accordingly. This role offers a competitive executive package that includes:

**Base Salary:** $175k – $225k plus annual bonus

**Executive Relocation:** Comprehensive support for a seamless transition

**Additional Enhancements:** Potential sign-on incentives and tailored rewards based on experience

*We offer a competitive compensation package aligned with skills & experience, with flexibility to reward top talent and extraordinary qualifications.*

*Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE). Qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, age, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, national origin, or veteran status.*

records.title: Sr. Director, Global Manufacturing Strategy & Network Transformation

postedPay.title: Sr. Director, Global Manufacturing Strategy & Network Transformation

records.description:
Location:
Buffalo, NY, US, 14213

Req ID: 41812

Segment: Supply Chain

Rich’s, also known as Rich Products Corporation, is a family-owned food company dedicated to inspiring possibilities. From cakes and icings to pizza, appetizers and specialty toppings, our products are used in homes, restaurants and bakeries around the world. Beyond great food, our customers also gain insights to help them stay competitive, no matter their size. Our portfolio includes creative solutions geared at helping food industry professionals compete in foodservice, retail, in-store bakery, deli, and prepared foods, among others. With more than 13,500 associates working globally in 100 countries and annual sales of $5.9 billion, Rich’s is a global leader with a focus on everything that family makes possible. Rich’s®—Infinite Possibilities. One Family.

**Purpose Statement**
---------------------

The Senior Director/VP, Global Manufacturing Strategy & Network Transformation will shape and drive the long-term manufacturing strategy for the enterprise, with primary accountability for the global TCCS manufacturing network and a broader mandate to identify opportunities across the total manufacturing enterprise. Reporting to the Head of Operations, this leader will guide critical decisions around manufacturing footprint, capacity and capability, capital deployment, technology, and operating standards across businesses and regions.

This role will be instrumental in ensuring the manufacturing network is positioned to support significant global growth and evolving business needs. The leader will take an enterprise-wide view of manufacturing, connecting sites, regions, and businesses to optimize existing assets and capabilities, identify network opportunities, anticipate future capacity requirements, and inform strategic investments.

Working across regional and business manufacturing organizations, Supply Chain, Quality, R&D, Finance, Procurement, and Commercial, this executive will bring together complex operational and business inputs to establish clear manufacturing priorities and translate strategy into an actionable, long-range network roadmap. The role will also serve as a trusted manufacturing advisor to the Head of Operations and broader executive leadership team.

**Key Accountabilities and Outcomes**
-------------------------------------

* Set the long-term vision and network roadmap for global TCCS manufacturing, aligned to the Enterprise TCCS strategic plan and Vision 2030, and help shape the broader enterprise manufacturing strategy.
* Act as the manufacturing business partner to the EBU lead: bring manufacturing input into the annual strategic planning cycle, flag where growth plans require new lines or capabilities, and coordinate regional responses through one point of contact.
* Partner with Supply Chain Planning to model capacity against growth plans over a five-year horizon, identifying where and when the network will run short and recommending the best response: add lines, build new capacity, use open capacity in another region, or consolidate.
* Lead network optimization and footprint scenarios across regions, such as building new capacity in one country versus using available capacity in another, or rebalancing frozen and aseptic/UHT capacity, recognizing that idle capacity also carries cost.
* Partner with Finance on major capacity and capability investments, including greenfield and brownfield projects: bring the operational view to the business case, test assumptions on cost, capacity, risk, and timing, and help shape recommendations for executive approval.
* Prepare the network for strategic global customers and programs by anticipating long-lead equipment needs, including when to pre-purchase or hold critical equipment so growth is not delayed by equipment lead times.
* Set equipment strategy across sites, including where to standardize equipment and line design (for example, common aerators and processing equipment), and define required certifications, specifications, and hygienic design standards.
* Partner with Procurement on equipment sourcing, including qualifying new and lower-cost vendors and using economies of scale when several lines are installed in different regions at the same time.
* Support the capital planning process, led by Finance, by working with plants and regional leaders to build the right capital requests, grounded in growth plans, equipment age and life cycle, and historical spend, so capital goes where it creates the most value.
* Design a global critical spare parts strategy, including hub- or region-based stocking of high-value parts such as homogenizer blocks, to lower cost while protecting uptime.
* Use manufacturing KPIs across the TCCS network (yield, OEE, cost, uptime, and resource use such as water per liter produced) to benchmark sites, spot gaps, and identify the biggest opportunities to optimize performance and cost.
* Turn those opportunities into results by working with program and functional leaders, including TPM, Smart Factory, Engineering, Quality, Procurement, and the regional manufacturing teams, to prioritize, launch, and track improvement initiatives, capture gains before adding capacity, and scale proven practices across the network.
* Support high-priority global customer launches by coordinating across regions when issues arise, such as shifting production to another site or country.
* Partner with regional manufacturing leaders as a peer and strategic advisor: align on network priorities, co-develop multi-year regional roadmaps, and support delivery through clear governance, milestones, decision gates, and measurable outcomes.
* Build organizational capability in manufacturing strategy, network optimization, and capital planning across the TCCS network, and lead a small, high-impact team that supports the regions.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Experience**
-------------------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Business, or a related field; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive experience in supply chain, manufacturing, operations, or engineering, including at least 5 years at the Director level or above with multi-site and multi-country responsibility.
* Experience across more than one supply chain discipline, such as manufacturing operations, engineering, network design and optimization, capacity planning, S&OP, or supply chain finance. Candidates from finance or strategy roles with significant supply chain exposure are encouraged to apply.
* Track record leading or shaping network and footprint decisions across multiple sites or countries, such as capacity expansion, consolidation, site selection, or make-versus-buy and inter-plant sourcing.
* Experience partnering with Finance to build business cases for capital investments (new lines, plant expansions, greenfield or brownfield projects) and supporting them through approval and execution.
* Food or beverage manufacturing experience preferred; experience with aseptic, UHT, frozen, or dairy processing is a plus.
* Exposure to manufacturing performance and asset programs such as TPM, OEE and yield improvement, lean, critical spares and equipment life-cycle management, equipment standardization and sourcing, or digital and Smart Factory initiatives.
* Experience working in a global, matrixed organization with teams across regions and time zones (for example, Asia, Europe, and Latin America). Fluency in English required; additional languages a plus.

**Attributes for Success**

* Influences without authority: has delivered results through plant and regional leaders who did not report to them, by building trust, negotiating, and showing others what is in it for them.
* Analytical and data-driven: comfortable working with operational and financial data, knows which questions to ask, and turns analysis into clear, practical recommendations.
* Learns fast and drives results: a self-starter who gets up to speed quickly on new businesses, technologies, and regions, and can build a new role and strategy with minimal direction.
* Clear communicator, humble, and collaborative: communicates well up and down the organization and across cultures, follows up in writing, readily shares credit, and adapts their style to different audiences.

**Location, Travel, and Work Schedule**

* Location is flexible; Buffalo, NY is preferred given close partnership with the Head of Operations and headquarters leadership.
* Travel of approximately 30%, mainly in the first year to learn the regions and build relationships with teams and sites in Asia, Latin America, and the US; ongoing travel based on business needs, not constant travel.
* As a global role, flexibility for early-morning or evening meetings with teams in Asia, Europe, and Latin America is required.

**Job Description** :

**Summary**

The Director of Continuous Improvement will support the AAI (Automotive, Aerospace, and Industrial) vertical. The services are primarily warehousing operations for distribution and inbound to manufacturing operations.

This position supports the Ryder Continuous Improvement culture across the Business Unit by actively promoting and facilitating the use of continuous improvement methods to support new and existing operations.

The Director will lead a team of CI Managers/Leads across the business to influence and drive change through data driven CI, Engineering, and Automation efforts to deliver higher levels of performance in safety, quality, delivery, cost and growth. Effectively leverage data analytics, engineering methodologies, and all Ryder lean tools to enable root cause identification and elimination.

This high influence position will interface with employees at all levels and functions across the business. This individual will work directly with his/her Operational peers in the business units to define and set a strategy for engineering efforts and continuous improvement activities. This position directly reports to the Group or Senior Director of CI with dotted-line reporting to the assigned Groub Director/VP of Operations (Business Unit/Vertical). This individual will work directly with his/her peers and their direct reports in the business units to define and set a strategy for engineering efforts and continuous improvement activities for new and existing operations.

**Essential Functions**

* Directs continuous improvement program and oversees engineering support functions .Supervise a team of continuous improvement Managers and quality professionals. Make employment decisions (hire, promote, coach, development) and manage performance. Develop CI Engineering bench to strategically support the BU/Vertical long term requirements. Manages and assigns CI resources for multiple and complex Supply Chain projects aligned with strategic and growth initiatives. Regularly interacts with Senior Management and/or customer(s).
* Aligns CI initiatives and project objectives to business strategy and prioritizes projects accordingly; includes key stakeholders in process, as required. Facilitate strategic planning (vertical blueprinting) and tactical process improvement events. Lead cross functional team to identify improvement opportunities and works with leadership to prioritize & plan initiatives. Present to executive leadership team on status and results of continuous improvement initiatives. Participate in regular business review session with VP of Operations, SCE team and Customers . Provide regular reports of data and actions to measure progress against strategic business objectives.
* Provide training, coaching, and mentoring: must be able to translate all Ryder Business System concepts and strategic objectives to local situations and help all levels of the organization develop understanding and application of tools for sustainable business improvements. Coach business owners to use Engineering, Data Analysis and Lean methods to achieve operational excellence. Support start-ups, retrofits and expansions including pricing inputs, go-live and steady state certifications.
* Work with vertical leaders to establish continuous improvement goals, and act as a liaison with finance to build continuous improvement budgets and validating actual improvement results. Develops, deploys and maintains account plans for assigned process areas designed to continually improve service offerings through the implementation of recognized engineering, quality, lean standards, continuous improvement strategies and demonstrated best practices. Manage monthly budget review process and financial reconciliation. Interfaces with senior level management to establish standard quality communications and action oriented forums (reviewing /analyzing operational performance, deploy policies and strategies, share best practices)
* Serve as the business owner, establish and regulate the standards for Quality Management Systems based on company and/or industry standards. Oversee internal auditing to ensure regulatory compliance and certification. Facilitate regular Performance Reviews with operations leadership and monitor metrics. Develop/implement strategy to manage scope and meet customer expectations. Support business start-ups, retrofits and expansions including pricing inputs, go-live and steady state certifications. Manage the design, implementation, monitoring and maintenance of the QMS based on established company and/or industry standards. Implement and monitor a standardized corrective action system. Support regulatory compliance and certification requirements. Oversee all functions related to Quality Assurance for a start-up or expansion
* Effective facilitation and execution of Value Stream Maps & Kaizen Events through all stages (A3 charter creation, pre-work identification and completion, delivery of results, regular follow up and follow through on sustainment). Independently identifies process gaps and recommends and leads CI Team to implement process improvement. Manage, track, and report the progress and value of the transformational activities and projects across customer accounts. Direct the assessment, development, implementation, and continuous improvement activities related to the implementation of lean processes across accounts.

**Additional Responsibilities**

* Manage the design, implementation, monitoring and maintenance of the QMS based on established company and/or industry standards.
* Implement and monitor a standardized corrective action system.
* Support regulatory compliance and certification requirements.
* Oversee all functions related to Quality Assurance for a start-up or expansion.
* Oversee internal auditing to ensure regulatory compliance and certification.
* Performs other duties as assigned

**Skills and Abilities**

* Microsoft Office Suite skills with emphasis on Access, Excel and PowerPoint & Visioexpert required
* Data visualization (PowerBI, Tableau) and database programming (SQL, DAX, etc.) intermediate preferred
* Expertise in developing and managing: Leader Standard Work, Visual Management Systems and Management Accountability Systems, Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA), Value Stream Mapping, Kaizen, 5S/Workplace Organization expert required
* Understanding and experience in core engineering and data analysis functions (slotting, utilization, labor planning, layouts, metrics, etc.) and warehouse design tools such as CAD (e.gAutoCAD); slotting (e.gSlot3D), Predetermined Motion and Time Systems and methods (e.gMOST); Warehouse Management Systems (e.gManhattan Scale), and Labor MgtSystems expert preferred
* Knowledge of Warehouse Management operations, data analytics, Industrial Engineering, warehouse types (ambient, temp control, warehouse layout/ design and Lean methods
* Knowledge of material handling solutions and automation types such as: powered industrial truck (PIT) applications; racking and other storage solution designs, packaging equipment; conveyor and sortation equipment; and other automation solutions (e.gAS/RS)expert required
* Knowledge of Dedicated Services and Managed Transportation Networks
* Knowledge of all available equipment types such as; dry van, temperature control, flat bed, other specialized equipment
* Transportation Design Tools ie; JDA, Appian, Network Design Tools ie; Llamasoft, Transportation Management Systems ie; JDA, OTM, , Mapping Software ie; Tableau expert required
* Knowledge working with HRM systems (e.gWorkday) and associated HR processes
* Knowledge on team member hiring/on-boardingKnowledge of goal setting and performance management/resolutionadvanced preferred

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree required Engineering, Business, Supply Chain
* Master's degree preferred Supply Chain Management or Industrial Engineering
* Ten (10) years or more Fourteen (14) yrs or more in the Distribution, Warehousing and/or Manufacturing, Transportation, Supply Chain Logistics industry required
* Microsoft Office Suite skills with emphasis on Access, Excel and PowerPoint & Visio. expert required
* Data visualization (PowerBI, Tableau) and database programming (SQL, DAX, etc.) intermediate preferred
* Expertise in developing and managing: Leader Standard Work, Visual Management Systems and Management Accountability Systems, Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA), Value Stream Mapping, Kaizen, 5S/Workplace Organization expert required
* Understanding and experience in core engineering and data analysis functions (slotting, utilization, labor planning, layouts, metrics, etc.) and warehouse design tools such as CAD (e.g. AutoCAD); slotting (e.g. Slot3D), Predetermined Motion and Time Systems and methods (e.g. MOST); Warehouse Management Systems (e.g. Manhattan Scale), and Labor Mgt. Systems. expert preferred
* Knowledge of Warehouse Management operations, data analytics, Industrial Engineering, warehouse types (ambient, temp control, warehouse layout/ design and Lean methods. Knowledge of material handling solutions and automation types such as: powered industrial truck (PIT) applications; racking and other storage solution designs, packaging equipment; conveyor and sortation equipment; and other automation solutions (e.g. AS/RS). expert required
* Knowledge of Dedicated Services and Managed Transportation Networks. Knowledge of all available equipment types such as; dry van, temperature control, flat bed, other specialized equipment. Transportation Design Tools ie; JDA, Appian, Network Design Tools ie; Llamasoft, Transportation Management Systems ie; JDA, OTM, , Mapping Software ie; Tableau. expert required
* Knowledge working with HRM systems (e.g. Workday) and associated HR processes. Knowledge on team member hiring/on-boarding. Knowledge of goal setting and performance management/resolution. advanced preferred
* Lean Six Sigma, required
* American Production Inventory Control Society (APICS) and/or Supply Chain Logistics Certification is preferred
* cPMP, ISO/QMS, preferred

This position is remote, when you are not traveling.

At Ryder, you’re trusted to make an impact—while enjoying room to grow and having a voice that’s heard. Our culture is built on respect, collaboration, and shared pride in doing great work rooted in innovation and safety.

records.title: Director, PXT - Amazon Leo Production Operations

postedPay.title: Director, PXT - Amazon Leo Production Operations

records.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Amazon has committed more than $10 billion to Amazon Leo, a low Earth orbit satellite network designed to bring fast, affordable broadband to customers around the world. Production Operations is where that ambition becomes physical. Every Leo satellite weighs more than 1,000 pounds, contains roughly 4 million individual components, and is designed and built in-house on a 172,000 square foot custom production line in Kirkland, Washington, capable of producing up to five satellite a day. The team completed its 1,000th satellite in September 2026 (https://www.aboutamazon.com/stories/how-amazon-leo-builds-satellites), making Leo one of the largest and most advanced satellite production operations in the world. 
From the factory, satellites move to a 100,000 square foot payload processing facility at Kennedy Space Center in Florida that can support three launch campaigns at once, and to launch operations in French Guiana. With more than 80 launches secured across four launch providers, Leo plans to double its launch rate to more than 20 missions in its second year. The organization spans eight sites today across multiple states and ground stations across multiple countries, with more investments coming through in the times ahead. 
This role builds on Amazon's deep operations heritage and takes it to newer heights. You will partner with an organization that brings together aerospace, RF, supply chain and manufacturing experts, recruited from the leading space and defense companies, alongside a skilled hourly production and launch workforce building and launching satellite in clean rooms, across shifts, and on mission-critical launch campaigns. Few people leaders anywhere get to shape all of this at once: precision satellite manufacturing across multiple satellite generations, export-controlled and government production, and Amazon Leo's first employing entity outside the US. 
The people decisions made in the next 18 months will shape this organization for the next decade. As the senior PXT leader for Production Operations, you will make them alongside the VP of Production Operations and the multiple Directors who lead satellite manufacturing, launch operations, supply chain, quality, ground gateways, global trade and compliance, enterprise technology, and Manufacturing Systems Engineering and New Product Introduction. You won't be inheriting a playbook. You'll be writing it. 
What makes this role unique 

* Two talent markets, one interwoven strategy. Build differentiated people programs for a highly technical corporate workforce competing in one of the most constrained talent markets in the world, and for a large, fast growing hourly manufacturing and launch workforce, under a single coherent people strategy.
* Organization design at a defining moment. Shape org design, leadership formation, and succession as the organization scales across multiple satellite generations, direct-to-device, and government production in parallel, with a leadership team forming as it grows.
* People infrastructure Amazon has never built. Create job families, compensation, and career frameworks for roles Amazon has never hired before, people processes for export-controlled and cleared work, and Amazon Leo's first non-US employing entity at a launch site.
* Proactive employee and labor relations. Set a direct-engagement and labor relations strategy for an hourly workforce, across factories and launch sites in multiple states and countries.

 
Key job responsibilities 

* Serve as strategic people partner to the VP of Production Operations and Director-level function leaders, advising on organizational design, talent architecture, site strategy, and workforce planning across corporate technical and hourly populations.
* Shape the multi-year organization design for Production Operations as it scales across multiple satellite generations, direct-to-device, and government production, including new leadership roles and structures.
* Lead talent strategy for specialized technical roles (aerospace manufacturing, RF and telecommunications engineering, satellite quality, supply chain and trade compliance, AI and automation), competing against established aerospace and defense employers.
* Build scalable HR infrastructure for a 24/7 manufacturing and launch operation, including new-to-Amazon approaches to timekeeping, attendance, performance management, and shift support.
* Lead people strategy for Launch Operations, including sustainable staffing models for launch campaigns, rotational teams, off-shift coverage, and recurring travel.
* Set a proactive labor and employee relations strategy in partnership with Global Employee Relations and Labor Relations, coaching senior operations leaders on direct employee engagement at every site.
* Define people requirements for export-controlled and government manufacturing, including security clearances, cleared hiring pipelines, and compliant people processes, with Legal and Security.
* Stand up Amazon Leo's first non-US employee population at an international launch site, including employment contracts, compensation and benefits, payroll, and statutory compliance.
* Drive leadership development, calibration, promotion readiness, and succession planning across a rapidly expanding senior leadership bench.
* Build and lead a team of HR Business Partners, operating through a deep matrix across HR Partners, Talent Acquisition, Compensation, Talent Management, Employee Relations, PXT Technology, and international partners.

 
Click the link to see how Amazon’s growing constellation of custom-built satellites will work together to bring internet connectivity anywhere on the planet: https://www.aboutamazon.com/stories/how-amazon-leo-satellite-internet-works

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or related field, or equivalent experience
* 15+ years of progressive human resources experience
* 10+ years of experience as an HR business partner supporting senior executives
* 7+ years of experience leading HR strategy for large-scale manufacturing, production, or operations organizations with hourly or shift-based workforces
* 5+ years of experience leading HR strategy for organizations operating across multiple countries and legal entities
* Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* Master's degree in Human Resources or MBA
* Experience with employee and labor relations in union represented or union-exposed environments
* Experience designing organizational structures, compensation frameworks, and job architecture for large, fast-growing organizations
* Experience leading people strategy in aerospace, defense, satellite, telecommunications, or advanced manufacturing
* Experience supporting highly technical engineering populations alongside hourly production workforces
* Experience supporting launch, flight, field, or campaign-based operations with rotational or travel-intensive staffing
* Experience designing people processes for export-controlled (ITAR/EAR) or government cleared work environments
* Experience standing up new sites, greenfield operations, or new country employing entities
* Track record of building senior leadership teams and coaching executives through rapid organizational change
* Ability to thrive in ambiguity and to build mechanisms that scale beyond any single leader

 
Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. 
 
Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits.

 
USA, WA, Bellevue - 200,700.00 - 271,600.00 USD annually
