records.title: Director of Quality
records.description:
**Position Overview:**

The Director of Quality will lead the quality function across the organization and create the operating model required for the company’s next stage of growth. This leader will be accountable for enterprise quality strategy, product and process quality, supplier and customer quality, and the effectiveness of the company’s quality management systems. The role will maintain applicable certifications, including ISO 13485, ISO 9001, and AS9100, while establishing a disciplined approach to quality diligence and integration for future acquisitions.

The Director of Quality must combine independent judgment with a practical understanding of manufacturing. This leader will know what strong quality looks like, but will build it in a way that fits the company's scale, products, customers, and maturity. Success requires the ability to move between enterprise strategy and a specific customer or production issue; challenge legacy practices while respecting operational knowledge; and bring people through change with clarity, evidence, and follow-through.

This is not a quality-systems-only position. The Director must remain close to manufacturing, customers, and the issues that affect product conformity, delivery, cost, and trust. The successful candidate will bring the rigor expected in regulated manufacturing, apply it without unnecessary bureaucracy, and build a quality organization that can identify risk early, solve problems at their source, and support sustainable growth.

**Essential Functions:**

* Set the global quality strategy. Assess the company's current quality environment and establish a multiyear roadmap aligned with business strategy, customer commitments, regulatory obligations, and acquisition plans. Translate the roadmap into clear priorities, resources, ownership, and measures of success.
* Lead the quality organization. Direct and develop quality leaders and teams across the sites. Define the structure, capabilities, decision rights, and functional accountability required to support a larger international manufacturing organization.
* Own the enterprise quality management system. Ensure effective governance and execution across document and change control, training, nonconformance, CAPA, complaints, risk management, supplier controls, internal audits, management review, and other core processes. Maintain applicable certifications and compliance with customer and regulatory requirements.
* Strengthen product and process quality. Partner with Operations and Engineering to improve quality planning, process validation and control, inspection, calibration, measurement systems, first-article or new-product readiness, and change execution. Use disciplined problem solving and prevention to reduce defects, scrap, rework, escapes, and recurring failures.
* Lead customer and supplier quality. Establish consistent expectations for customer issue response, supplier qualification and monitoring, supplier corrective action, and escalation. Ensure material issues are contained quickly, investigated to root cause, resolved with effective corrective action, and communicated with credibility.
* Create audit and inspection readiness. Lead the enterprise internal audit program and oversee registrar, customer, and regulatory audits. Maintain visibility to findings, commitments, certification status, and systemic risk, and verify that corrective actions are timely and effective.
* Use data to govern performance. Establish a focused set of enterprise and site quality measures, including customer complaints, defects, escapes, scrap and rework, supplier performance, CAPA effectiveness, and audit performance. Lead global management review and give executives a clear view of trends, risk, and required actions.
* Harmonize with purpose. Define the policies, standards, escalation requirements, and controls that must be common across the organization. Rationalize legacy processes and quality technologies, including eQMS capabilities, while preserving local differences that are justified by product, customer, regulatory, or operating needs.
* Lead quality through acquisitions. Support quality due diligence by assessing systems, certifications, audit history, customer and regulatory commitments, product and process risk, and organizational capability. Build and execute risk-based integration plans with clear Day 1 controls, remediation priorities, and a realistic path to the quality model.
* Exercise independent quality authority. Ensure that Quality has direct access to the information and leaders needed to escalate material risk. Maintain clear authority to contain nonconforming product and stop release or shipment when applicable requirements may not be met, while building shared ownership of quality across the business.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, science, quality, or a related technical field.
* At least 10 years of progressive quality experience in manufacturing, including at least five years leading quality teams or leaders.
* Demonstrated success leading quality across multiple manufacturing sites, business units, or regions.
* Experience with product and process quality, quality engineering, customer quality, supplier quality, and quality management systems in a regulated or highly technical environment.
* Strong working knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 9001, and AS9100, including direct responsibility for audits, certification, corrective action, and management review. Equivalent experience spanning multiple regulated standards will be considered.
* Deep experience with CAPA, nonconformance, root-cause analysis, risk management, process validation and control, measurement systems, and data-driven continuous improvement.
* Ability to identify and communicate material product, customer, and compliance risk and to influence operational and executive decisions with sound evidence and judgment.
* Experience building teams, developing leaders, and driving change across a matrixed or decentralized organization.
* Ability and willingness to travel regularly within the United States and Europe.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Experience in precision manufacturing serving medical device, aerospace, life sciences, or other regulated and quality-sensitive markets.
* Experience in an acquisition-driven, or rapidly scaling organization.
* Experience conducting quality due diligence and integrating acquired manufacturing businesses, sites, or quality systems.
* Experience with electronic quality management systems, quality data architecture, or digital quality transformation.
* Working knowledge of applicable medical device regulations and audit programs, such as FDA QMSR, EU MDR, or MDSAP.
* Lead Auditor, ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, Certified Quality Engineer, or Lean Six Sigma certification.
* Experience leading quality across the United States and Europe.

**How will you make your impact?**
As the
**Head of Quality,**
you will leader to define, implement, and continuously improve the Quality Management System across the Americas. This role is responsible for ensuring quality is designed into every stage of project delivery, from engineering and procurement through construction, commissioning, and closeout. This is a highly visible leadership role with direct influence on project performance, supplier quality, operational discipline, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement across the Americas.
  
  
The
**Head of Quality**
will establish and lead a quality organization that embeds quality into how projects are planned, executed, and continuously improved.
  
  
You will drive a preventive approach to quality by strengthening planning, supplier oversight, project controls, auditing, and lessons learned. You will create the frameworks that connect Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Project Delivery, and Quality into a single system focused on delivering projects right the first time. Success will be measured by reductions in rework and recurring issues, stronger supplier performance, improved audit outcomes, increased first-time-right execution, and the maturity of the quality culture across the organization.
  
  
**What will you do?**

* You will lead the development and continuous improvement of the Americas Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring consistent standards, governance, and accountability across the region.
* You will establish quality requirements and controls from tender through project closeout to ensure quality is built into project delivery from the outset.
* You will implement risk-based supplier qualification, surveillance, inspection, and release processes to improve supplier quality performance.
* You will ensure inspection and test plans align with engineering requirements, contract obligations, and construction execution strategies.
* You will lead audits, management reviews, quality assurance programs, and performance reporting across the project portfolio.
* You will drive root-cause analysis and corrective action processes that address systemic issues rather than isolated events.
* You will establish and lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on reducing defects, rework, and the Cost of Poor Quality.
* You will build and develop a high-performing Quality Assurance and Quality Control organization across the Americas.
* You will strengthen collaboration across Engineering, Procurement, PMO, Construction, and HSE to improve quality outcomes throughout the project lifecycle.
* You will develop quality capability, training programs, succession plans, and best practices that support long-term organizational growth.
* You will assess and strengthen the Americas Quality Management System, focusing resources on the highest-priority risks and improvement opportunities.
* You will establish clear quality governance, accountability, and performance reporting across the region.
* You will standardize project quality planning, supplier quality management, inspection requirements, and NCR governance practices.
* You will improve visibility into the Cost of Poor Quality, quality trends, and leading indicators across the project portfolio.
* You will reduce recurring quality issues, rework, and warranty exposure through stronger preventive controls and root-cause resolution.
* You will improve audit performance, supplier quality outcomes, and project readiness before execution begins.
* You will create a culture where quality is proactively planned, owned, measured, and continuously improved across functions.
* You will build a scalable quality organization capable of supporting Linxon's continued growth across the Americas.

**Who you are?**

* You are an experienced quality leader with 7-15+ years of experience in EPC, power, industrial, construction, manufacturing, or other complex project environments.
* You are proven in leading multi-project or regional Quality Management Systems and driving quality performance across diverse operations.
* You are knowledgeable in ISO 9001 principles, supplier quality management, project QA/QC, auditing practices, and root-cause methodologies.
* You are skilled at translating quality data and performance trends into preventive actions, operational discipline, and business improvements.
* You are experienced in developing quality organizations, improving governance, and building sustainable quality cultures.
* You hold a degree in engineering, quality, or a related technical field, and quality or auditing certifications are considered an asset.
* You are a leader who puts the mission, the customer, and the team ahead of individual recognition.
* You are comfortable making decisions with incomplete information and adjusting course as conditions change.
* You are committed to raising standards while fostering respect, inclusion, and psychological safety.
* You are passionate about developing people, sharing knowledge, and strengthening organizational capability.
* You are trusted because of your actions, credibility, and follow-through rather than your title.
* You are disciplined, data-driven, and focused on creating systems that prevent issues rather than simply react to them.

records.description:
Shape the future of quality and patient trust. Join us as the Vice President, Global Quality Control and lead a world-class laboratory network that powers our clinical and commercial programs across the globe. Reporting to the Chief Quality Officer, you will set the enterprise strategy and build a unified, high-performing Quality Control organization that delivers reliable data, inspection-ready laboratories, and timely product release support—while advancing standardization, digital innovation, scientific excellence, and operational performance.

The work we do at FUJIFILM Biotechnologies has never been more important—and we are looking for talented candidates to join us. We are growing our locations, our capabilities, and our teams, and looking for passionate, mission-driven people like you who want to make a real difference in people’s lives.
  
  
Join FUJIFILM Biotechnologies and help make the next vaccine, cure, or gene therapy in partnership with some of the most innovative biopharma companies across the globe. We are proud to cultivate a culture that will fuel your passion, energy, and drive - what we call Genki.
  
  
Fujifilm is globally headquartered in Tokyo with over 70,000 employees across four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging. We are guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles.” Visit: https://www.fujifilm.com/us/en/about/region/careers
  
  
**Job Description**
Your impact In this enterprise role, your leadership will directly influence patient safety, product quality, inspection outcomes, batch disposition timelines, and continuity of supply across a diverse global portfolio. You will advise senior executives on investment, capacity, technology, organizational design, and regulatory strategy—shaping multi‑year business and quality plans. Your decisions will strengthen client trust, accelerate revenue recognition, reduce the cost of quality, and protect the company’s license to operate.
  
  
What you will do
  
  

* Define and execute a global Quality Control strategy, operating model, and multi‑year roadmap across sites, modalities, and development phases. Establish enterprise standards, clear decision rights, and governance forums that enable consistent, phase‑appropriate control while allowing justified site or platform differences.
* Provide executive oversight of end‑to‑end Quality Control operations, including analytical, biochemical, biological, microbiological, raw‑material, in‑process, release, and stability testing; as well as environmental and utility monitoring. Ensure capacity, prioritization, and flawless execution to meet program milestones, product disposition, client commitments, and uninterrupted supply.
* Govern the analytical method lifecycle from early development through transfer, qualification, validation, comparability, continued performance verification, and retirement. Ensure control strategies and specifications evolve appropriately through clinical development, process performance qualification, launch, and sustained commercial supply.
* Set global expectations for current good manufacturing practice, applicable good laboratory practice principles, data governance, principles that ensure data are attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate and complete, laboratory investigations, out of specification and out of trend management, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, change control, and audit readiness. Lead enterprise strategy and executive response for regulatory inspections and critical client audits.
* Build and deliver the digital and technology roadmap for laboratory information management systems, electronic laboratory notebooks, laboratory execution systems, chromatography data systems, laboratory automation, advanced analytics, and instrument connectivity. Sponsor validated deployment, master‑data governance, cybersecurity, and adoption that improve right‑first‑time outcomes and cycle time.
* Direct enterprise Quality Control capacity planning, capital prioritization, make‑versus‑buy decisions, laboratory footprint strategy, and governance of external testing partners. Align resources and contingency plans with demand forecasts, technology transfers, new product introductions, and network resiliency needs.
* Establish enterprise metrics and management review for on‑time testing and release support, lead time, invalid results, out of specification and out of trend rates, investigation cycle time, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, stability execution, method performance, cost, and productivity. Drive risk‑based priorities, Lean practices, and cross‑site learning to deliver sustainable improvement.
* Serve as the senior Quality Control liaison for strategic clients, regulatory authorities, and executive governance. Translate complex laboratory, method, and compliance risks into clear business implications, negotiate technically sound solutions, and ensure commitments are realistic, documented, and delivered.
* Build and lead a global organization through senior leaders. Define capabilities and succession plans, develop technical career paths and communities of practice, and cultivate a culture of scientific rigor, transparency, accountability, inclusion, and proactive risk management.
* Own escalation and coordinated response for significant Quality Control events, laboratory constraints, critical data‑integrity concerns, assay failures, method or specification issues, and testing disruptions. Make or recommend risk‑based decisions on testing strategy, product impact, remediation, and continuity of supply.
* Perform other duties in support of the broader Global Quality strategy and company objectives.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline, with fifteen or more years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or contract development and manufacturing organization Quality Control; or a Master’s degree with ten or more years.
* Ten or more years of people leadership, including five or more years leading senior leaders with accountability for multiple laboratories, sites, or functional areas.
* Demonstrated leadership of Quality Control across development and commercial stages, including method transfer, qualification and validation, release and stability testing, microbiology, and environmental and utility monitoring.
* Proven experience with global regulatory inspections and client audits, and with complex out of specification, out of trend, data‑integrity, and laboratory‑compliance matters.
* Experience managing budgets, capital portfolios, headcount, capacity, external laboratories, and enterprise transformation in a matrixed global organization.
* Executive‑level communication and client‑facing experience in a regulated, technically complex environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced scientific degree and/or a Master of Business Administration.
* Global leadership within a contract development and manufacturing organization supporting biologics, vaccines, advanced therapies, or sterile manufacturing.
* Experience scaling Quality Control from clinical development through process performance qualification, launch, and sustained commercial supply.
* Working knowledge of the following: Food and Drug Administration; European Medicines Agency; Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency; Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency; International Council for Harmonisation guidelines Q2, Q5, Q6, Q9, Q10, and Q14; United States Pharmacopeia; European Pharmacopoeia; Japanese Pharmacopoeia; Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations Parts 210, 211, and 11; and European Union Good Manufacturing Practice Annexes 1 and 11; as well as applicable data‑integrity expectations.
* Experience deploying global laboratory information management systems and laboratory digitalization and automation.
* Credentials from the American Society for Quality, and training in Lean and Six Sigma or equivalent quality and operational excellence disciplines.

If you are a strategic, hands‑on executive who thrives at the intersection of science, operations, and leadership, we would love to hear from you. Apply today and help us raise the bar for quality worldwide.

**ABOUT THE COMPANY**

We are a Silicon Valley, San Jose based stealth start-up and are looking for a passionate, ambitious individual who shares our vision of next generation disruptive memory solutions for Agentic AI inference and high performance data center computing applications.

This is an impactful and senior leadership role allowing you to mastermind the realization of our strategic ambitions and shape the direction of our product portfolio development.

**ABOUT THE ROLE**

This is a senior leadership role for manufacturing enablement of our disruptive product which is a purpose-built memory for AI inference computing. As the Vice President of Manufacturing you will lead the enablement of the road to manufacturing, lead manufacturing strategic scoping of manufacturing partnerships, negotiate supply chain agreements, and be responsible for our global fab operations and supply chain execution for our memory product lines.

**CORE RESPONSIBILITIES**

* **Fab & Production Leadership:**
  Oversee high-volume semiconductor fabrication plants, assembly, test, and packaging operations across global sites. Define a winning manufacturing strategy based on a deep understanding of our specific materials, device and memory type.
* **Yield & Quality Optimization:**
  Drive continuous improvement in wafer/die yields, defect reduction, test coverage, reliability metrics and cost competitiveness.
* **CapEx & Technology Roadmaps:**
  Own multi-million-dollar capital expenditure budgets for cleanroom expansion, lithography/etch equipment upgrades, and next-gen node transitions.
* **Executive Collaboration:**
  Partner with the CEO, CTO, CCO and technology teams to align fab strategies and output with market demand, product lifecycles, and customer commitments.
* **Supply Chain & Risk Management:**
  Manage strategic foundry/supplier relationships, raw material security (silicon wafers, specialty gases), and emergency crisis responses.
* **Compliance & Safety:**
  Enforce strict cleanroom safety protocols, environmental regulations, and corporate governance.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS**

* **Education:**
  Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, or Industrial Engineering.
* **Experience:**
  15+ years of progressive executive or senior leadership experience in semiconductor manufacturing, operations, or process/device engineering. At least 7+ years of prior experience at leading memory IDMs or semiconductor foundries is required. Ability to bring up new products and scale up to high volume manufacturing (HVM) is preferred.
* **Domain Expertise:**
  Deep technical mastery of memory devices, technology products and associated manufacturing trade-offs and cleanroom/foundry dynamics.
* **Financial Acumen:**
  Proven P&L (Profit and Loss) management and large-scale CapEx justification experience.
* **Leadership Skills:**
  Track record of managing global operations, scaling global engineering teams, and driving continuous manufacturing improvement cultures.

records.description:
Eaton’s Electrical Sector America’s business is curretly hiring for a VP of Continuous Improvement & Lean. This role can be based at Eaton’s Cleveland or Pittsburgh office. Relocation within hiring country is offered. 50 percent travel is anticipated.
  
  
Reporting directly to the SVP of Operations, Electrical Sector – Americas (ESA), the VP of CI & Lean is the senior executive accountable for the vision, strategy, and results of the Eaton Continuous Improvement System (ECIS) across the $16B ESA business, spanning 60 manufacturing sites and 14 divisions. This role sets the multi-year Lean transformation agenda, builds continuous improvement into the sector's strategic and annual profit plans, and holds the business accountable for measurable improvement in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and growth.
  
  
The VP leads and develops the ESA CI team, defines the sector-wide operating model, standards, and governance the team deploys, and serves as a strategic advisor to the ESA leadership team. Rather than leading deployment within a division, this role directs CI resources to the highest-value opportunities, owns the sector's CI talent pipeline, and shapes a Lean leadership culture at the executive level. The VP also represents ESA in enterprise CI forums, partnering with Corporate CI & Quality to align standards and scale best practices across Eaton.
  
  
**Job Responsibilities**

* Defines the multi-year ESA Lean and continuous improvement vision, strategy, and roadmap, and integrates it into the sector's strategic plan and annual profit plan.
* Owns the ECIS operating model for ESA: sets the standards, maturity expectations, and governance that the CI team deploys across divisions, functions, and sites.
* Leads, coaches, and develops the ESA CI team; sets objectives, allocates CI resources, and holds the team accountable for results.
* Chairs the Divisional CI Council across all ESA divisions and leads sector-level performance reviews, establishing the operating cadence that links CI results to business performance.
* Accountable for the ESA cost-out and productivity commitments delivered through CI; builds the sector project pipeline and validates financial impact.
* Serves as strategic advisor to the SVP of Operations and the ESA leadership team, prioritizing the transformation initiatives with the greatest business value.
* Sponsors large-scale, cross-divisional transformations (e.g., footprint changes, acquisition integrations, and Lean in office and transactional processes).
* Builds the sector CI talent strategy: capability standards, certification pathways (e.g., ASCEND X, PME), succession planning, and rotation of high-potential leaders through CI roles.
* Coaches ESA executives on Lean leadership behaviors and role-models a culture of accountability and continuous improvement from the top.
* Sets sector maturity targets and owns the EBSA and OpA assessment strategy; reviews results with leadership and directs closure of systemic gaps.
* Represents ESA in enterprise CI forums; partners with Corporate CI & Quality to shape Eaton-wide standards and scale proven practices across sectors.
* Manages the ESA CI function budget and champions digital and data analytics tools that accelerate improvement.

**Qualifications**
Required Qualifications:
  
  

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline from an accredited institution.
* Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in Continuous Improvement, Quality, or Operations
* Minimum 5 years leading leaders (managers or directors) at a multi-site, division, or business-unit level
* Proven track record leading Lean transformations that delivered measurable financial results, preferably in a multi-division manufacturing environment
* Professional experience in a global matrixed organization
* Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree or MBA preferred

**Position Success Criteria**

* Expert-level command of Lean and Six Sigma; Master Black Belt or Black Belt certification required
* Experience designing, governing, and maturing a business operating system and maturity model at scale
* Strong business and financial acumen: builds cost-out and productivity plans, quantifies impact, and ties CI results to the P&L
* Experience designing CI talent, certification, and capability programs across a large, multi-site organization
* Applies Lean to both manufacturing and office/transactional processes
* Executive presence; a trusted advisor who influences, challenges, and aligns senior executives
* Proven ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing teams of senior CI leaders
* Strategic thinker who turns vision into multi-year roadmaps and leads change at scale
* Excellent communication at every level, from the shop floor to the executive leadership team

The expected annual salary range for this role is $203000 - $297000 a year. This position is also eligible for a variable incentive program.

All positions may require participation in video and in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.

Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

Your responsibilities
  
  
**Lead Quality Excellence in a Fast-Paced Manufacturing Environment**
We are seeking an experienced
**Head of Quality**

This leadership role is responsible for overseeing the Quality Management System, developing quality strategies, leading customer and supplier quality initiatives, and driving continuous improvement throughout the organization.
  
  

* Lead and maintain the Quality Management System in compliance with IATF 16949 requirements.
* Develop and execute quality objectives, metrics, and improvement initiatives aligned with business goals.
* Manage customer and supplier quality activities, including audits, APQP, PPAP, launch readiness, corrective actions, and change management.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action efforts for internal and external quality issues.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance product quality, operational performance, and customer satisfaction.
* Monitor and report key quality metrics, including scrap, rework, and overall quality performance.
* Partner with cross-functional teams to support production, new product launches, and supplier development.
* Build, develop, and lead high-performing quality teams.

**Success Competencies**
The Head of Quality embodies the following competencies:
  
  

* Manages Complexity: Making sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems.
* Decision Quality: Making good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.
* Action Oriented: Taking on new opportunities and tough challenges with a sense of urgency, high energy and enthusiasm.
* Ensures Accountability: Holding self and others accountable to meet commitments.
* Drive Results: Consistently achieving results, even under tough circumstances.
* Develops Talent: Developing people to meet both their career goals and the organization’s goals.
* Builds Effective Teams: Building strong-identity teams that apply their diverse skills and perspective to achieve common goals.
* Communicates Effectively: Developing and delivering multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.
* Instills Trust: Gaining the confidence and trust of others though honesty, integrity, and authenticity.
* Manages Ambiguity: Operating effectively, even when things are not certain or the way forward is not clear.
* Being Resilient: Rebounding from setbacks and adversity when facing difficult situations.

Your profile

The Director is accountable for delivering strong performance in safety, quality, customer service, cost, productivity, and inventory while building manufacturing capabilities to support future business growth.
  
  
The successful candidate will bring strong manufacturing and technical leadership, business judgment, and experience leading complex operations in a regulated environment. This position partners closely with Quality, EH&S, R&D, Supply Chain, Finance, Legal, and business leadership to ensure reliable operations, successful new product introductions, and a resilient manufacturing network.

* Lead chemical manufacturing operations with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, inventory, and customer service.
* Develop and execute manufacturing strategies aligned with business requirements, capacity needs, gross margin objectives, and long-term growth.
* Lead and develop a multidisciplinary organization across Production, Materials, Chemical Development, Engineering, QC, Plant Maintenance, Regulatory, and Safety.
* Drive operational excellence through Lean, Six Sigma, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure compliance with applicable quality, environmental, health and safety, chemical process safety, and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with EH&S, Quality, Regulatory, Legal, and other functions to proactively identify and mitigate operational, regulatory, and business continuity risks.
* Develop and execute equipment, infrastructure, automation, and capital investment strategies to improve reliability, capacity, and efficiency.
* Drive cost and productivity improvements across labor, yield, scrap, waste, material usage, manufacturing variances, and inventory.
* Partner with R&D and business teams to enable effective new product introduction, scale-up, industrialization, and technology transfer.
* Lead development of pilot manufacturing capabilities in Suzhou to support new product introduction and greater flexibility across the manufacturing network.
* Develop manufacturing budgets and capital plans and ensure disciplined management of operating expenses and investments.
* Build organizational capability through talent development, succession planning, employee engagement, and development of strong leaders.
* Foster a culture of safety, quality, accountability, continuous improvement, collaboration, and customer focus.

**What You Bring**

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Life Sciences, Biochemistry, or another relevant scientific or technical discipline required; Master’s degree or PhD preferred.
* Work Experience: 12+ years experience leading manufacturing operations in a regulated and technically complex environment, preferably within chemical, life science, diagnostics, pharmaceutical, or related industries.

* Experience working across functions and geographies in a global organization preferred.

This position must be based in
**Richmond, CA**

At Bio-Rad, we’re empowered by our purpose and recognize that our employees are as well. The estimated compensation range for this position is posted. For 70 years, Bio-Rad has focused on advancing the discovery process and transforming the fields of science and healthcare. As one of the top five life science companies, we are a global leader in developing, manufacturing, and marketing a broad range of high-quality research and clinical diagnostic products. We help people everywhere live longer, healthier lives. Bio-Rad offers a unique employee experience with collaborative teams that span the globe. ***Why Valmont***
**We’re Here to Move the World Forward.**
Valmont impacts millions of people around the world every day, yet they might not realize the many ways. Our technology is helping feed the growing population, supplying the world with more reliable energy and access to renewables, enhancing connectivity in remote and urban locations to create a sustainable future and so much more. Simply put, Valmont is advancing agricultural productivity and reimagining vital infrastructure to make life better.
  
  
Join a
*Fortune*
1000 company that respects hard work, honors diversity and invests in our employees as we focus on creating the world of tomorrow, today.
*We are the modern workforce*
. Are you ready to move the world forward? Apply now.
  
  
**A Brief Summary Of This Position**
The Plant Manager is accountable for end-to-end operations of the Elkhart plant and for achieving Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC) objectives. The incumbent provides leadership, direction, planning, and control across manufacturing, materials/purchasing, production scheduling, and shipping to ensure products are produced safely, meet customer and regulatory requirements, and are delivered complete and on time. This role drives continuous improvement and operational excellence, develops and coaches leaders, and manages budgets and cost controls to optimize productivity, quality performance, and overall plant profitability.
  
  
**Essential Functions**

* Ensure that all administrative, supervisory and hourly positions are staffed with the best qualified personnel available.
* Drive team engagement through regular coaching, feedback and involvement in day-to-day operations.
* Foster an environment of open communication.
* Maintain required professional competencies; assess staffing levels and capability; and develop direct reports through training and development opportunities.
* Empower all employees to seek and recommend work methods, tools and procedures to improve safety, quality, delivery and cost functions.
* Develop, coach, and hold leaders and teams accountable through clear expectations, training, and performance management.
* Enforce company policies and procedures in partnership with HR, the Site Controller and operational leadership.
* Lead and sustain a continuous improvement culture across all departments.
* Own site performance to Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC) targets by setting expectations, reviewing results, and driving corrective actions with the Production and Materials team, including:

+ Safety: OSHA recordable incident rate (TRIR) and VSI leading indicators
+ Quality: CoPQ: Internal (scrap and rework) and External (customer defects/complaints)
+ Delivery: SCOT (Ship Complete On Time)
+ Cost: labor and overhead (burden) performance vs. budget/standard
+ Cost: operating profit / plant financial performance
+ Cost/Working Capital: inventory turns and inventory accuracy
+ Cost: manufacturing expense per earned hour / pcs (TME)

* Ensure equipment, processes, and behaviors comply with safety requirements.
* Maintain product quality standards and lead ongoing continuous improvement efforts related to quality.
* Ensure that production and shipment of product meets or exceeds the conformance and delivery expectations of product users and customers.
* Lead cross-functional alignment across sales/marketing, engineering, manufacturing, production control, and off-site operations to achieve SQDC commitments.
* Review daily/weekly SQDC performance and implement countermeasures to protect on-time shipment and cost targets.
* Communicate plant priorities, performance, and changes to hourly and salaried employees.
* Manage inventory to support SCOT while minimizing working capital and obsolescence.
* Oversee preventative maintenance systems in an effort to maintain and protect physical corporate assets.
* Ensure strong systems are in place and functioning to drive asset reliability.
* Lead site-level control activities by communicating expectations and ensuring alignment through a strong partnership with the site Controller.
* Recommend improvements to controls, monitor compliance, and provide accountability to senior management.

**Required Qualifications of Every Candidate (Education, Experience, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities):**

* Preferred Bachelors with 7+ years relevant experience or Associates Degree with 9+ years relevant experience or 11+ years of relevant experience
* Seven or more years of progressive management experience in a manufacturing environment
* Extensive experience with budget and cost management
* Working knowledge of all areas of production from material procurement, transformation, through to shipment
* Experience using MS Office (PowerPoint, Word, Excel, Outlook)
* Ability to travel up to 10%, including overnights

**Highly Qualified Candidates Will Also Possess These Qualifications**

* B.S. in Manufacturing, Business, Technology, or related field is preferred
* Master’s Degree
* Prior experience as a Plant Manager of a manufacturing facility

**Working Environment And Physical Efforts**
Work is typically performed in a manufacturing plant environment and the incumbent needs to be able to move about the office and production environments. There is often exposure to conditions such as dust, dirt, heat, fumes, and cold as well as noise levels above 80 decibels. Many aspects of this role are physical and the incumbent has to be able to lift up to 50 lbs. The employee is regularly required to reach with hands and arms. The incumbent is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, use hands to finger, handle, feel, as well as balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, talk, and hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, and depth perception.
  
  
**Benefits**
Valmont offers employees and their families a comprehensive Total Wellbeing benefit package to ensure their individual and family’s overall wellness needs are met. Some offerings are dependent upon the role, work schedule, or location and can include the following:
  
  

* Healthcare (medical, prescription drugs, dental and vision)
* 401k retirement plan with company match
* Paid time off
* Employer paid life insurance
* Employer paid short-term and long-term disability including maternity leave
* Work Life Support
* Tuition Reimbursement up to $5,250 per year
* Voluntary programs like tobacco cessation, Type 2 diabetes reversal, one-on-one health coaching, mortgage services and more

Valmont does not discriminate against any employee or applicant in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, genetic information, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by law. As Plant Manager, you will be responsible for ensuring the efficient and reliable operation of the facility, while maintaining compliance with all regulatory requirements.

* Identify opportunities for continuous improvement in plant operations, maintenance practices, and environmental performance.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant power industry experience, such as experience as a Power Plant Manager or in a comparable power generation leadership role, in lieu of a degree.

* Comprehensive knowledge of ERCOT market operations and regulatory requirements.
* Demonstrated leadership skills with the ability to manage and motivate a diverse team.
* Excellent problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
* Commitment to safety, environmental stewardship, and operational excellence.

**Job Title**
Sr Manager Manufacturing Operations
  
  
As the Senior Manager, Manufacturing Operations you will be the senior production leader for the Oak Ridge Plant manufacturing execution, responsible for translating site priorities and customer requirements into safe, reliable manufacturing results. You will lead all production operations through a period of significant growth and increasing customer demand, with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, productivity, capacity utilization, and workforce performance.
  
  
As a leader, you will create and drives urgency, clarity, and accountability across the manufacturing organization. You will lead through production managers and supervisors, partners across functions to remove barriers, and represents the plant on customer calls related to production performance, capacity, delivery, and recovery plans. Overall site strategy, P&L ownership, capital allocation, and leadership of non-production functions remain with senior plant/regional leadership.
  
  
**Roles & Responsibilities:**

* Lead production execution across the Oak Ridge manufacturing operation, establishing clear priorities and delivering safety, quality, output, delivery, productivity, and workforce objectives.
* Lead, coach, and develop production managers, supervisors, and frontline teams; set clear expectations, reinforce accountability, and build leadership capability for continued growth.
* Create a visible and engaging leadership presence on the manufacturing floor, connecting employees to customer commitments, business priorities, and daily performance expectations.
* Establish disciplined daily management systems, operating rhythms, performance metrics, and escalation processes that enable teams to identify issues early and respond with urgency.
* Identify and remove constraints across labor, equipment, process flow, materials, maintenance, quality, and manufacturing systems to improve throughput and capacity utilization.
* Partner with Planning, Supply Chain, Engineering, Maintenance, Quality, Human Resources, Finance, and Commercial teams to align resources, resolve barriers, and deliver production commitments.
* Represent the plant on customer calls and internal operating reviews, partnering with Commercial, Planning, Quality, and other teams to communicate production status, risks, recovery actions, and commitments.
* Lead the manufacturing response to customer-impacting issues, ensuring timely containment, clear communication, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and sustainable resolution.
* Use production, labor, maintenance, yield, quality, capacity, and delivery data to identify trends, prioritize actions, and drive measurable improvement.
* Champion Lean, Theory of Constraints, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement to reduce waste and variation, improve flow, and strengthen operational capability.
* Support approved equipment installations, capacity expansions, and manufacturing-readiness activities required to meet current and future demand.
* Ensure production activities comply with safety, environmental, quality, regulatory, and company requirements, reinforcing that safety and quality are never compromised.

**Job Requirements:**
**Education & Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Business, or a related field; equivalent relevant manufacturing leadership experience may be considered.
* At least 7 years of progressive manufacturing or operations experience, including significant responsibility for leading managers, supervisors, or large production teams.
* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing through growth, capacity expansion, operational transformation, or substantial increases in customer demand.
* Proven results improving throughput, delivery, productivity, quality, capacity utilization, and operational stability.
* Experience applying Lean, Theory of Constraints, Six Sigma, or other structured continuous improvement and problem-solving methods.

* Visible, decisive leadership style that creates alignment, urgency, engagement, and accountability.
* Ability to lead through other leaders and strengthen the performance of a multi-layer manufacturing organization.
* Strong understanding of production planning, capacity management, equipment utilization, labor productivity, yield, quality, delivery, and manufacturing cost.
* Ability to influence across functions and resolve complex operational barriers without direct authority over partner teams.
* Executive-level communication skills and the credibility to represent manufacturing with customers, frontline employees, technical teams, and senior leaders.
* Composure and sound judgment during operational pressure, changing priorities, and customer escalations.
* Business acumen to connect manufacturing performance with customer outcomes, revenue delivery, and sustainable growth.
* Learning agility and leadership potential to progress toward broader plant leadership responsibility.

records.description:
Divergent is building the new industrial age. Every day, our teams design, manufacture, and assemble advanced systems for some of the world’s most demanding industries. Our integrated engineering and manufacturing platform transforms complex designs into production-ready solutions, helping customers move faster, build smarter, and deliver critical systems when they matter most. Divergent is a qualified Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and supports leading U.S. aerospace and defense companies.
  
  
Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built.
  
  
Purpose
  
  
We are seeking an exceptional, results-driven
**Senior Manager of Additive Manufacturing Operations**
to lead and scale our Factory 1 production organization. This is a high-impact leadership role responsible for driving world-class execution across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people development while shaping the future of manufacturing.
  
  
The Additive Manufacturing organization leverages proprietary, state-of-the-art systems and processes to execute metal laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), depowdering, manual and automated support removal, surface finishing, heat treatment, and inspection across multiple factory sites supporting both prototype and high-rate production.
  
  
This role is ideal for an ambitious operations leader who thrives in fast-paced, high-growth environments and combines strong manufacturing fundamentals with data-driven decision making, automation, and continuous improvement. Beyond delivering daily operational performance, this leader will develop people, build scalable operating systems, and partner with engineering to industrialize new technologies that will define the next generation of manufacturing.
  
  
The ideal candidate is energized by difficult manufacturing challenges, inspires high-performing teams, and is passionate about building organizations capable of delivering exceptional results.
  
  
The Role
  
  
**Operational Leadership**

* Lead Factory 1 additive manufacturing operations to achieve world-class performance in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and equipment reliability.
* Build, develop, and mentor a high-performing team while fostering a culture of accountability, ownership, urgency, and continuous improvement.
* Drive disciplined daily management through standard work, visual management, structured problem solving, and operational rigor.
* Optimize manufacturing flow by increasing equipment uptime, eliminating bottlenecks, improving process repeatability, and maximizing production throughput.
* Partner closely with Platform Development, Manufacturing Engineering, and Automation teams to successfully launch new equipment, technologies, and manufacturing capabilities.

**Operational Excellence**

* Champion Lean Manufacturing principles and continuous improvement across all additive manufacturing processes.
* Establish scalable operating systems that improve efficiency, stability, and manufacturing readiness as production grows.
* Utilize manufacturing data, KPIs, and analytics to drive operational decisions and prioritize improvement initiatives.
* Develop meaningful performance dashboards and operating rhythms that enable rapid identification and resolution of production issues.
* Lead initiatives to improve Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), first-pass yield, cycle time, labor productivity, and cost per part.

**Equipment Reliability & Technical Capability**

* Continue developing the in-house Additive Manufacturing Service organization by strengthening technical capability, preventive maintenance programs, troubleshooting processes, and technician training.
* Drive reliability initiatives that maximize printer availability, reduce unplanned downtime, and improve long-term equipment performance.
* Partner with technical teams to identify recurring equipment issues and implement sustainable corrective actions.

**Performance Monitoring & Compliance**

* Ensure strict adherence to Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), work instructions, process controls, and quality standards.
* Monitor key operational metrics and hold teams accountable for achieving business objectives.
* Drive disciplined root cause analysis and corrective actions to eliminate recurring manufacturing issues.
* Develop clear, actionable operational reporting that enables data-driven decision making across the organization.

**Safety, Quality & Financial Management**

* Foster a safety-first culture aligned with Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) standards and best practices.
* Partner with EHS to proactively develop and implement safety initiatives that reduce operational risk.
* Ensure manufacturing processes consistently meet internal quality requirements and applicable industry standards.
* Develop, manage, and execute the Factory 1 Additive Manufacturing operating budget while balancing productivity, cost, and long-term capability investments.

**Basic Qualifications**

* Ability to lawfully access information and technology that is subject to US export controls.
* Demonstrated success leading complex manufacturing operations in high-performance production environments.
* Proven ability to build, develop, and lead high-performing technical organizations.
* Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing, operational excellence, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Experience using manufacturing data and operational metrics to drive strategic decision making and measurable business results.
* Proven ability to execute in startup or rapidly scaling manufacturing environments while effectively navigating ambiguity and change.
* Demonstrated success improving operational performance through equipment reliability, process optimization, and organizational development.
* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Weld Engineering, or a related technical discipline (or equivalent practical experience).

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Leadership experience in metal additive manufacturing or other advanced manufacturing environments.
* Experience with Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) production systems.
* Experience with aerospace manufacturing standards, including AS9100 and NADCAP.
* Experience implementing Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Theory of Constraints, or similar operational excellence methodologies.
* Experience leading automation, Industry 4.0, MES, or digital manufacturing initiatives.
* Demonstrated success scaling manufacturing organizations through periods of rapid growth.

Pay Range: $156,640 USD - $215,380 USD

* Wellness and Time Off: Embrace a healthy lifestyle with paid vacation, sick time, and company holidays, including a year-end shutdown to recharge. We support growing families with paid parental leave, recognizing the importance of bonding time.

records.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering
records.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!
  
  
In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by
*TIME*
as a “Best Invention”,
*MIT Technology Review*
as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and
*Fast Company*
as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.
  
  
Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.
  
  
**Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.**
Role Description
  
  
As the Senior Manager of Assembly Manufacturing Engineering, you will serve as the primary architect of the production lifecycle, bridging the gap between research prototypes and high-volume factory operations. You will lead a multidisciplinary team of engineers to develop and internalize robust manufacturing processes for both battery enclosures and module/pack assembly—including robotic joining, sealing, electrolyte filling, and leak testing. By owning the full equipment lifecycle, from defining detailed user requirements through to factory testing and final site commissioning, you ensure that production lines are world-class, delivering a "machine that builds the machine" with precision and technical rigor.
  
  
Strategically, your objective is to drive operational scale by ensuring products are designed specifically for ease of manufacturing and assembly during the earliest development phases. You will champion a data-driven culture that utilizes failure mode analysis and advanced root-cause investigation to reduce production risks and achieve aggressive targets for quality, output rate, and equipment uptime. By fostering collaboration between Product Design, Quality, and Supply Chain, you will manage the critical transition from initial design to full-scale production, ensuring that every process is statistically validated to guarantee long-term reliability and cost-effectiveness.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Lead the development and optimization of battery manufacturing processes for battery assembly manufacturing.
* Ensure highly capable processes are identified and demonstrated for our production facilities ahead of detailed equipment design.
* Oversee the design and implementation of manufacturing processes such as: manual and robotic assembly, joining, sealing, system leak testing, and quality checks to achieve optimal performance and reliability.
* Collaborate with product design team, R&D, quality, and supply chain, to translate product requirements into a battery design and manufacturing process that achieve our company targets.
* Collaborate cross functionally to develop and maintain PFMEA, process specifications, measurement systems GR&R, control plan, and quality inspection methods (incoming, outgoing, and in-process).
* Lead troubleshooting efforts to identify root causes of manufacturing issues and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
* Internalize responsibility for delivery of equipment and processes that enable the operations team to achieve factory production metrics (quality, yield, rate, and availability).
* Identify trends/correlations, and make data-driven decisions for process optimization.

**What You'll Bring**

* Hands-on experience in a high-volume manufacturing organization.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering.
* 10 years of experience in engineering roles within battery manufacturing or a related industry, with expertise in complex assembly processes. 4+ leading technical teams.
* Demonstrated experience in manufacturing equipment procurement, setup, and commissioning, including a clear understanding of equipment qualification and validation protocols.
* Strong understanding of lean manufacturing principles and their application in a high-volume production environment.
* Proven track record of successfully leading cross-functional teams in the development and optimization of manufacturing processes for electrochemical systems.
* Proficiency in process engineering principles, statistical analysis, and quality management systems for process optimization and improvement.
* Strong communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams and convey technical concepts to diverse stakeholders.
* Leadership and mentoring abilities with a commitment to fostering a culture of continuous learning and accelerated innovation through quick iteration.
* Experience working in a fast-paced startup environment is a plus.

*This opportunity is based out of Form Factory 1 – Form Energy’s 550,000-square-foot, state-of-the-art manufacturing facility located in Weirton, WV, a commutable distance from Pittsburgh. Purpose-built for high-volume, advanced battery production, Form Factory 1 is a hub of fast-moving, collaborative work driving a new era of large-scale American energy manufacturing in the heart of the Rust Belt.*
*Relocation assistance is available.*
*Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.*
*When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.*
*To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.*
*If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.*
*Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will
**never**
solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.*

records.description:
**Job Description**
As an S&C Electric team member, you’ll work on projects that have real-world impact. You’ll help transform the grid for resilient and reliable power worldwide. S&C has more than a 100-year history of innovation and has been 100% employee-owned since 2012. We continue this legacy as a trusted, forward-thinking leader in the electrical industry. You will advance a safer, more reliable, and more resilient electrical grid. Our products help the grid adapt to severe weather and transition to clean energy. We’re big enough to be a respected industry leader but small enough for you to impact our company directly. Our commitment gives you opportunities to impact on and off the job positively. Join S&C to make an impact on tomorrow’s energy challenges and become an employee-owner.
  
  
**Hours**

* 8:00 am – 5:00 pm (Mon-Fri) On Site Palatine, IL

**Compensation**
At S&C, we are dedicated to providing competitive and equitable compensation for all our team members, and we are committed to transparency in our pay practices.
**The estimated annual base salary range for this position is $154,968- $205,332.60.**
Individual pay within this salary range is determined by several compensable factors, including performance, knowledge, job-related skills and experience, and relevant education or training. This role is also eligible for S&C’s annual incentive plan (AIP), subject to eligibility criteria.
  
  
**Join Our Team as a Senior Manager – Productions Operations!**
The Senior Manager – Production Operations is responsible for planning, overseeing, and managing the operations and production processes for the department, leading a team of Managers, Assistant Managers, and Supervisors to achieve strategic Objectives and Key Results (OKRs), and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in safety, quality, delivery, and cost (SQDC). The Senior Manager – Production Operations focuses on strategic and tactical operations planning with a mid-term focus, contributing towards greater functional strategies, directing the smooth operations of multiple departments, driving strategic problem-solving and continuous improvement initiatives, reporting out to executive leadership on results, and making strategic adjustments and countermeasures when targets are missed.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Health & Safety Compliance: Drive a safety-first culture, ensuring leaders understand and enforce safety rules. Ensure that health & safety is considered in all departmental plans in order to maintain and promote a safety-conscious manufacturing environment and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards related to production operations.
* Leadership & People Management: Lead, inspire, and develop a high-performing team. Role model appropriate and professional workplace behaviors, address/mediate conflicts to restore harmony, and support a positive, healthy, and inclusive workplace culture in accordance with S&C's mission, vision, values, and guiding principles. Manage departmental administrative team member processes, including but not limited to recruitment, induction, vacation management, performance reviews, performance improvement plans, and workforce/succession planning. Proactively establish, monitor, and hold team members accountable to clear responsibilities and accountabilities; provide ongoing performance feedback, both positive and developmental; address performance gaps in a timely manner; recognize and reward achievements and initiate decisions for corrective actions and terminations where required. Foster a culture that supports the growth and development of team members and proactively train, mentor, and coach team members.
* Strategy Implementation: Cascade strategies to develop mid-term tactical and operational plans for the function, in line with the company’s overall business objectives, including automation, insourcing, and unattended machining. Oversee a leadership team that directs the day-to-day operations of activities within the department and span of control, ensuring the timely and cost-effective delivery of outputs to KPIs. Work with senior leaders to recommend and implement strategic adjustments to operational plans in order to meet OKRs and KPIs.
* Production Planning & Operations: Lead strategic production planning initiatives, collaborating with cross-functional teams to develop a mid-term plan for the department and initiate strategies that contribute to long-term production planning. Work with leaders to optimize production schedules, identify bottlenecks, and determine capacity plans and processing methods. Evaluate machine resources to ensure continued production and minimal downtime. Establish a balance between increased productivity and reduced costs of manufacturing operations. Set mid-term productivity goals and analyze report-outs from Managers.
* Lean Performance Systems: Recommend and implement goals for departmental performance improvement, supporting leaders as they identify and implement process improvements to enhance production efficiency, reduce costs, and increase overall operational effectiveness. Collaborate with other leaders to formulate high-level solutions and develop plans for how to implement improvements throughout multi-faceted functions. Serve as a change agent by influencing, communicating, and institutionalizing a culture of continuous improvement, simplification, standard work, process improvement, and lean principles.
* Quality Management: Oversee the implementation of broad quality control programs, ensuring leaders fully understand quality issues and their corresponding solutions.Discuss and understand high-level, multi-faceted quality issues and help leaders formulate resolutions. Monitor and guide leaders responsible for the department’s communication of corrective action plans, resolutions, and quality results.
* Reporting: Analyzes reports and reviews provided by first-line supervisors. Communicates regularly with upper management regarding problems impacting production. Reports issues regarding production, quality, maintenance, or personnel to senior and executive leadership.
* Budget Management: Develop and manage the function’s budget, ensuring accuracy and appropriate allocation of resources to maximize ROI and the achievement of larger functional strategies and objectives. Approve expenditures for the achievement of operational goals and work with senior leaders to identify investment opportunities for gains towards mid-term goals.
* Compliance: Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
* Maintain regular and punctual attendance.
* Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required.
* Communicate effectively and respectfully with others.
* Drive a car or other vehicle.
* Other responsibilities as assigned.

**Required**
**What you’ll need to succeed:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a technical discipline such as Engineering, or a related field.
* Beliefs in, and alignment with, S&C Guiding Principles and Core Values
* 10+ years of manufacturing experience in an industrial metals fabrication environment, including advanced CNC machining, welding, laser cutting, forming, punching, stamping and related finishing operations.
* 5+ years of supervisory or management experience in a fabrication environment leading hourly and salaried employees.
* Leadership experience in workforce planning, scheduling, and staffing, employee development, coaching, and performance management.Experience managing multiple shifts is preferred.
* Knowledge of precision machining processes and practices within a high mix, low-to-medium volume environment.
* Demonstrated track record of lean manufacturing leadership, sustained improvements, and KPI attainment.
* Great leadership skills within a multi-level manufacturing environment, with an ability to lead, guide, motivate, and delegate to deliver results.
* Sound critical thinking, organizational, planning, and project management skills, and creative problem-solving when obstacles arise.
* Great interpersonal skills to establish meaningful relationships built on mutual trust and respect, navigate and resolve conflict, moderate behaviors, and foster collaborative working relationships amongst a diverse audience.
* Excellent communication skills, (written, verbal, listening, and presentation) ability to liaise with internal and external stakeholders at all levels, from leadership to support staff, and present influentially to achieve buy-in from executives, managers, and team members.
* Sound analytical skills with the ability to use and analyze data to drive informed decisions, problem-solve difficult issues, and leverage data and learnings to drive continuous improvement.
* Proven success partnering across teams, creating effective partnerships at all levels, and collaborating at an operational level.
* Adapts to change and different ways of doing things quickly and positively and finds ways to get things accomplished, even when faced with challenges.
* Proficient computer skills, including Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook) and preferably, Oracle.

**Preferred**

* Master’s degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field.
* Six Sigma Certification(s).
* Certified Lean Six Sigma (CLSS).
* Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE).

S&C Electric is committed to equal-opportunity employment. All employees and applicants will be considered without regard to age, color, disability, gender, national origin, race, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, protected veteran status, or any other classification protected by federal, state, or local law. If you are an individual with a disability and need an accommodation to complete the application, please email us at TAsupport@sandc.com.
  
  
No fixed deadline
  
  
**About Us**
In 1909, S&C Electric Company transformed the delivery of safe, reliable electricity with the invention of the Liquid Power Fuse. Today, as the world faces extreme weather events and the demand for electricity grows, S&C continues to innovate and advance the electrical grid, ensuring reliable and resilient power for homes, communities, and critical infrastructure around the world.
  
  
With a diverse, global workforce and core values around integrity, safety, and quality, S&C is a trusted industry leader and top workplace that offers meaningful careers to more than 3,500 team members. As a people-first organization, S&C is committed to fostering an inclusive and collaborative workplace where team members advance their careers through robust talent-development programs and involved leadership.
  
  
S&C’s deeply rooted belief diversity fosters greater creativity, innovation, and success guides the company to advance and sustain a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace culture.
  
  
**S&C provides a comprehensive and competitive benefit package that includes the following (eligibility requirements apply):**

* Health and Welfare Benefits: Medical & Prescription, Dental, Vision, Health Care and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts, , Health Savings Account (HSA), Group Life Insurance, optional Supplemental Life and AD&D Insurance, Wellbeing Resources including Employee Assistance Program and Family Forming Benefits (i.e., Adoption and Fertility support)
* Leave Benefits: Vacation Time, Sick Time, Paid Holidays and Company Shutdown days, Short-Term Disability, Long-Term Disability, Other Leaves, Paid Parental Time and Military Leave

Retirement Benefits: 401(k) Retirement Savings and Employee Stock Ownership Plan (KSOP) offering traditional and Roth 401(k) options and an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) component; KSOP participants can receive annual ESOP company contributions of over 11% of eligible earnings (3% Core, up to 3.5% Match, Variable Periodic).

**About The Role**
As a Senior Manager, LEU+ Manufacturing Process Engineering, you will lead process engineering. This role is part of the LEU+ Manufacturing Program, a capital expansion of Westinghouse's Columbia Fuel Fabrication Facility. The program aims to manufacture LEU+ (higher-enrichment low-enriched uranium) nuclear fuel. Accountable for the design, qualification and startup of the new manufacturing processes, including uranium conversion, pellet production, fuel rod and assembly manufacturing, uranium recovery and recycling, and the laboratory and maintenance areas. Plan and direct the methods, equipment and processes needed to deliver safe, high-quality, cost-effective fuel, and develops the engineers who deliver them.
  
  
You will report to the Project Director, LEU+ Manufacturing Program and be located at Columbia, SC. You will support this role 100% onsite.

We’re big enough to be a respected industry leader but small enough for you to impact our company directly. Our commitment gives you opportunities to impact on and off the job positively.
  
  
Join S&C to make an impact on tomorrow’s energy challenges and become an employee-owner

**Compensation**
At S&C, we are dedicated to providing competitive and equitable compensation for all our team members, and we are committed to transparency in our pay practices.
