Individual pay within this salary range is determined by several compensable factors, including performance, knowledge, job-related skills and experience, and relevant education or training. This role is also eligible for S&C’s annual incentive plan (AIP), subject to eligibility criteria.
  
  
**Join Our Team as a Senior Manager - Supplier Quality**
!
  
  
The Senior Manager - Supplier Quality is responsible for ensuring that all suppliers meet or exceed the company’s quality standards through strategic audits, risk mitigation, and continuous supplier development. This role emphasizes proactive engagement with suppliers to ensure compliance, minimize risks, and ultimately ensure the quality of supplied components to S&C. The position also oversees the qualification and ongoing evaluation of suppliers to align with the company’s operational and commercial objectives.
  
  
**Essential Functions**

* Supplier Audits & Qualification: Formulate and implement a comprehensive operational strategy to drive continuous quality improvement initiatives within the supplier quality function. Lead a team that conducts comprehensive audits and supplier qualification processes, ensuring compliance with quality standards and the prevention of defective component shipments from the supplier to S&C. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to assess supplier capabilities and align with company requirements.
* COPQ: Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) Reduction: Take ownership of reducing the cost of poor quality (COPQ) by analyzing trends in supplier-reported issues, identifying root causes, and implementing preventative measures to ensure continuous improvement in product quality.
* Production Part Approval Process (PPAP): Oversee the PPAP process to validate supplier-provided components meet specified requirements. Ensure that documentation, testing, and approvals are conducted thoroughly and accurately.
* Risk Analysis and Mitigation: Perform supplier risk analysis by evaluating historical performance, process controls, and financial stability. Develop and execute mitigation strategies to minimize potential supply chain disruptions.
* Corrective Action and Accountability: Lead the resolution of supplier-related quality issues through effective corrective action processes. Establish clear accountability frameworks to ensure sustained improvements and proactive prevention of non-confirming/defective components before receiving them.
* Subject Matter Expertise: Serve as a subject matter expert in Supplier Quality, staying abreast of industry best practices, standards, and technological advancements and ensuring the greater quality function is well-versed in the latest quality methodologies and tools, facilitating a high level of technical proficiency.
* Continuous Improvement: Analyze quality feedback and metrics to identify trends and improvement opportunities. Set team targets for various KPIs and collaborate with production groups to recommend quality targets. Implement a data-driven decision-making process to enhance overall product quality and operational efficiency.
* QA System Support: Manage the meticulous documentation of quality processes, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and internal and external compliance requirements. Provide strategic guidance for regular review and updates, incorporating changes in processes, standards, and best practices to maintain a compliant and dynamic quality management system.
* Functional Leadership: Provide strong leadership and direction to managers and senior contributors, setting clear performance expectations, and fostering a culture of accountability and excellence. Conduct regular performance assessments, provide constructive feedback, and facilitate career development opportunities to support individual growth and organizational succession planning.
* Thought Leadership: Provide thought leadership and best-practice direction to the quality assurance team, ensuring the execution of quality goals that contribute towards the larger goals of S&C.
* Compliance: Understand and comply with all applicable content standards, brand guidelines, company policies, and rules.

**Required**
**Core Leadership & Management**

* 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in Supplier Quality, Quality Engineering, or related manufacturing quality roles.
* 5+ years in leadership or senior management roles overseeing global suppliers and multi-site operations.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical field; advanced degree or Six Sigma Black Belt preferred Preferred
* Experience in a large (2+ billion-dollar revenue) B2B manufacturing company.
* Proven ability to lead and develop a global Supplier Quality Engineering (SQE) team, setting strategic direction, driving accountability, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement.
* Strong executive presence with the capability to influence cross‑functional leaders in engineering, operations, procurement, and manufacturing.
* Demonstrated track record of managing complex supplier ecosystems and driving measurable improvements in quality performance.
* Technical & Quality Expertise
* Deep expertise in advanced quality tools and methodologies, including APQP, PPAP, FMEA, MSA, SPC, 8D, and root-cause/containment fundamentals.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing process controls, capability studies, product validation, and statistical quality management.
* Ability to assess supplier technical capability and process maturity through detailed audits and data-driven evaluation Supplier Management & Performance Improvement
* Experience developing and deploying supplier quality strategies to ensure robust selection, onboarding, and ongoing performance monitoring.
* Proven ability to drive corrective action and continuous improvement using structured problem-solving techniques.
* Hands-on experience establishing supplier scorecards, performance targets, and escalation management processes. Operational Excellence & Risk Management
* Strong capability in managing supplier risk, including process risk assessments, qualification reviews, and proactive risk mitigation planning.
* Demonstrated experience improving cost, quality, and delivery through Lean/Six Sigma methodologies.
* Expertise in quality system requirements such as ISO 9001, IATF 16949, or industry-specific standards Experience & Education

**Education**

* Required
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Operations, Business, or a related field.
* Preferred
* Master’s degree in engineering or a related technical field.

**Certifications & Licenses**

* Preferred
* Six Sigma Black Belt or Green Belt
* Certified Quality Engineer (CQE) / Certified Manager of Quality (CMQ)
* ISO 9001 Lead Auditor

GKN Aerospace is reimagining air travel: going further, faster and greener! Fuelled by great people whose expertise and creativity sets the standards in our industry, we’re inspired by the opportunities to innovate and break boundaries. We’re proud to play a part in protecting the world’s democracies. And we’re committed to putting sustainability at the centre of everything we do, opening up and protecting our planet. With over 16,000 employees across 32 manufacturing sites in 12 countries we serve over 90% of the world’s aircraft and engine manufacturers and achieved sales of £3.6bn in 2025. There are no limits to where you can take your career.
  
  
Role Summary
  
  
As part of GKN Aerospace Airframes E&T, Chief Manufacturing Engineers (CME) lead the development, industrialisation and improvement of Manufacturing Systems whilst serving as the customer-facing representatives of the ME function.
  
  
Day-to-day, a CME is focused on delivery of non-recurring engineering projects including New Product Introductions (NPI), Transfers of Work (ToW), Major Modifications (Mods), Technology Insertions and resolving manufacturing process related quality and delivery challenges together with production engineering teams.
  
  
When necessary, a CME may lead deployed ME resources to deliver these projects, ensuring compliance with identified requirements (e.g. Produceability, Productivity, Cost, Schedule, Regulatory) and adherence to Zero Defect Manufacturing (ZDM) standards.
  
  
**Remote Role**
Travel Requirements
  
  
This is a remote working position that requires frequent routine and occasional non-routine travel (up to 25-50%) to be on-site at GKN facilities and suppliers, including but not limited to; Phoenix (AZ), Wichita (KS), Sumner (WA), Chihuahua (Mexico), Tallassee (AL).
  
  
Candidates must live in a location with strong transport links. This could be 1-2 hours drive (approx.) from a major international hub airport (e.g. Dallas, Atlanta, Houston) or locally to a regional airport with multiple flights per day to major hub airports.
  
  
Role Accountabilities
  
  

* Bids– Accountable to validate and approve the proposed definition of the Manufacturing System and its associated performance targets which are submitted at LG3 (Programme Launch). Working closely with the Industrial Architect, the CME reviews output for technical risks and communicates these to the Programme. This may include process flow, bill of materials, proposed industrial setting, product cost estimates, requirements compliance or technology developments needed. The CME owns the Non-Recurring Engineering cost estimate for the ME technical content delivery.
* NPI– Accountable for delivering a Manufacturing System that fulfils all agreed stakeholder requirements (technical, quality, regulatory), business case metrics and system performance targets between LG3 (Programme Launch) and LG7 (Steady State Production) whilst ensuring that planning, development and commissioning is completed on-schedule and on-cost.
* Sustaining – Accountable for the governance and oversight of a portfolio of Manufacturing Systems, delivered through regular review of system KPIs and Industrial Review assessments. Takes corrective action to ensure Manufacturing Systems continue to perform in-line with the productivity & quality targets set.
* Leadership of Projects- Accountable for delivery of the non-recurring ME activities within a given programme or project. Responsible to provide technical leadership and direction using project management fundamentals: planning & estimating, resourcing & budgeting and reporting on project performance (earned value) to internal business standards.
* Leadership of Teams – Accountable to the Programme and Site for effective utilisation of deployed manufacturing engineering resource while delivering ME content of projects by providing day-to-day coordination, recognition and accountability and implementing ME best practice with the deployed team.
* Quality – Accountable for delivery of manufacturing systems that are Zero Defect Manufacturing (ZDM) capable through a relentless focus on delivering APQP to the AS9145 standard during the NPI phase. Must exhibit and drive a product quality mind-set within ME and ensure compliance to agreed Customer, Regulatory, Business and functional standards.
* Relationships – Accountable to maintain positive and functional working relationships with internal and external customers, to communicate and inform clearly and frequently with key stakeholders within the business, and to foster and champion GKN’s 5 principles within sphere of influence.

**Required**
Role Qualifications
  
  

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional qualification in Engineering (Aerospace, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials, Electrical, Chemical, or related discipline).
* Minimum of 8 years of experience in aerospace manufacturing or similar, highly regulated environments operating under AS9100 Quality Management Systems.
* Recent experience developing a manufacturing system for a New Product Introduction (NPI) with a comprehensive understanding of product lifecycle gate processes.
* Broad, hands-on experience with common manufacturing processes (e.g. machining, forming, welding, composites, assembly, metrology).
* Knowledgeable of structured problem solving and RCCA methodologies (e.g. 8D) and how to apply these to complex problems.
* Demonstrated capability to organise and drive technical projects to achieve business goals, preferably in complex multi-site environments.
* Ability to lead and influence people, build trust and establish effective working relationships within a global organisation and with external customer stakeholders.
* Fluent in English language, both written and spoken.
* US Person for Export Control purposes

**Preferred**

* Demonstrated deployment of AS9145 APQP process.
* Working knowledge of digital systems for manufacturing (PLM, MES, ERP).
* Deep, expert knowledge in one or more manufacturing process areas (e.g. machining, forming, welding, composites, assembly, metrology).
* Experience working with or for major aerospace OEMs and their systems.
* Proven ability to lead change in a Manufacturing System with evidence of delivering significant improvements in terms of cost, quality or throughput.
* Proven ability to identify and deliver industrial productivity improvements and monitor their efficacy by setting appropriate metrics.
* Project / Programme Management Professional Qualification.
* Six Sigma Certification.

Salary Range
  
  
$120-160k
  
  
We’ll offer you fantastic challenges and amazing opportunities. This is your chance to be part of an organisation that has proven itself to be at the cutting edge of our industry; and is committed to pushing the boundaries even further. And with some of the best training on offer in the industry, who knows how far you can go?
  
  
**A Great Place to work needs a Great Way of Working**
Everyone is welcome to apply to GKN. We believe that we can only achieve our ambitions through a coming together of diverse minds who enjoy collaborating in an inspirational environment. Through our commitment to diversity, inclusion and belonging and by living our five powerful principles we’ve created a culture where everyone feels welcome to contribute. It’s a culture that won us ‘The Best Workplace Culture Award’. By embracing and celebrating what makes us unique we encourage everyone to bring their full self to work.
  
  
We’re also committed to providing an accessible recruitment process, so if you require reasonable adjustments at any stage during our recruitment process please get in touch and let us know.
  
  
We are the place where human dreams, plus human endeavour, shape the future of aerospace innovation and technology.

*Simtra BioPharma Solutions (Simtra) is a world-class Contract Development Manufacturing Organization, partnering with pharmaceutical and biotech companies to bring their sterile injectable products to market. With facilities in Bloomington, Indiana, US and Halle/Westfalen, Germany, we offer a wide range of delivery systems including pre-filled syringes, liquid/lyophilized vials, diluents for reconstitution, powder-filled vials and sterile crystallization.*
*Our product types include biologics and small molecules, cytotoxics, highly potent compounds, diluents for reconstitution and vaccines – which are all directly injected into patients worldwide. As such, there is a strong emphasis on quality and continuous improvement at Simtra. We hold ourselves to the highest quality and regulatory standards.*
*While our primary focus is cGMP manufacturing, we offer many support services including formulation and development, lyophilization optimization, global regulatory support and secondary packaging.*
*Our teams are driven to help clients scale, innovate and bring life-changing medicines to patients worldwide.*
**Why join Team Simtra?**
**Because we:**
Make it HAPPEN – We bring a growth mindset to every opportunity, developing new skillsets and exceeding our expectations and those of our customers.
  
  
Make it TOGETHER – We work as one, respecting each voice and tapping into our unique strengths across teams—so we can solve problems in new ways.
  
  
Make it RIGHT – We hold ourselves to a high standard of excellence, fulfilling our commitments to the customer, their patients, and our team members.
  
  
Make it COUNT – We take pride in our day-to-day work, knowing the impact we make – taking on challenges big and small to improve patient health.
  
  
**This role:**
Simtra Biopharma Solutions is seeking a dynamic and experienced Director of Operational Excellence (OpEx) to lead performance improvement initiatives across the Bloomington site partnering with manufacturing, quality, and supporting departments. This role is pivotal in driving operational discipline, lean execution, and data-informed performance management to ensure consistent, high-quality production and timely delivery of life-saving pharmaceutical products. The Director, OpEx is a member of the site senior leadership team, and reports to the Site Head.
  
  
**The responsibilities:**
**Leadership And Strategy**

* Work with at-site, above-site, and cross-site leadership to develop the Simtra Production System based on Lean Six Sigma principles
* Champion Simtra Production System principles across the site to power stable, predictable, high-quality operations and instill a culture of continuous lean improvement
* Develop and execute annual OpEx objectives, kaizens, and projects and track and deliver impact based on measured KPIs
* Lead and mentor a team of OpEx professionals, fostering a culture of accountability and high performance

**Process Improvement And Lean Execution**

* Proactively identify opportunities to streamline manufacturing, quality, and other processes, reduce lead times, and enhance overall efficiency, increase capacity, or reduce costs.
* Oversee the execution of continuous improvement initiatives and Kaizens, ensuring alignment with client and regulatory requirements and quality standards
* Ensure that the OpEx team has a strong presence on the shop floor to both understand the ground truth on the floor and drive initiatives on the front line, helping to coach operators and supervisors on the Simtra Production System

Performance Management and Reporting & Analytics
  
  

* Work with digital teams to develop and maintain performance dashboards and executive scorecards tailored to business and operational needs
* Build, maintain, and roll out management infrastructure best practices such as tier meetings, visual management, and leader standard work across the site
* Develop and present reports on operational performance, key improvement initiatives, and strategic projects for senior management and clients
* Analyze real-time operational data to identify trends, deviations, and improvement opportunities
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to design and implement corrective actions based on data insights
* Ensure alignment of operational activities with strategic KPIs, including:

+ Right First Time (RFT)
+ On-Time Delivery (OTD)

**Required qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Operations management or related field
* 10+ years of experience in pharmaceutical or similarly regulated manufacturing operations with 5+ years of experience in a people leadership role, with a strong track record in operational excellence and performance improvement
* Proven experience in leading cross-functional teams and driving change in high-complexity environments
* Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills
* Proficiency in Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, Powerpoint, Outlook) and the ability to use enterprise and AI software (e.g., D365, SAP, TrackWise, ServiceNow, Veeva, Claude, ChatGPT)

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master’s Degree equivalent or higher
* Strong knowledge of sterile manufacturing processes and regulatory requirements (FDA, cGMP, etc.)
* Experience with software such as Quality Management Systems, ERPs, OT
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt
* Strong analytical skills with proficiency in data visualization and performance reporting tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau, Excel)
* Project Management Professional (PMP)

**Physical / safety requirements:**

* Duties may require overtime work, including nights and weekends
* Use of hands and fingers to manipulate office equipment is required

The Director, Operational Excellence provides strategic leadership and oversight for the Operational Excellence program. Directs the development and implementation of division-wide process improvement strategies, methodologies, governance frameworks, and performance measures that enhance operational effectiveness and service delivery. Leads a centralized Operational Excellence function while providing strategic guidance and oversight to embedded Operational Excellence resources across multiple divisions. records.description:
Global Director, Operational Excellence COE
  
  
At Nouryon, our global team takes positive action every day, to reach higher collectively and individually. We create innovative and sustainable solutions for our customers to answer society’s needs – today and in the future.
  
  
We are looking for team members who bring ideas forward, champion others and work together to do better. Does that sound like you?
  
  
**About the job**
The Global Director, Operational Excellence (OpEx) COE is a senior leadership role responsible for defining the strategic direction, standards, and governance of Nouryon’s global OpEx program. This role owns the organizational design, frameworks, methodologies, and capability pipelines that enable sustainable continuous improvement across 63 manufacturing sites in the Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) organization – spanning the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific.
  
  
This role is the architect of OpEx productivity engine. The COE Director owns the design of the systems, standards, and organizational capabilities that enable VMC and FMC delivery – including ownership of the enterprise systems of record for productivity tracking (ANT) and performance reporting (PowerBI). Execution of productivity targets is driven through the regional OpEx Manager network; this role ensures those teams are equipped, aligned, and operating within a governance structure capable of sustaining results.
  
  
This role leads a newly consolidated Center of Excellence that brings together CI methodology and Lean/Six Sigma certification, ISC Learning & Development, End-to-End Process Management, and Manufacturing Excellence under a single governance structure. The COE Director sets priorities, establishes the program architecture, and holds accountability for outcomes – operating through a team of direct reports who own execution across regions. Key relationships span the COO, regional OpEx Managers, Site Directors, and ISC functional leaders across three regions.
  
  
This is a permanent, full-time position reporting to the VP, Global Operational Excellence & Digital Manufacturing, based in a Nouryon regional hub (Amsterdam, Houston, or Shanghai) with global travel of 15–25%.
  
  
**In your future role as the Global Director, Operational Excellence COE, you will**
**CI Methodology, Standards & Governance**

* Own the global Operational Excellence methodology, ensuring a consistent, fit-for-purpose CI framework is deployed across all 63 Nouryon manufacturing sites.

* Define and govern the Lean/Six Sigma certification pathway from Yellow Belt through Master Black Belt, establishing quality standards for program content, assessment, and progression.
* Partner with regional OpEx Managers to translate global standards into site-level execution plans, maintaining strategic alignment while enabling regional adaptation.
* Establish and sustain a durable CI Governance model – defining the review cadence, accountability structure, and performance mechanisms that ensure CI maturity compounds over time across the Nouryon network.
* Own the enterprise systems of record for productivity tracking and performance reporting, including the ANT productivity platform and PowerBI reporting architecture, ensuring data integrity and leadership visibility across all sites.

**ISC Learning & Development**

* Lead the design and continuous improvement of the ISC Learning & Development program, spanning CI capability, technical skills, and leadership development for the ISC organization.
* Direct the L&D team to build and maintain a structured curriculum that supports onboarding, role progression, and organizational capability uplift.
* Connect L&D investment directly to VMC and FMC delivery targets, ensuring program outcomes are measurable and business-relevant.
* Own the design mandate for Digital Literacy and AI capability across the ISC organization – defining the people, process, and metrics framework required to build and sustain enterprise AI competency at scale. This includes establishing program objectives, identifying ownership, and proposing a deployment model aligned to Nouryon’s broader digital strategy.

**End-to-End Process Management**

**Brief Description**
**About Us**
At
**FreshDirect**
, we are reinventing the grocery experience.
  
  
Since day one, our mission has been simple: bring the best, freshest food directly from the farm to people’s homes — faster, fresher, and smarter than anyone else.

We partner directly with farmers, fishermen, and artisans to source the highest quality ingredients — then use smart data, automation, and logistics to deliver them at peak freshness.
  
  
It’s grocery shopping reimagined — and we’re just getting started.
  
  
If you’re passionate about innovation, care deeply about what people eat, and want to help build the future of food, we’d love to meet you.

The Senior Director of Operations & Transformation is responsible for driving operational excellence, strategic initiatives, and enterprise-wide transformation efforts across the organization. records.description:
**About Monster Energy:**
-------------------------

Forget about blending in. That's not our style. We're the risk-takers, the trailblazers, the game-changers. We're not perfect, and we don't pretend to be. We're raw, unfiltered, and a bit unconventional. But our drive is unrivaled, just like our athletes. The power is in your hands to define what success looks like and where you want to take your career. It's not just about what we do, but about who we become along the way. We are much more than a brand here. We are a way of life, a mindset. Join us.

**A day in the life:**
----------------------

As the Director, SAP Supply Chain Planning & Manufacturing Systems, you will own the design, implementation, and optimization of Monster's end-to-end supply chain planning landscape within the SAP ecosystem. Your primary focus is SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP) covering demand planning, supply planning, S&OP, inventory optimization, order based planning and the roadmap of S/4HANA.

You will also guide the connected Manufacturing and Quality solutions, including SAP PP, PP/DS, production execution, and SAP QM, so that planning decisions flow cleanly into the plant floor and quality processes. You will set global processes, solution architecture, and governance; lead a team of SAP IT professionals; and partner with Supply Chain, Operations, and Quality leaders to drive continuous improvement and innovation.

**The impact you'll make:**
---------------------------

***Supply Chain Planning (primary focus)***

* Own the global SAP planning solution, with SAP IBP and SAP APO (DP, SNP, PP/DS) as the core platforms, and define the target architecture and roadmap, including to S/4HANA.
* Lead solution design and configuration decisions across demand planning, supply planning, S&OP, inventory optimization, and response/deployment planning.
* Lead planning projects from inception to completion, including implementations, upgrades, enhancements, and migrations, delivered on time, in scope, and on budget.
* Establish planning master data standards, parameter governance, and integration between IBP/APO, S/4HANA, and connected systems (e.g., RTI, CPI).
* Serve as the point of contact on emerging trends in supply chain planning and evaluate solutions that improve forecast accuracy, service levels, and inventory performance.

***Manufacturing & Quality (supporting scope)***

* Oversee SAP production execution solutions so that plans translate into executable production schedules across plants and co-manufacturers.
* Guide SAP QM processes, including inspection planning, batch management, quality notifications, and release, in partnership with Quality and Regulatory teams.
* Ensure end-to-end integration across Planning, Manufacturing, and Quality so the business runs on one consistent process.

***Leadership & strategy***

* Analyze business requirements, prioritize based on cost/benefit, and present a clear implementation roadmap to IT and business leadership.
* Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing global team of SAP specialists and manage system integrator and partner relationships.
* Partner closely with end-to-end solution verticals to understand requirements, manage business risk, and deliver quality outcomes on budget and timeline.
* Engage operations leaders to identify problems suited to AI, automation, and advanced analytics, in line with the Digital Transformation (DT) roadmap and vision.

**Who you are:**
----------------

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Information Technology, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.
* 10+ years of SAP supply chain experience working on the IT side, including hands-on process mapping, solution design, configuration, and customization.
* **7+ years of hands-on SAP IBP and/or SAP APO experience**, including at least one full-lifecycle implementation you led or owned. APO-to-IBP migration experience strongly preferred.
* Working experience with SAP PP, and production execution, and exposure to SAP QM. Depth here is valued but secondary to Planning.
* Experience with SAP S/4HANA and SAP SCM implementations as part of an IT team.
* Proven track record making solution design and roadmap decisions and leading SAP teams and system integrators.
* Experience aligning teams to a common business process and driving application adoption.

***Preferred***

* Certifications: SAP IBP, APICS (CPIM/CSCP), SAP Manufacturing, or SAP Quality.
* Experience in consumer packaged goods, beverage, or other high-volume manufacturing environments.
* Background with automation and analytics tools and platforms (e.g., RPA, workflow automation, process mining, AI/ML forecasting).
* Technical skills: SAP IBP, SAP APO (DP, SNP, PP/DS), S/4HANA, SAP PP, SAP QM, SAP Analytics Cloud, and Microsoft tools.

records.description:
**WHO WE ARE**  
At Ghirardelli, we honor tradition and drive innovation, aiming to be the top choice for premium chocolate. Our commitment to *Making Life A Bite Better* inspires both our products and the way we do business. We support personal and professional growth, recognizing that each employee’s contribution directly impacts Ghirardelli’s growth and success. Join our dynamic team and help shape Ghirardelli's future.

**Job Summary**

The Head of Production is accountable for safe, compliant, reliable, and cost-effective production across all three shifts of the factory. This role leads the production organization, establishes consistent operating standards and management routines across shifts, and ensures delivery of safety, food safety, quality, service, cost, productivity, waste, and people objectives.

The Head of Production translates factory strategy into clear production priorities, develops leadership capability throughout the production organization, creates the accountability required for sustained execution and deliver on key organizational metrics. The role partners and collaborates cross-functionally to resolve systemic losses, strengthen operating discipline, improve asset and labor performance, and embed TPM and continuous improvement practices into daily operations.

  
  

* Establish and sustain a culture of Safety and Food Safety, shifting the mindset to one of immediate intervention, learning, correction, and prevention of unsafe behaviors or conditions.
* Ensure production leaders visibly demonstrate safety and food-safety leadership on every shift
* Ensure timely containment, investigation, corrective action, and verification following significant incidents or deviations
* Partner with Safety and Quality to ensure standards are understood, implemented, audited, and sustained
* Ensure production readiness for internal, customer, and regulatory audits
* Lead, coach, and develop the production team to ensure clear expectations, accountability, and effective succession plans
* Establish consistent leadership expectations and operating discipline across all three shifts
* Ensure recognition, coaching, corrective action, and performance management are applied consistently across shifts
* Create an environment where standards are understood, leaders address deviations promptly, and follow-through is visible
* Identify systemic losses and ensure effective corrective and preventive actions are implemented
* Sponsor cross-functional improvement teams addressing systemic production losses
* Lead the AM pillar implementation into the culture and mindset of the factory
* Verify that corrective actions address root causes and prevent recurrence across applicable shifts and production areas
* Drive recovery plans when production performance deviates from plan
* Manage production spending, labor, overtime, material variances, and productivity commitments
* Ensure production capacity, labor capability, and operating constraints are represented in annual and long-term planning
* Partner with Maintenance and Reliability to align production plans, preventive maintenance, equipment access, shutdown execution, and chronic-loss elimination
* Partner with Planning and Warehouse to align production schedules, material availability, inventory requirements, and service priorities
* Partner with Quality to manage holds, deviations, and release priorities
* Partner with Engineering on design reviews, commissioning, qualifications, start-up, stabilization, and operational handoff of capital projects
* Partner with Training on workforce planning, leadership capability, and capability development plans
* Partner with HR and factory leadership on labor relations, grievance resolution, contract administration, negotiations, mediation, and arbitration, as required.
* Hire, develop and manage performance of team. Create an inclusive environment that embraces our values and purpose.
* Ensure reconciliation of production workorders and partner with finance function to reconcile and resolve any losses
* Partner with IP team for execution of projects to systematically reduce waste across processing and packaging streams
* Enable a proactive, positive, collaborative and engaged culture across all levels of the production organization
* Complete special projects and other duties as assigned or as necessary.
  

  

Minimum Education and Experience

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations management, food science, supply chain, business, or a related field
* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience in a complex, multi-shift operation
* Experience leading managers and an organization with multiple levels of leadership
* Demonstrated accountability for safety, quality, service, cost, productivity and people results
* Experience in food, beverage, consumer packaged goods, or another regulated manufacturing environment
* Working knowledge of food-safety systems, manufacturing quality systems, and applicable regulatory requirements
* Experience applying Lean, TPM, or another structured continuous-improvement system
* Experience with labor planning, operating budgets, and performance management
* Ability to lead effectively in a union-represented environment
  

  

Other Job Requirements

* Regular presence in manufacturing and production areas is required
* Flexibility to work across all three shifts to provide leadership visibility, conduct reviews, coach leaders, and respond to operational needs.
* Availability outside of normal business hours for significant safety, food safety, quality, people, equipment, or service events
* Ability to operate in manufacturing environments involving noise, heat, cold, moving equipment, stairs, elevated areas, and required PPE
* Limited travel may be required for business meetings, training, supplier visits, benchmarking, or project support

records.description:
**At ACI we build our company and our culture not by counting people, but by making our people count!**

Atlantic Constructors is seeking dynamic, motivated, career minded individuals to join our expanding team! Atlantic Constructors has been recognized as an industry leader in the Mid-Atlantic Region for over 50 years.

**Benefits:**

* ***$0.00 COST FOR MEDICAL, DENTAL, SHORT TERM DISABILITYLIFE INSURANCE (EMPLOYEE ONLY) COVERAGE!***
* Dental Insurance Plan
* Vision Insurance Plan
* 401(K) Retirement Plan with Generous Company Matching
* Health Savings Plan with Generous Company Matching
* Wellness Programs

Atlantic Constructors offers competitive benefits, for more information check out our comprehensive list on our website. ACIBuilds.com

**Role Overview:**
==================

The Director of Offsite Production is responsible for the leadership, performance, and continued growth of offsite production across company facilities. The role oversees carbon and stainless steel pipe fabrication and non-volumetric prefabrication and manufacturing, including pipe racks, equipment skids, supports, frames, and multi-trade assemblies. The Director establishes the operating systems, production standards, capacity, and cross-functional coordination required to deliver safe, compliant, high-quality work on schedule.

This leader is accountable for implementing improvements that increase production capacity, labor productivity, throughput, and schedule reliability. The Director will implement and sustain Lean manufacturing methodologies, eliminate waste and production constraints, reduce rework, and create repeatable processes that support scalable offsite manufacturing. The position works closely with Estimating, Engineering, VDC, Procurement, Project Management, Quality, Safety, and field operations to align production with project and business objectives.

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

**Offsite Production Leadership**
---------------------------------

* Provide enterprise leadership for pipe fabrication, prefabrication, and manufacturing operations across company facilities and approved external production partners.
* Translate backlog, project schedules, and sales forecasts into capacity plans, staffing requirements, production priorities, and facility needs.
* Establish a consistent operating cadence for production planning, readiness reviews, constraint management, performance reporting, and executive escalation.
* Develop scalable operating standards that support growth while maintaining safety, quality, cost control, and predictable delivery performance.
* Coordinate work across facilities to balance demand, available labor, equipment, and production capability.

**Pipe Fabrication Operations**
-------------------------------

* Direct carbon and stainless steel pipe fabrication operations, including material receiving, cutting, beveling, fit-up, welding, inspection, testing, coating coordination, staging, and shipment.
* Ensure spool sequencing, production release, shop loading, and work packaging align with approved drawings, project priorities, and field installation requirements.
* Maintain compliance with applicable codes, specifications, welding procedures, ASME and AWS requirements, customer quality plans, and company standards.
* Improve material traceability, weld documentation, inspection records, testing status, and turnover packages for fabricated systems.

**Prefabrication and Manufacturing Operations**
-----------------------------------------------

* Lead production of non-volumetric prefabricated assemblies, including pipe racks, equipment skids, structural supports, frames, and multi-trade assemblies.
* Develop repeatable production cells, workstations, tooling, fixtures, travelers, and assembly sequences that improve flow and reduce variation.
* Ensure manufacturing plans account for structural, mechanical, electrical, controls, insulation, coatings, testing, preservation, packaging, and logistics requirements, as applicable.
* Support the transition of first-of-a-kind work into stable, repeatable production through lessons learned, standardized design, and controlled process updates.

**Production Planning and Readiness**
-------------------------------------

* Establish production-readiness criteria to confirm approved drawings, bills of material, work instructions, quality requirements, tooling, materials, and labor are available before work is released.
* Partner with Engineering and VDC to improve constructability, spool and assembly breakdown, drawing release sequencing, and design for manufacturing and assembly.
* Coordinate with Procurement and material-control teams to maintain visibility to shortages, supplier commitments, receiving status, kitting, and point-of-use material availability.
* Identify production constraints early, assign recovery actions, and communicate schedule or capacity risks to Project Management and executive leadership.
* Maintain production schedules that clearly identify priorities, dependencies, resource loading, planned output, and required shipment dates.

**Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement**
-------------------------------------------------

* Lead continuous-improvement initiatives that increase production capacity, labor productivity, throughput, and schedule reliability across all offsite operations.
* Implement and sustain Lean manufacturing methodologies, including 5S, standard work, value-stream mapping, visual management, cellular production, daily tiered accountability, Kaizen events, mistake-proofing, and continuous-flow principles.
* Evaluate workflows, facility layouts, material movement, staffing, tooling, and equipment utilization to identify and eliminate bottlenecks, waste, waiting, excess handling, rework, and other non-value-added activity.
* Use time studies, cycle-time analysis, workload balancing, root-cause analysis, and structured problem-solving to improve production performance and reduce manufacturing lead time.
* Develop and maintain standard work instructions and repeatable manufacturing processes that improve safety, quality, training effectiveness, and output predictability.
* Lead initiatives to reduce setup and changeover time, control work in process, improve material flow, and increase productive labor utilization.
* Maintain an improvement pipeline with defined owners, target benefits, implementation dates, and verified results; ensure completed improvements are standardized and sustained.
* Evaluate and implement automation, machinery, software, tooling, and manufacturing technologies that improve safety, quality, efficiency, and capacity.

**Throughput Capacity and Performance Management**
--------------------------------------------------

* Establish production targets and capacity models based on takt time, cycle time, labor availability, equipment constraints, facility limits, and project demand.
* Track and improve key performance indicators such as safety performance, labor hours per spool or assembly, plan attainment, throughput, work in process, first-pass yield, rework, equipment utilization, and on-time completion and shipment.
* Develop visual dashboards and tiered performance reviews that provide timely, accurate information to supervisors, project teams, and executive leadership.
* Analyze performance gaps, determine root causes, implement corrective and preventive actions, and verify that results are sustained.

Every Zoox vehicle depends on the electronic and sensor hardware our Advanced Hardware Manufacturing team builds and tests. As Director, you will lead the organization that takes this hardware from early builds to serial volume, helping bring safer, cleaner mobility to cities.

Our team values safety first, ownership, and learning together. We solve problems in the open and improve how we work every day. You will be part of the Manufacturing Operations leadership team, reporting to the Vice President of Manufacturing Operations. You will partner closely with Hardware Engineering, Test Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Logistics, Environmental Health and Safety (EHS), and Program Management. This role offers room to grow as our production footprint and team expand.

### **In this role, you will:**

* Lead daily operations of advanced hardware assembly and test lines across multiple shifts, delivering on safety, quality, delivery, and cost, and build a culture that puts people and product safety first.
* Turn the vehicle demand plan into production and capacity plans covering labor, equipment, shifts, and yield, and lead expansion into new lines and areas with Equipment Engineering and Facilities.
* Improve first pass yield and process capability through standardized processes, and partner cross-functionally on root cause analysis and corrective actions.
* Manage the Advanced Hardware Laboratories to support R&D across the sensors and compute domains. Lead the build, testing, and pilot production of early-stage prototypes, maturing technical solutions for seamless transition to high-volume manufacturing.
* Bring new products and design changes from pilot builds to volume production with Hardware and Test Engineering, giving design-for-manufacturing input early.
* Apply lean methods and structured problem solving, and run a data-driven operating rhythm on delivery, cycle time, yield, utilization, and unit cost.
* Own operating, capital, and headcount budgets, and deliver cost reduction roadmaps.
* Hire, develop, and retain managers, supervisors, line leads, and technicians, with succession and training plans that support multi-shift operations.

### **Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Management, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* At least 15 years in manufacturing operations for complex electronic or sensor hardware, including at least 8 years leading multi-level production organizations and presenting to executive leadership.
* Experience taking hardware products from new product introduction through ramp to serial production.
* Results improving safety, quality, delivery, and cost through lean manufacturing and structured problem solving.
* Experience owning operating, capital, and headcount budgets, including investments in production lines or facilities.

### **Bonus Qualifications**

* Experience standing up new production lines or facilities in a high-growth environment.
* Experience with electronics assembly and automated test, including ESD control and end-of-line test.

records.description:
**About Tutor**
---------------

We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.

Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

**The Role**
------------

As Head of Technical Operations, you’ll own manufacturing, supply chain, quality, field service and robot operations. We build hundreds of robots a year today and need to build a lot more. You’ll own how we get there, including the teams, suppliers and facilities, and work closely with engineering along the way.

You’ll report to the CTO. This is an onsite role in Watertown, MA.

**What You'll Own**
-------------------

* Scaling production from hundreds of robots a year to many more
* Manufacturing, supply chain, quality, field service and robot operations
* The teams, suppliers and facilities behind production
* A close partnership with engineering

**Requirements**
----------------

* Ran manufacturing or operations at a company that builds complex hardware in volume
* Built an operations function and hired the people who run it
* Been responsible for a fleet of products in the field, including service and support
* Sets clear targets and hires well
* Comfortable on a factory floor

**Nice to have:**

* Robotics, or other products that combine hardware and software
* Experience with contract manufacturers
* Experience with quality systems

**What to Expect**
------------------

We want you to know exactly what to expect. Here’s what our interview process typically looks like:

* **Recruiter interview:** A conversation with a member of our Recruiting team about your background and what you’re looking for.
* **Hiring manager interview:** A deeper conversation with the hiring manager about the role and your experience.
* **Onsite:** A presentation with the team, 1:1s with key team members, and a tour of our facility.

Some roles include additional steps, such as a technical assessment or take-home exercise. If yours does, we’ll let you know up front. Throughout the process, we’ll aim to keep you updated at each step as quickly as possible.

**Why Tutor?**
--------------

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

**Benefits**
------------

We take care of our team so they can do their best work. At Tutor, you’ll get:

* Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium.
* A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.
* Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
* Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

Compensation Range: $250K - $350K

Director of Operations, North America

**About Us:**

We are committed to finding smart solutions that enable an intelligent and seamless world. Our success as a world-class leader in technology has evolved from humble beginnings. In 1896, the enterprising father and son team of A.J. and George A. Briggs partnered with S.A. Buffington, a Chicago lawyer, to establish Chicago Telephone Supply Company (later to become CTS).

Today, CTS is a leading designer and manufacturer of sensors, actuators, and electronic components for suppliers and original equipment manufacturers. We have over 20 locations in 12 countries and more than 3,500 employees. Our innovative sensing, connectivity, and motion solutions offer a diverse range of products across diversified end markets including transportation, medical, aerospace and defense, and industrial. We are at the forefront of supporting innovating life-changing technology, focusing on quality to keep people safe, healthy, and happy.

**Position Summary**

The Operations Director, North America provides strategic and operational leadership for the regional manufacturing network, ensuring safe, compliant, cost-effective, and customer-focused execution across assigned sites. This position requires a hands-on, execution-focused leader who can standardize operating processes, improve performance variability across sites, coach plant leadership teams, and convert strategic business priorities into measurable operational and financial results. records.title: Director, MSAT/External Manufacturing Management
records.description:
OPPORTUNITY

Mammoth Biosciences is seeking a Director, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) to lead the scale-up of our lipid nanoparticle (LNP) drug product process from Phase 1 into Phase 2 and toward late stage readiness. This leader will own the technical path from the current clinical process to a well-characterized, scalable process that is ready for process performance qualification (PPQ).

All manufacturing and analytical work is performed at external contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) and contract testing labs. The Director will be Mammoth's technical owner of the process at those partners, ensuring that development, technology transfer, process characterization and PPQ are executed in line with current regulatory guidance and industry best practice.

This is a build role. Initially the Director will deliver through external resources (CDMOs, consultants and contract staff), then grow an internal MSAT team in stages as program milestones are met. The role reports to the Head of CMC and works closely with Process Development, Analytical Development, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Supply Chain and Program Management.

### **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Process scale-up and technology transfer

* Lead scale-up of the Phase 1 LNP process (nucleic acid payload formulation, mixing, buffer exchange/TFF, sterile filtration and fill) to Phase 2 and late-stage clinical scale
* Define the scale-up strategy, including equipment selection, mixing platform scalability, scale-down model development and comparability between process versions
* Plan and execute technology transfers of processes and methods between Mammoth, development partners and GMP CDMOs, including transfer protocols, gap assessments and engineering runs
* Own the technical risk assessments (e.g., FMEA) that drive scale-up and characterization priorities

Process characterization and PPQ readiness

* Build the control strategy using a QbD approach: define CQAs and CPPs, link material attributes to product quality, and set proven acceptable ranges
* Design and oversee process characterization studies (DoE, qualified scale-down models, hold times, mixing and filtration studies) that support the control strategy and regulatory filings
* Lead PPQ planning and execution: validation master plan inputs, PPQ protocols and reports, acceptance criteria, sampling plans and the transition to continued process verification
* Partner with Analytical Development to make sure methods are phase-appropriate, validated on time and fit to support characterization and PPQ

External manufacturing and CDMO management

* Serve as Mammoth's technical lead and person-in-plant at CDMOs and contract labs for development, engineering and GMP campaigns
* Lead selection, qualification and oversight of CDMO partners for drug product manufacturing, fill-finish operations and drug product testing, including technical due diligence, capacity and capability assessment, and scale-up fit
* Provide technical oversight for engineering and GMP runs at external partners
* Develop scalable, phase-appropriate aseptic drug product processes at CDMOs, including fill-finish operations, cryogenic handling (as applicable) and cold-chain compatibility
* Assess and implement suitable container-closure systems (vials, syringes) that meet regulatory and operational requirements
* Accountable for review and approval of batch records in accordance with regulatory guidelines; review campaign plans, deviations, investigations, CAPAs and change controls in partnership with Quality
* Manage partner timelines, budgets, deliverables and quality in collaboration with internal stakeholders; drive technical decisions and escalate issues early
* Project manage external stakeholders and high-profile partner meetings (up to 10% of time)
* Contribute to technical sections of quality agreements, statements of work and budgets

Regulatory and cross-functional support

* Author and review CMC sections for IND/IMPD/CTA amendments, end-of-Phase 2 and later filings (Module 3 process description, process development history, process validation)
* Support regulatory interactions and inspections with process knowledge and data
* Provide manufacturing input to program plans, timelines and supply forecasts

Team and resource leadership

* In the early phase, deliver through external resources: CDMO technical teams, consultants and contract MSAT staff
* Build the internal MSAT function in stages tied to milestones, including hiring plans, roles and the balance of internal and outsourced work
* Set up MSAT systems and practices: tech transfer templates, process knowledge management, data trending and lifecycle documentation

### **REEQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* PhD in chemical engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry or a related field with 10+ years of industry experience, or MS with 14+ or BS with 16+ years of experience
* 6+ years in MSAT, process development or technical operations for parenteral drug products, including at least 3 years in a leadership role
* Hands-on experience scaling up LNP or comparable complex parenteral processes (liposomes, nanoparticles, nucleic acid formulations) from early clinical to late-stage scale
* Led at least one process characterization and PPQ campaign through completion, with working command of ICH Q8–Q12 and FDA/EMA process validation expectations
* Extensive experience managing CDMOs and contract labs as the sponsor's technical lead, including tech transfer, person-in-plant oversight, deviations and change control
* Experience with fill-finish operations, aseptic processing and external manufacturing oversight
* Strong working knowledge of cryogenic storage and cold-chain management for LNP drug products
* Track record of authoring CMC regulatory sections and supporting agency interactions
* Ability to influence and direct external partners without line authority, and to make sound technical calls under timeline pressure
* Ability for frequent domestic and international travel to CDMO and contract lab sites, estimated at up to [30–40]% and peaking during engineering, characterization and PPQ campaigns
* Must be able to travel internationally on short notice and hold, or be able to obtain, a valid passport and any visas needed for partner sites
* Ability to commit to extended on-site presence at CDMOs (person-in-plant) during critical campaigns, sometimes across time zones.
* Based in the San Francisco Bay Area preferred, with ability to work onsite at our Brisbane, CA location; hybrid or remote arrangements are available
* Ability to work Pacific Time Zone hours if not located on the West Coast
* Ability to travel to Mammoth’s Brisbane, CA HQ regularly if not local

### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Direct experience with mRNA/LNP or gene editing drug products
* Experience with impingement jet or microfluidic mixing scale-up, TFF and sterile filtration of LNPs
* Experience with commercial process validation and BLA/MAA preparation
* Experience building a function or team from the ground up in a small or mid-size biotech
* Working knowledge of statistical tools for DoE and process data analysis (e.g., JMP, Minitab)

### **BENEFITS**

* Company-paid health/vision/dental benefits
* Unlimited vacation and generous sick time
* Company-sponsored meals and snacks
* Wellness, caregiver and ergonomics benefits
* 401(k) with company matching

Actual base salary will be determined by relevant professional experience, applicable skills, and internal equity

**COMPANY**

Mammoth Biosciences is a biotechnology company focused on leveraging its proprietary ultracompact CRISPR systems to develop long-term curative therapies, as well as other applications such as decentralized precision diagnostics. Founded by CRISPR pioneer and Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna and Trevor Martin, Janice Chen, and Lucas Harrington, the company’s ultracompact proteins are designed to enable *in vivo* gene editing in difficult to reach tissues utilizing both nuclease applications and new editing modalities beyond double stranded breaks, including base editing, gene writing, and epigenetic editing. The company is building out its pipeline of potential *in vivo* gene editing therapeutics and capabilities and has partnerships with leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies to broaden the reach of its innovative and proprietary technology. Mammoth’s deep science and industry experience, along with a robust and differentiated intellectual property portfolio, have enabled the company to further its mission to transform the lives of patients and deliver on the full promise of CRISPR technologies.

This policy covers all facets of employment including, but not limited to: recruitment, selection, placement, promotions, transfers, demotions, terminations, training, and compensation.

*Mammoth Biosciences requires that all employees be vaccinated against COVID as a condition of at-will employment, with exceptions for medical or religious reasons in compliance with local, state, and federal law.*

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. **About Voltava:**  
At Voltava, people power everything we do. Our vibrant, collaborative, and people-focused culture is the foundation for everything we deliver, from complex module assembly and sequencing to contract manufacturing, supply chain, automation, and tooling and equipment design for OEM customers across the automotive, industrial, e-mobility, heavy truck, defense, and technology sectors. Kinetyc, our scalable contract manufacturing arm based in Wixom, Michigan, expands our capabilities and capacity to support customers across a range of industries. Together, we are Building A Better Everything.
  
  
**About the Role:**  
**At Voltava, we're Building Better Manufacturing:** operations where people, technology, and operational excellence come together to deliver exceptional results.
  
As Plant Manager, you will run the full production operation for your customer-centric unit, including Materials, Assembly, Shipping, Quality, Maintenance, and Engineering. You own results in safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, profitability, and people, and you build the leadership bench that sustains them.
  
This is a highly visible role for a leader who pairs operational depth and business acumen with a servant leadership mindset. You will build an engaged, high-performing culture while leading deployment of VIBE (Voltava Business System) and the Daily Management System (DMS), continuous improvement, and the adoption of AI, automation, and best-in-class manufacturing technology on the shop floor.
  
  
**What You Will Do:**  

* Own plant performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, profitability, and employee engagement.
* Build, coach, and develop a high-performing leadership team, with real succession depth at every level.
* Champion servant leadership grounded in trust, accountability, collaboration, and employee development.
* Turn employee feedback into visible action that improves employee experience.
* Use KPIs and operational data to track performance, solve problems at the root, and drive continuous improvement.
* Lead implementation of VIBE (Voltava Business System) at the plant, embedding Lean Manufacturing, standardized work, 5S, and PFEP as the daily operating system.
* Own plant adoption of the Daily Management System (DMS): establish daily routines for reviewing performance, escalating and solving problems, and holding leaders accountable for consistent execution.
* Lead innovation and the implementation of AI solutions, automation, and advanced technology that modernize the shop floor and improve safety, quality, productivity, profitability, and efficiency.

* Servant leadership mindset, with demonstrated success building culture, engagement, accountability, and talent.
* Experience using KPIs and operational data to improve safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost.
* Strong financial, analytical, and problem-solving skills in a manufacturing environment.
* Preferred: experience championing innovation, automation, AI, or emerging manufacturing technologies.
* Clear communicator and collaborator who can influence and lead at every level of the organization.

**What Success Looks Like:**  
Success means a plant where people are engaged, leaders are empowered, VIBE and DMS drive consistent daily execution, technology enables better performance, and operational excellence is part of how we work every day.
  
  
**You will know you are making an impact when:**  

* Safety is part of the culture, and leaders and team members take ownership every day.
* The plant delivers consistent results in safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, profitability, and customer satisfaction.
* Employee engagement keeps improving, with real follow-through on feedback.
* Leaders model servant leadership and create an environment of trust, accountability, collaboration, respect, and development.
* Innovation projects and new technologies, including AI and advanced manufacturing solutions, are implemented and deliver measurable improvements on the shop floor and in the office.
* Teams embrace continuous improvement and keep finding smarter, safer, more efficient ways to work.
* VIBE and the Daily Management System are fully implemented and sustained, with daily management routines running consistently, leaders accountable for them, and results that hold.
* The leadership pipeline is strong, with talented team members developed and ready for their next role.

**Education:**

Our total rewards package supports you at every stage of your career and life, and may include comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage; retirement savings with employer contributions; tuition reimbursement; paid time off and holidays; employee assistance resources; and wellness programs that support your health, financial well-being, and professional growth.
  
  
**Our Core Values:**

* Integrity: We earn trust through every interaction.

At Voltava, employment decisions are based on qualifications, skills, experience, and business needs. We believe that a diverse and inclusive workforce strengthens our ability to innovate, serve our customers, and achieve our goals.
  
Accessibility and Accommodations

**About Us:**

  

**Tidal Vision:**

We believe that sustainability should not require customers to compromise on price, convenience, or performance. Our mission is to create positive and systemic environmental impact by making our biopolymer solutions cost competitive, more convenient, and better performing than the synthetic chemicals we displace. We value innovation and take pride in challenging the status-quo; we choose to view obstacles as opportunities. We value new ideas and encourage the team to apply creativity and invent new solutions to meet challenging demands. We value open, direct communication and foster a collaborative working environment through our unique approach to work culture. We value our employees and demonstrate that through our compensation and benefits programs and opportunities for growth and development.

  

**About Cesco Solutions**:  
Cesco Solutions is the leader in creating client value in liquid/solids industrial water and process applications. Specializing in industries such as food & beverage, paper process and high-organics wastewater overall, we focus on eliminating waste/sludge through reduction and upcycling, at the same time, reducing contamination of downstream biological systems so they run more effectively and efficiently.

As part of Tidal Vision, Cesco leverages chitosan-based chemistry as a sustainable resource recovery approach, to traditional synthetic and metal-based chemistry, to improve paper strength, waste clarification, reduce sludge, and enhance treatment efficiency. By combining advanced chemistry, application expertise, and operational support, Cesco helps facilities optimize wastewater performance, lower chemical consumption, and maintain regulatory compliance while advancing more sustainable treatment practices.

Tidal Vision strives to build and invest in the highest performing and most innovative team. We put our people and customers above process, avoid company-wide rules as much as possible, and have the courage to take unusual approaches to advance our mission. The ideal candidate is a proven leader with experience managing manufacturing or food processing operations, preferably within the seafood, meat, poultry, dairy, or other protein processing industries. **Job Summary**

The position of **Plant Manager** is responsible for directing, coordinating, and managing the overall facility operation in conjunction with the customer’s production requirements. Ensure facility production objectives are achieved at the lowest cost consistent with IATF16949 quality requirements. Delegate production leadership responsibilities to achieve the desired objectives set forth in the corporate business plan while maintaining compliance to Federal, State, and Local Safety and Environmental regulations and laws.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Plant Operation
  + Coordinate with the operations manager in the execution of production schedules based on sales requirements and plant capacity.
  + Coordinate and communicate with leadership team and department managers in meeting production goals while focusing on continuous improvement and cost reduction initiatives.
  + Schedule manufacturing activities based on customer releases to minimize inventory.
  + Ensure orders are released in chronological order (FIFO) unless circumstances dictate a change in customer needs.
  + Ensure all “work in process” is properly tagged in accordance with procedures and instructions.
  + Receive and review daily shift reports from leadership team and address areas of concern.
* Ensure the production floor is well equipped, well maintained and efficiently designed
  + Per the IATF16949 requirements, ensure that production floor is equipped with proper work instructions and procedures to carry out production activities.
  + Ensure properly maintained equipment and appropriate trained personnel are available to carry out these activities.
  + Work with operations, program management, and process engineering teams to ensure new programs and process changes are implemented within designated launch plan requirements.
  + Support new program launches and engineer changes that may include floor layouts, staffing, quality and/or tooling requirements.
  + Provide continuous review of departmental processes to improve overall efficiencies.
  + Ensure facility management, making sure the facility meets all production operation requirements.
* Adherence to established policies, processes and procedures
  + Work with leadership team to enforce written policies and procedures to ensure consistency and fairness while maintaining a healthy and safe work environment.
  + Review and approve recommendations of subordinates in matters of position changes and promotions.
  + Work with leadership team to identify and record any issues relating to process failures, policy or procedure violations, or quality system failures
  + When and where required, assist leadership team with attendance management, performance management and corrective action of employees.
* Assist with implementation and compliance of all health, safety, environmental and quality control plans
  + Work with quality department to ensure adherence to the IATF16949 quality standards and corporate quality best practices.
  + Review and disposition of nonconforming products.
  + Assist in providing solutions to prevent reoccurrence.
  + Ensure consistency with implementation and adherence of the company health, safety and environmental policies and processes.
  + Ensure compliance with Federal, State and Local regulatory requirements such as OSHA, EPA, etc.
  + Be visible, assume leadership, and assist in developing and initiating an effective health and safety attitude. Participate and initiate in continuous safety training.

**Qualifications**

* Education
  + Minimum Required: Associates Degree or Technical Accreditation
  + Preferred: Bachelor’s Degree in Business Management, Administration or equivalent
* Experience
  + Minimum Required: 5+ years working in a production environment
  + 2+ years working in a manager or supervisory role in manufacturing/production environment
  + Preferred: 5+ years working in a managerial role in a manufacturing/production environment
* Must have and maintain a valid Driver’s License
* Strong technical background and a general understanding of a manufacturing/production process
* Fluent in English (verbal, reading, writing)
* Must be team-oriented and have excellent communication, organizational and computer literacy skills
* Requires a high level of professionalism and strong work ethic
* Preferred: Familiarity with TS16949 or IATF 16949, Quality Audits, and Environmental Management System and OSHA Requirements

**Working Conditions**

The following working conditions are present or expected on a daily basis:

* Manufacturing/production floor environment with a presence on the production floor required for at least 50% of daily work time.
* Frequent exposure to industrial manufacturing, automotive vehicles, weather elements, chemicals and robotics.
* Personal protective equipment must be worn at all times on the production floor.

The organization reserves the right to change, amend or disuse this job description at any time. This document is intended to provide an overview of the required responsibilities and qualifications.

Required
