records.title: Senior Manager, Additive Manufacturing Operations
records.description:
Divergent is building the new industrial age. Every day, our teams design, manufacture, and assemble advanced systems for some of the world’s most demanding industries. Our integrated engineering and manufacturing platform transforms complex designs into production-ready solutions, helping customers move faster, build smarter, and deliver critical systems when they matter most. Divergent is a qualified Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and supports leading U.S. aerospace and defense companies.
  
  
Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built.
  
  
Purpose
  
  
We are seeking an exceptional, results-driven
**Senior Manager of Additive Manufacturing Operations**
to lead and scale our Factory 1 production organization. This is a high-impact leadership role responsible for driving world-class execution across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people development while shaping the future of manufacturing.
  
  
The Additive Manufacturing organization leverages proprietary, state-of-the-art systems and processes to execute metal laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), depowdering, manual and automated support removal, surface finishing, heat treatment, and inspection across multiple factory sites supporting both prototype and high-rate production.
  
  
This role is ideal for an ambitious operations leader who thrives in fast-paced, high-growth environments and combines strong manufacturing fundamentals with data-driven decision making, automation, and continuous improvement. Beyond delivering daily operational performance, this leader will develop people, build scalable operating systems, and partner with engineering to industrialize new technologies that will define the next generation of manufacturing.
  
  
The ideal candidate is energized by difficult manufacturing challenges, inspires high-performing teams, and is passionate about building organizations capable of delivering exceptional results.
  
  
The Role
  
  
**Operational Leadership**

* Lead Factory 1 additive manufacturing operations to achieve world-class performance in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and equipment reliability.
* Build, develop, and mentor a high-performing team while fostering a culture of accountability, ownership, urgency, and continuous improvement.
* Drive disciplined daily management through standard work, visual management, structured problem solving, and operational rigor.
* Optimize manufacturing flow by increasing equipment uptime, eliminating bottlenecks, improving process repeatability, and maximizing production throughput.
* Partner closely with Platform Development, Manufacturing Engineering, and Automation teams to successfully launch new equipment, technologies, and manufacturing capabilities.

**Operational Excellence**

* Champion Lean Manufacturing principles and continuous improvement across all additive manufacturing processes.
* Establish scalable operating systems that improve efficiency, stability, and manufacturing readiness as production grows.
* Utilize manufacturing data, KPIs, and analytics to drive operational decisions and prioritize improvement initiatives.
* Develop meaningful performance dashboards and operating rhythms that enable rapid identification and resolution of production issues.
* Lead initiatives to improve Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), first-pass yield, cycle time, labor productivity, and cost per part.

**Equipment Reliability & Technical Capability**

* Continue developing the in-house Additive Manufacturing Service organization by strengthening technical capability, preventive maintenance programs, troubleshooting processes, and technician training.
* Drive reliability initiatives that maximize printer availability, reduce unplanned downtime, and improve long-term equipment performance.
* Partner with technical teams to identify recurring equipment issues and implement sustainable corrective actions.

**Performance Monitoring & Compliance**

* Ensure strict adherence to Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), work instructions, process controls, and quality standards.
* Monitor key operational metrics and hold teams accountable for achieving business objectives.
* Drive disciplined root cause analysis and corrective actions to eliminate recurring manufacturing issues.
* Develop clear, actionable operational reporting that enables data-driven decision making across the organization.

**Safety, Quality & Financial Management**

* Foster a safety-first culture aligned with Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) standards and best practices.
* Partner with EHS to proactively develop and implement safety initiatives that reduce operational risk.
* Ensure manufacturing processes consistently meet internal quality requirements and applicable industry standards.
* Develop, manage, and execute the Factory 1 Additive Manufacturing operating budget while balancing productivity, cost, and long-term capability investments.

**Basic Qualifications**

* Ability to lawfully access information and technology that is subject to US export controls.
* Demonstrated success leading complex manufacturing operations in high-performance production environments.
* Proven ability to build, develop, and lead high-performing technical organizations.
* Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing, operational excellence, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Experience using manufacturing data and operational metrics to drive strategic decision making and measurable business results.
* Proven ability to execute in startup or rapidly scaling manufacturing environments while effectively navigating ambiguity and change.
* Demonstrated success improving operational performance through equipment reliability, process optimization, and organizational development.
* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Weld Engineering, or a related technical discipline (or equivalent practical experience).

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Leadership experience in metal additive manufacturing or other advanced manufacturing environments.
* Experience with Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) production systems.
* Experience with aerospace manufacturing standards, including AS9100 and NADCAP.
* Experience implementing Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Theory of Constraints, or similar operational excellence methodologies.
* Experience leading automation, Industry 4.0, MES, or digital manufacturing initiatives.
* Demonstrated success scaling manufacturing organizations through periods of rapid growth.

Pay Range: $156,640 USD - $215,380 USD
  
  
**What We Offer Our Regular, Full-Time Employees:**

* Holistic Compensation Package: Enjoy a world-class compensation package that includes a competitive salary, equity plan, and discretionary results-based incentive bonus opportunities, ensuring you're truly valued for your contributions.
* Wellness and Time Off: Embrace a healthy lifestyle with paid vacation, sick time, and company holidays, including a year-end shutdown to recharge. We support growing families with paid parental leave, recognizing the importance of bonding time.
* Comprehensive Health and Wellness: Prioritize your well-being with our comprehensive health and wellness benefits, offering both HMO and Premium PPO options. Additionally, benefit from company-sponsored life insurance and short and long-term disability coverage for peace of mind.
* Investment in Growth: We're committed to your professional development. Take advantage of reimbursement opportunities for learning and development initiatives, empowering you to continuously expand your skill set and reach peak performance.
* Collaborative and High-Performing Environment: Join our collaborative, dynamic, and high-performing team within a fast-paced, mission-driven company. Together, we're disrupting the traditional manufacturing industry, fostering innovation, and integrating people and technology to reduce our footprint.

records.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering
records.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!
  
  
In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by
*TIME*
as a “Best Invention”,
*MIT Technology Review*
as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and
*Fast Company*
as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.
  
  
Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.
  
  
**Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.**
Role Description
  
  
As the Senior Manager of Assembly Manufacturing Engineering, you will serve as the primary architect of the production lifecycle, bridging the gap between research prototypes and high-volume factory operations. You will lead a multidisciplinary team of engineers to develop and internalize robust manufacturing processes for both battery enclosures and module/pack assembly—including robotic joining, sealing, electrolyte filling, and leak testing. By owning the full equipment lifecycle, from defining detailed user requirements through to factory testing and final site commissioning, you ensure that production lines are world-class, delivering a "machine that builds the machine" with precision and technical rigor.
  
  
Strategically, your objective is to drive operational scale by ensuring products are designed specifically for ease of manufacturing and assembly during the earliest development phases. You will champion a data-driven culture that utilizes failure mode analysis and advanced root-cause investigation to reduce production risks and achieve aggressive targets for quality, output rate, and equipment uptime. By fostering collaboration between Product Design, Quality, and Supply Chain, you will manage the critical transition from initial design to full-scale production, ensuring that every process is statistically validated to guarantee long-term reliability and cost-effectiveness.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Lead the development and optimization of battery manufacturing processes for battery assembly manufacturing.
* Ensure highly capable processes are identified and demonstrated for our production facilities ahead of detailed equipment design.
* Oversee the design and implementation of manufacturing processes such as: manual and robotic assembly, joining, sealing, system leak testing, and quality checks to achieve optimal performance and reliability.
* Collaborate with product design team, R&D, quality, and supply chain, to translate product requirements into a battery design and manufacturing process that achieve our company targets.
* Collaborate cross functionally to develop and maintain PFMEA, process specifications, measurement systems GR&R, control plan, and quality inspection methods (incoming, outgoing, and in-process).
* Lead troubleshooting efforts to identify root causes of manufacturing issues and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
* Internalize responsibility for delivery of equipment and processes that enable the operations team to achieve factory production metrics (quality, yield, rate, and availability).
* Identify trends/correlations, and make data-driven decisions for process optimization.

**What You'll Bring**

* Hands-on experience in a high-volume manufacturing organization.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering.
* 10 years of experience in engineering roles within battery manufacturing or a related industry, with expertise in complex assembly processes. 4+ leading technical teams.
* Demonstrated experience in manufacturing equipment procurement, setup, and commissioning, including a clear understanding of equipment qualification and validation protocols.
* Strong understanding of lean manufacturing principles and their application in a high-volume production environment.
* Proven track record of successfully leading cross-functional teams in the development and optimization of manufacturing processes for electrochemical systems.
* Proficiency in process engineering principles, statistical analysis, and quality management systems for process optimization and improvement.
* Strong communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams and convey technical concepts to diverse stakeholders.
* Leadership and mentoring abilities with a commitment to fostering a culture of continuous learning and accelerated innovation through quick iteration.
* Experience working in a fast-paced startup environment is a plus.

*This opportunity is based out of Form Factory 1 – Form Energy’s 550,000-square-foot, state-of-the-art manufacturing facility located in Weirton, WV, a commutable distance from Pittsburgh. Purpose-built for high-volume, advanced battery production, Form Factory 1 is a hub of fast-moving, collaborative work driving a new era of large-scale American energy manufacturing in the heart of the Rust Belt.*
*Relocation assistance is available.*
*Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.*
*When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.*
*To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.*
*If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.*
*Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will
**never**
solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.*

As an S&C Electric team member, you’ll work on projects that have real-world impact. You’ll help transform the grid for resilient and reliable power worldwide. S&C has more than a 100-year history of innovation and has been 100% employee-owned since 2012. We continue this legacy as a trusted, forward-thinking leader in the electrical industry. You will advance a safer, more reliable, and more resilient electrical grid. Our products help the grid adapt to severe weather and transition to clean energy. We’re big enough to be a respected industry leader but small enough for you to impact our company directly. Our commitment gives you opportunities to impact on and off the job positively. Join S&C to make an impact on tomorrow’s energy challenges and become an employee-owner.
  
  
**Hours**

* 8:00 am – 5:00 pm (Mon-Fri) On Site Palatine, IL

**Compensation**
At S&C, we are dedicated to providing competitive and equitable compensation for all our team members, and we are committed to transparency in our pay practices.
**The estimated annual base salary range for this position is $154,968- $205,332.60.**
Individual pay within this salary range is determined by several compensable factors, including performance, knowledge, job-related skills and experience, and relevant education or training. This role is also eligible for S&C’s annual incentive plan (AIP), subject to eligibility criteria.
  
  
**Join Our Team as a Senior Manager – Productions Operations!**
The Senior Manager – Production Operations is responsible for planning, overseeing, and managing the operations and production processes for the department, leading a team of Managers, Assistant Managers, and Supervisors to achieve strategic Objectives and Key Results (OKRs), and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in safety, quality, delivery, and cost (SQDC). The Senior Manager – Production Operations focuses on strategic and tactical operations planning with a mid-term focus, contributing towards greater functional strategies, directing the smooth operations of multiple departments, driving strategic problem-solving and continuous improvement initiatives, reporting out to executive leadership on results, and making strategic adjustments and countermeasures when targets are missed.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Health & Safety Compliance: Drive a safety-first culture, ensuring leaders understand and enforce safety rules. Ensure that health & safety is considered in all departmental plans in order to maintain and promote a safety-conscious manufacturing environment and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards related to production operations.
* Leadership & People Management: Lead, inspire, and develop a high-performing team. Role model appropriate and professional workplace behaviors, address/mediate conflicts to restore harmony, and support a positive, healthy, and inclusive workplace culture in accordance with S&C's mission, vision, values, and guiding principles. Manage departmental administrative team member processes, including but not limited to recruitment, induction, vacation management, performance reviews, performance improvement plans, and workforce/succession planning. Proactively establish, monitor, and hold team members accountable to clear responsibilities and accountabilities; provide ongoing performance feedback, both positive and developmental; address performance gaps in a timely manner; recognize and reward achievements and initiate decisions for corrective actions and terminations where required. Foster a culture that supports the growth and development of team members and proactively train, mentor, and coach team members.
* Strategy Implementation: Cascade strategies to develop mid-term tactical and operational plans for the function, in line with the company’s overall business objectives, including automation, insourcing, and unattended machining. Oversee a leadership team that directs the day-to-day operations of activities within the department and span of control, ensuring the timely and cost-effective delivery of outputs to KPIs. Work with senior leaders to recommend and implement strategic adjustments to operational plans in order to meet OKRs and KPIs.
* Production Planning & Operations: Lead strategic production planning initiatives, collaborating with cross-functional teams to develop a mid-term plan for the department and initiate strategies that contribute to long-term production planning. Work with leaders to optimize production schedules, identify bottlenecks, and determine capacity plans and processing methods. Evaluate machine resources to ensure continued production and minimal downtime. Establish a balance between increased productivity and reduced costs of manufacturing operations. Set mid-term productivity goals and analyze report-outs from Managers.
* Lean Performance Systems: Recommend and implement goals for departmental performance improvement, supporting leaders as they identify and implement process improvements to enhance production efficiency, reduce costs, and increase overall operational effectiveness. Collaborate with other leaders to formulate high-level solutions and develop plans for how to implement improvements throughout multi-faceted functions. Serve as a change agent by influencing, communicating, and institutionalizing a culture of continuous improvement, simplification, standard work, process improvement, and lean principles.
* Quality Management: Oversee the implementation of broad quality control programs, ensuring leaders fully understand quality issues and their corresponding solutions.Discuss and understand high-level, multi-faceted quality issues and help leaders formulate resolutions. Monitor and guide leaders responsible for the department’s communication of corrective action plans, resolutions, and quality results.
* Reporting: Analyzes reports and reviews provided by first-line supervisors. Communicates regularly with upper management regarding problems impacting production. Reports issues regarding production, quality, maintenance, or personnel to senior and executive leadership.
* Budget Management: Develop and manage the function’s budget, ensuring accuracy and appropriate allocation of resources to maximize ROI and the achievement of larger functional strategies and objectives. Approve expenditures for the achievement of operational goals and work with senior leaders to identify investment opportunities for gains towards mid-term goals.
* Compliance: Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
* Maintain regular and punctual attendance.
* Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required.
* Communicate effectively and respectfully with others.
* Drive a car or other vehicle.
* Other responsibilities as assigned.

**Required**
**What you’ll need to succeed:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a technical discipline such as Engineering, or a related field.
* Beliefs in, and alignment with, S&C Guiding Principles and Core Values
* 10+ years of manufacturing experience in an industrial metals fabrication environment, including advanced CNC machining, welding, laser cutting, forming, punching, stamping and related finishing operations.
* 5+ years of supervisory or management experience in a fabrication environment leading hourly and salaried employees.
* Leadership experience in workforce planning, scheduling, and staffing, employee development, coaching, and performance management.Experience managing multiple shifts is preferred.
* Knowledge of precision machining processes and practices within a high mix, low-to-medium volume environment.
* Demonstrated track record of lean manufacturing leadership, sustained improvements, and KPI attainment.
* Great leadership skills within a multi-level manufacturing environment, with an ability to lead, guide, motivate, and delegate to deliver results.
* Sound critical thinking, organizational, planning, and project management skills, and creative problem-solving when obstacles arise.
* Great interpersonal skills to establish meaningful relationships built on mutual trust and respect, navigate and resolve conflict, moderate behaviors, and foster collaborative working relationships amongst a diverse audience.
* Excellent communication skills, (written, verbal, listening, and presentation) ability to liaise with internal and external stakeholders at all levels, from leadership to support staff, and present influentially to achieve buy-in from executives, managers, and team members.
* Sound analytical skills with the ability to use and analyze data to drive informed decisions, problem-solve difficult issues, and leverage data and learnings to drive continuous improvement.
* Proven success partnering across teams, creating effective partnerships at all levels, and collaborating at an operational level.
* Adapts to change and different ways of doing things quickly and positively and finds ways to get things accomplished, even when faced with challenges.
* Proficient computer skills, including Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook) and preferably, Oracle.

**Preferred**

* Master’s degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field.
* Six Sigma Certification(s).
* Certified Lean Six Sigma (CLSS).
* Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE).

S&C Electric is committed to equal-opportunity employment. All employees and applicants will be considered without regard to age, color, disability, gender, national origin, race, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, protected veteran status, or any other classification protected by federal, state, or local law. If you are an individual with a disability and need an accommodation to complete the application, please email us at TAsupport@sandc.com.
  
  
No fixed deadline
  
  
**About Us**
In 1909, S&C Electric Company transformed the delivery of safe, reliable electricity with the invention of the Liquid Power Fuse. Today, as the world faces extreme weather events and the demand for electricity grows, S&C continues to innovate and advance the electrical grid, ensuring reliable and resilient power for homes, communities, and critical infrastructure around the world.
  
  
With a diverse, global workforce and core values around integrity, safety, and quality, S&C is a trusted industry leader and top workplace that offers meaningful careers to more than 3,500 team members. As a people-first organization, S&C is committed to fostering an inclusive and collaborative workplace where team members advance their careers through robust talent-development programs and involved leadership.
  
  
S&C’s deeply rooted belief diversity fosters greater creativity, innovation, and success guides the company to advance and sustain a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace culture.

Retirement Benefits: 401(k) Retirement Savings and Employee Stock Ownership Plan (KSOP) offering traditional and Roth 401(k) options and an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) component; KSOP participants can receive annual ESOP company contributions of over 11% of eligible earnings (3% Core, up to 3.5% Match, Variable Periodic).

**Join Our Team as a Senior Manager - Supplier Quality**
!
  
  
The Senior Manager - Supplier Quality is responsible for ensuring that all suppliers meet or exceed the company’s quality standards through strategic audits, risk mitigation, and continuous supplier development. This role emphasizes proactive engagement with suppliers to ensure compliance, minimize risks, and ultimately ensure the quality of supplied components to S&C. The position also oversees the qualification and ongoing evaluation of suppliers to align with the company’s operational and commercial objectives.
  
  
**Essential Functions**

* Supplier Audits & Qualification: Formulate and implement a comprehensive operational strategy to drive continuous quality improvement initiatives within the supplier quality function. Lead a team that conducts comprehensive audits and supplier qualification processes, ensuring compliance with quality standards and the prevention of defective component shipments from the supplier to S&C. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to assess supplier capabilities and align with company requirements.
* COPQ: Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) Reduction: Take ownership of reducing the cost of poor quality (COPQ) by analyzing trends in supplier-reported issues, identifying root causes, and implementing preventative measures to ensure continuous improvement in product quality.
* Production Part Approval Process (PPAP): Oversee the PPAP process to validate supplier-provided components meet specified requirements. Ensure that documentation, testing, and approvals are conducted thoroughly and accurately.
* Risk Analysis and Mitigation: Perform supplier risk analysis by evaluating historical performance, process controls, and financial stability. Develop and execute mitigation strategies to minimize potential supply chain disruptions.
* Corrective Action and Accountability: Lead the resolution of supplier-related quality issues through effective corrective action processes. Establish clear accountability frameworks to ensure sustained improvements and proactive prevention of non-confirming/defective components before receiving them.
* Subject Matter Expertise: Serve as a subject matter expert in Supplier Quality, staying abreast of industry best practices, standards, and technological advancements and ensuring the greater quality function is well-versed in the latest quality methodologies and tools, facilitating a high level of technical proficiency.

records.title: Chief Manufacturing Engineer-Remote
records.description:
**Fantastic challenges. Amazing opportunities.**
GKN Aerospace is reimagining air travel: going further, faster and greener! Fuelled by great people whose expertise and creativity sets the standards in our industry, we’re inspired by the opportunities to innovate and break boundaries. We’re proud to play a part in protecting the world’s democracies. And we’re committed to putting sustainability at the centre of everything we do, opening up and protecting our planet. With over 16,000 employees across 32 manufacturing sites in 12 countries we serve over 90% of the world’s aircraft and engine manufacturers and achieved sales of £3.6bn in 2025. There are no limits to where you can take your career.
  
  
Role Summary
  
  
As part of GKN Aerospace Airframes E&T, Chief Manufacturing Engineers (CME) lead the development, industrialisation and improvement of Manufacturing Systems whilst serving as the customer-facing representatives of the ME function.
  
  
Day-to-day, a CME is focused on delivery of non-recurring engineering projects including New Product Introductions (NPI), Transfers of Work (ToW), Major Modifications (Mods), Technology Insertions and resolving manufacturing process related quality and delivery challenges together with production engineering teams.
  
  
When necessary, a CME may lead deployed ME resources to deliver these projects, ensuring compliance with identified requirements (e.g. Produceability, Productivity, Cost, Schedule, Regulatory) and adherence to Zero Defect Manufacturing (ZDM) standards.
  
  
**Remote Role**
Travel Requirements
  
  
This is a remote working position that requires frequent routine and occasional non-routine travel (up to 25-50%) to be on-site at GKN facilities and suppliers, including but not limited to; Phoenix (AZ), Wichita (KS), Sumner (WA), Chihuahua (Mexico), Tallassee (AL).
  
  
Candidates must live in a location with strong transport links. This could be 1-2 hours drive (approx.) from a major international hub airport (e.g. Dallas, Atlanta, Houston) or locally to a regional airport with multiple flights per day to major hub airports.
  
  
Role Accountabilities
  
  

* Bids– Accountable to validate and approve the proposed definition of the Manufacturing System and its associated performance targets which are submitted at LG3 (Programme Launch). Working closely with the Industrial Architect, the CME reviews output for technical risks and communicates these to the Programme. This may include process flow, bill of materials, proposed industrial setting, product cost estimates, requirements compliance or technology developments needed. The CME owns the Non-Recurring Engineering cost estimate for the ME technical content delivery.
* NPI– Accountable for delivering a Manufacturing System that fulfils all agreed stakeholder requirements (technical, quality, regulatory), business case metrics and system performance targets between LG3 (Programme Launch) and LG7 (Steady State Production) whilst ensuring that planning, development and commissioning is completed on-schedule and on-cost.
* Sustaining – Accountable for the governance and oversight of a portfolio of Manufacturing Systems, delivered through regular review of system KPIs and Industrial Review assessments. Takes corrective action to ensure Manufacturing Systems continue to perform in-line with the productivity & quality targets set.
* Leadership of Projects- Accountable for delivery of the non-recurring ME activities within a given programme or project. Responsible to provide technical leadership and direction using project management fundamentals: planning & estimating, resourcing & budgeting and reporting on project performance (earned value) to internal business standards.
* Leadership of Teams – Accountable to the Programme and Site for effective utilisation of deployed manufacturing engineering resource while delivering ME content of projects by providing day-to-day coordination, recognition and accountability and implementing ME best practice with the deployed team.
* Quality – Accountable for delivery of manufacturing systems that are Zero Defect Manufacturing (ZDM) capable through a relentless focus on delivering APQP to the AS9145 standard during the NPI phase. Must exhibit and drive a product quality mind-set within ME and ensure compliance to agreed Customer, Regulatory, Business and functional standards.
* Relationships – Accountable to maintain positive and functional working relationships with internal and external customers, to communicate and inform clearly and frequently with key stakeholders within the business, and to foster and champion GKN’s 5 principles within sphere of influence.

**Required**
Role Qualifications
  
  

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional qualification in Engineering (Aerospace, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials, Electrical, Chemical, or related discipline).
* Minimum of 8 years of experience in aerospace manufacturing or similar, highly regulated environments operating under AS9100 Quality Management Systems.
* Recent experience developing a manufacturing system for a New Product Introduction (NPI) with a comprehensive understanding of product lifecycle gate processes.
* Broad, hands-on experience with common manufacturing processes (e.g. machining, forming, welding, composites, assembly, metrology).
* Knowledgeable of structured problem solving and RCCA methodologies (e.g. 8D) and how to apply these to complex problems.
* Demonstrated capability to organise and drive technical projects to achieve business goals, preferably in complex multi-site environments.
* Ability to lead and influence people, build trust and establish effective working relationships within a global organisation and with external customer stakeholders.
* Fluent in English language, both written and spoken.
* US Person for Export Control purposes

**Preferred**

* Demonstrated deployment of AS9145 APQP process.
* Working knowledge of digital systems for manufacturing (PLM, MES, ERP).
* Deep, expert knowledge in one or more manufacturing process areas (e.g. machining, forming, welding, composites, assembly, metrology).
* Experience working with or for major aerospace OEMs and their systems.
* Proven ability to lead change in a Manufacturing System with evidence of delivering significant improvements in terms of cost, quality or throughput.
* Proven ability to identify and deliver industrial productivity improvements and monitor their efficacy by setting appropriate metrics.
* Project / Programme Management Professional Qualification.
* Six Sigma Certification.

Salary Range
  
  
$120-160k
  
  
We’ll offer you fantastic challenges and amazing opportunities. This is your chance to be part of an organisation that has proven itself to be at the cutting edge of our industry; and is committed to pushing the boundaries even further. And with some of the best training on offer in the industry, who knows how far you can go?
  
  
**A Great Place to work needs a Great Way of Working**
Everyone is welcome to apply to GKN. We believe that we can only achieve our ambitions through a coming together of diverse minds who enjoy collaborating in an inspirational environment. Through our commitment to diversity, inclusion and belonging and by living our five powerful principles we’ve created a culture where everyone feels welcome to contribute. It’s a culture that won us ‘The Best Workplace Culture Award’. By embracing and celebrating what makes us unique we encourage everyone to bring their full self to work.
  
  
We’re also committed to providing an accessible recruitment process, so if you require reasonable adjustments at any stage during our recruitment process please get in touch and let us know.
  
  
We are the place where human dreams, plus human endeavour, shape the future of aerospace innovation and technology.

*Simtra BioPharma Solutions (Simtra) is a world-class Contract Development Manufacturing Organization, partnering with pharmaceutical and biotech companies to bring their sterile injectable products to market. As such, there is a strong emphasis on quality and continuous improvement at Simtra. We hold ourselves to the highest quality and regulatory standards.*
*While our primary focus is cGMP manufacturing, we offer many support services including formulation and development, lyophilization optimization, global regulatory support and secondary packaging.*

records.description:
Global Director, Operational Excellence COE
  
  
At Nouryon, our global team takes positive action every day, to reach higher collectively and individually. We create innovative and sustainable solutions for our customers to answer society’s needs – today and in the future.
  
  
We are looking for team members who bring ideas forward, champion others and work together to do better. Does that sound like you?
  
  
**About the job**
The Global Director, Operational Excellence (OpEx) COE is a senior leadership role responsible for defining the strategic direction, standards, and governance of Nouryon’s global OpEx program. This role owns the organizational design, frameworks, methodologies, and capability pipelines that enable sustainable continuous improvement across 63 manufacturing sites in the Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) organization – spanning the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific.
  
  
This role is the architect of OpEx productivity engine. The COE Director owns the design of the systems, standards, and organizational capabilities that enable VMC and FMC delivery – including ownership of the enterprise systems of record for productivity tracking (ANT) and performance reporting (PowerBI). Execution of productivity targets is driven through the regional OpEx Manager network; this role ensures those teams are equipped, aligned, and operating within a governance structure capable of sustaining results.
  
  
This role leads a newly consolidated Center of Excellence that brings together CI methodology and Lean/Six Sigma certification, ISC Learning & Development, End-to-End Process Management, and Manufacturing Excellence under a single governance structure. The COE Director sets priorities, establishes the program architecture, and holds accountability for outcomes – operating through a team of direct reports who own execution across regions. Key relationships span the COO, regional OpEx Managers, Site Directors, and ISC functional leaders across three regions.
  
  
This is a permanent, full-time position reporting to the VP, Global Operational Excellence & Digital Manufacturing, based in a Nouryon regional hub (Amsterdam, Houston, or Shanghai) with global travel of 15–25%.
  
  
**In your future role as the Global Director, Operational Excellence COE, you will**
**CI Methodology, Standards & Governance**

* Own the global Operational Excellence methodology, ensuring a consistent, fit-for-purpose CI framework is deployed across all 63 Nouryon manufacturing sites.

* Define and govern the Lean/Six Sigma certification pathway from Yellow Belt through Master Black Belt, establishing quality standards for program content, assessment, and progression.
* Partner with regional OpEx Managers to translate global standards into site-level execution plans, maintaining strategic alignment while enabling regional adaptation.
* Establish and sustain a durable CI Governance model – defining the review cadence, accountability structure, and performance mechanisms that ensure CI maturity compounds over time across the Nouryon network.
* Own the enterprise systems of record for productivity tracking and performance reporting, including the ANT productivity platform and PowerBI reporting architecture, ensuring data integrity and leadership visibility across all sites.

**ISC Learning & Development**

* Lead the design and continuous improvement of the ISC Learning & Development program, spanning CI capability, technical skills, and leadership development for the ISC organization.
* Direct the L&D team to build and maintain a structured curriculum that supports onboarding, role progression, and organizational capability uplift.
* Connect L&D investment directly to VMC and FMC delivery targets, ensuring program outcomes are measurable and business-relevant.
* Own the design mandate for Digital Literacy and AI capability across the ISC organization – defining the people, process, and metrics framework required to build and sustain enterprise AI competency at scale. This includes establishing program objectives, identifying ownership, and proposing a deployment model aligned to Nouryon’s broader digital strategy.

**End-to-End Process Management**

* Own the ISC End-to-End process architecture, defining process standards, documentation requirements, and governance for core ISC value streams.
* Drive process modeling and SIPOC-level design across ISC, working through the Process Modeler and Global Process Owner to ensure clarity of accountability and performance standards.
* Identify and close process design gaps that create risk, inefficiency, or measurement inconsistency across the ISC organization.

**Manufacturing Excellence**

* Define the Manufacturing Excellence framework for Nouryon, including OEE, TPM, reliability, and asset performance standards applied across the manufacturing network.
* Direct the Manufacturing Excellence Manager to develop and deploy site-level improvement programs, closing the loop between plant performance data and structured intervention.
* Integrate manufacturing excellence priorities into the broader OpEx roadmap, ensuring alignment with Digital Manufacturing, Palantir-enabled analytics, and capital investment decisions.

**People Leadership & COE Development**

* Lead a geographically distributed team of nine direct reports
* Define team structure, role clarity, and succession priorities for the COE
* Build a high-performance COE culture grounded in Nouryon’s Leadership Capability Framework

This role requires approximately 15–25% global travel across the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific.
  
  
**Key Performance Indicators**
The Global Director, Operational Excellence COE is measured against the same Breakthrough KPIs as the VP, Global Operational Excellence & Digital Manufacturing. This alignment is intentional – the COE’s organizational design, capability systems, and governance structures exist to enable these outcomes. Execution is driven through the regional OpEx Manager network; this role is accountable for building and sustaining the organization capable of delivering them.
  

* People Safety
* Process Safety
* FMC — Fixed Manufacturing Cost Productivity
* VMC — Variable Manufacturing Cost Productivity
* OEE — Overall Equipment Effectiveness
* OTIF — On-Time In-Full
* Quality Sigma Level
* CI Activation Rate

**We believe you bring**

* A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* A minimum of 15 years of progressive experience in Operational Excellence, Continuous Improvement, or manufacturing leadership roles in a global, multi-site environment.
* Certified Master Black Belt (MBB) or Black Belt in Lean/Six Sigma, with demonstrated capability to design, govern, and quality-assure a full belt certification program.
* Proven track record of leading change management initiatives in large, matrixed, multi-regional organizations – with the ability to align diverse stakeholders and shift organizational culture.
* Deep knowledge of Manufacturing Excellence frameworks including OEE, TPM, and reliability methodologies, with experience deploying these at scale across a manufacturing network.
* Demonstrated people leadership across multiple geographies and organizational grades, including experience developing high-performing teams in a distributed structure.

**Great if you have**

* Experience in specialty chemicals, process manufacturing, or a similarly regulated, capital-intensive industrial environment.
* Hands-on expertise in End-to-End process design and governance, including SIPOC-level architecture and process ownership models.
* Experience designing and leading corporate Learning & Development programs, including competency frameworks and structured curricula for technical disciplines.
* Prior experience building or structuring a Center of Excellence from the ground up, including team design, governance models, and stakeholder alignment.
* Working proficiency with PowerBI or equivalent reporting platforms for program performance tracking and executive communication.

**We believe you are**
...
  
  
A systems thinker who sees the whole before diving into the parts. You lead through frameworks, not firefighting – you understand that durable operational excellence is built on governance, capability, and culture, not individual heroics. You bring intellectual rigor to every conversation and are comfortable challenging assumptions at any level of the organization, including in rooms where the answer is already assumed.
  
  
You are energized by building – building teams, building programs, building the conditions for others to succeed. You know how to hold standards without being rigid, and how to drive urgency without creating chaos. The right candidate is someone who finds genuine satisfaction in watching a global organization improve because of the systems they put in place – and who brings the patience, persistence, and precision that transformation at scale demands.
  
  
**We offer you**
This is a rare opportunity to architect and lead a newly consolidated global COE with a clear mandate from senior leadership, a defined team, and direct line of sight to enterprise value delivery. You will operate with significant autonomy, build the structure you believe is right, and leave a measurable legacy across a global manufacturing organization at an inflection point in its CI and digital transformation journey.
  
  
At Nouryon, we provide a great job and friendly coworkers, plus benefits in addition to salary.

**Brief Description**
**About Us**
At
**FreshDirect**
, we are reinventing the grocery experience.
  
  
Since day one, our mission has been simple: bring the best, freshest food directly from the farm to people’s homes — faster, fresher, and smarter than anyone else.
  
  
We’re not just a food company. We’re a technology-powered, customer-obsessed team building one of the most innovative end-to-end food supply chains in the industry. From proprietary routing systems to our state-of-the-art fulfillment center, every part of our business is designed to deliver unmatched quality, convenience, and care.
  
  
We partner directly with farmers, fishermen, and artisans to source the highest quality ingredients — then use smart data, automation, and logistics to deliver them at peak freshness.
  
  
It’s grocery shopping reimagined — and we’re just getting started.
  
  
If you’re passionate about innovation, care deeply about what people eat, and want to help build the future of food, we’d love to meet you.
  
  
**The Role**
The Senior Director of Operations & Transformation is responsible for driving operational excellence, strategic initiatives, and enterprise-wide transformation efforts across the organization. This leader will partner with executive stakeholders to improve business performance, optimize processes, and implement scalable solutions that support growth, efficiency, and customer experience.
  
  
Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the role will lead cross-functional projects that enhance organizational effectiveness and drive measurable business impact.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Lead high-impact transformation and continuous improvement initiatives across the business.
* Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency, productivity, and scalability.
* Partner with leaders across Operations, Supply Chain, Transportation, Manufacturing, Technology, and other functions to drive performance improvements.
* Establish and track KPIs, leveraging data and analytics to support decision-making and business outcomes.
* Develop and implement standardized processes, governance, and best practices.
* Lead complex cross-functional projects from strategy through execution.
* Drive change management efforts to ensure successful adoption of new processes and initiatives.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on operational strategy, performance, risks, and opportunities.

**What You’ll Bring**

* 10+ years of leadership experience in operations, transformation, continuous improvement, consulting, or a related field.
* Proven success leading large-scale operational and business transformation initiatives.
* Strong people leadership skills with experience building, developing, and motivating high-performing teams.
* Strong project management, change management, and stakeholder leadership skills.
* Experience driving process improvement and operational excellence in a fast-paced environment.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with a data-driven approach.
* Bachelor's degree required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

**Our Values at FreshDirect**
We live these values every day:
  
  
**A Passion for our customers**
Our customers are at the heart of everything we do. We listen, innovate, and act quickly to exceed expectations with every order and interaction.
  
  
**One team, one mission**
Everyone contributes & every role matters. We break silos, lift each other up, and share a relentless focus on delivering results. That way, we win together.
  
  
**Delivering excellence, every time**
We take pride in the quality of our food, service, and the experience we create. Our team goes above and beyond to earn trust and guarantee 100% freshness.
  
  
**Act with integrity**
We operate with honesty, respect, and accountability in how we treat our customers, teammates, and partners. We own our outcomes and always do what’s right, even when no one is watching.
  
  
**Make fast, bold decisions**
We challenge the status quo, embrace technology, and take smart risks to build a better future. At the same time, we stay true to our NYC roots and care for our community.
  
  
**We love food. Yes, literally all of us.**
**What You’ll Love About Working Here**

* A fast-paced, innovative environment where ideas turn into action
* Opportunities for growth — many of our leaders have risen through the ranks
* Direct impact on how thousands of customers experience food every day

**Salary**
$170,000-$200,000
  
  
**Total Rewards & Benefits**

* Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits
* PTO, Safe & Sick Time, and Paid Holidays
* Medical, Vision, Dental, and Voluntary Disability coverage
* 401(k) with employer match and Life Insurance
* State-of-the-art Bronx campus with on-site basketball court, cafeteria, and employee market
* Onsite FREE parking
* FREE employee shuttle bus service from nearby Subway station
* Training, leadership development, and tuition discount at local colleges
* 20% employee discount on FreshDirect online orders and Brooklyn wine store
* Minimum 50% employee discount at our onsite employee market
* Mobile phone discounts through partnerships with T-Mobile and Verizon
* Gym membership discounts through NYSC

**Our Culture**
We embrace an in-office culture, composed of individuals who thrive on the collaboration and energy that comes from working together in a shared space. We are looking for people who excel in this environment, where physical presence enhances connections and engagement. At FreshDirect, we've created an environment that thrives on teamwork, where associates can innovate, grow, and have successful careers. Many of our leaders have successfully come up through our ranks. Because of our team's extraordinary efforts, we are a leading innovator in the e-commerce and grocery industries.
  
  
**Equal Opportunity**
We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

**About the Role**
------------------

The Director, Revenue Cycle Management provides strategic leadership across key Revenue Cycle functions, including outsourced operations and vendor management, credit balance management, and quality assurance. This role is accountable for improving financial and operational performance, strengthening controls, and ensuring internal teams and external partners consistently meet established service, quality, and compliance expectations.

  
  

You will partner across Revenue Cycle, Finance, Compliance, Operations, IT, and Training to improve cash and accounts receivable performance, resolve operational risks, and drive standardized, sustainable processes. This role provides leadership across multiple teams, vendors, and functional areas and translates organizational strategy into measurable operational goals and results.

  
  

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Lead Revenue Cycle operations and strategic support functions across areas such as patient access, business office operations, claims, accounts receivable, registration, insurance verification, payment and adjustment activities, and customer service.
* Provide governance and performance oversight for **third-party and BPO vendors**, including service-level agreements (SLAs), key performance indicators (KPIs), productivity, quality, contractual performance, issue escalation, and remediation.
* Lead **credit balance operations**, including identification, validation, refunds, adjustments, aging, resolution, root-cause analysis, and prevention of recurring patient and payer credit balances.
* Lead the **Revenue Cycle Quality Assurance program**, including quality standards, audit methodologies, sampling, scoring, performance reporting, corrective action plans, controls, and ongoing monitoring.
* Drive financial and operational performance across assigned Revenue Cycle functions, including cash, accounts receivable, operating expense, vendor spend, quality, compliance, customer experience, and productivity.
* Partner with Revenue Cycle, Finance, Compliance, Operations, IT, Training, and external vendors to identify operational risks, resolve complex issues, standardize processes, and execute continuous improvement initiatives.
* Establish governance, reporting, and escalation processes that identify performance gaps and support accountability, risk mitigation, root-cause analysis, and measurable improvement.

*Other duties may be assigned as needed to meet Company goals.*

  
  

**Basic Requirements**
----------------------

* **Degree or equivalent experience. Typically requires 12+ years of professional experience and 4+ years of management experience.**
* Demonstrated professional experience in **Revenue Cycle Management or Revenue Cycle Operations**, including accounts receivable or related healthcare financial operations.
* Experience leading **third-party vendors, outsourced operations, or Business Process Outsourcing (BPO)** relationships, including vendor performance, SLAs, KPIs, or contract performance.
* Experience with **credit balance management**, including refunds, adjustments, resolution, aging, or related accounts receivable processes.
* Experience with **Revenue Cycle quality assurance, auditing, controls, or performance improvement**.
* Experience leading cross-functional teams and initiatives across complex or multi-site healthcare operations.
  

  

**Preferred Skills/Experience**
-------------------------------

* Experience leading Revenue Cycle functions across hospital, physician, infusion, or other healthcare environments.
* Demonstrated experience with root-cause analysis, process standardization, continuous improvement, risk mitigation, and corrective action planning.
* Strong ability to influence internal stakeholders and external partners and translate complex operational and financial information into actionable business decisions.
  

  
  

This position offers the possibility of a hybrid work arrangement based on recent updates to our in-office/work‑from‑home model. If located in DFW area, the selected candidate may be expected to work on‑site at our Las Colinas office a minimum of two (2) days per week, with the remaining days worked remotely. Specific in‑office days may be designated according to team needs and business priorities.

We are proud to offer a competitive compensation package at McKesson as part of our Total Rewards. records.description:
**About Tutor**
---------------

We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.

Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

**The Role**
------------

As Head of Technical Operations, you’ll own manufacturing, supply chain, quality, field service and robot operations. We build hundreds of robots a year today and need to build a lot more. You’ll own how we get there, including the teams, suppliers and facilities, and work closely with engineering along the way.

You’ll report to the CTO. This is an onsite role in Watertown, MA.

**What You'll Own**
-------------------

* Scaling production from hundreds of robots a year to many more
* Manufacturing, supply chain, quality, field service and robot operations
* The teams, suppliers and facilities behind production
* A close partnership with engineering

**Requirements**
----------------

* Ran manufacturing or operations at a company that builds complex hardware in volume
* Built an operations function and hired the people who run it
* Been responsible for a fleet of products in the field, including service and support
* Sets clear targets and hires well
* Comfortable on a factory floor

**Nice to have:**

* Robotics, or other products that combine hardware and software
* Experience with contract manufacturers
* Experience with quality systems

**What to Expect**
------------------

We want you to know exactly what to expect. Here’s what our interview process typically looks like:

* **Recruiter interview:** A conversation with a member of our Recruiting team about your background and what you’re looking for.
* **Hiring manager interview:** A deeper conversation with the hiring manager about the role and your experience.
* **Onsite:** A presentation with the team, 1:1s with key team members, and a tour of our facility.

Some roles include additional steps, such as a technical assessment or take-home exercise. If yours does, we’ll let you know up front. Throughout the process, we’ll aim to keep you updated at each step as quickly as possible.

**Why Tutor?**
--------------

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

**Benefits**
------------

We take care of our team so they can do their best work. At Tutor, you’ll get:

* Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium.
* A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.
* Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
* Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

Compensation Range: $250K - $350K

We are seeking a Head of Production & Supply Chain Operations to lead our Hardware Production Team and the end-to-end logistics and inventory function that keeps Carbon’s global supply chain running. This role is critical to scaling our production operations while maintaining our commitment to safety, quality, and cost efficiency, while ensuring the accuracy, compliance, and reliable flow of Carbon’s inventory and freight worldwide. The ideal candidate is a disciplined, detail-oriented leader who thrives in a hands-on manufacturing environment, knows how to build, inspire, and motivate high-performing teams, and can operate effectively across both production and supply chain disciplines. Reporting to the Director of Supply Chain, this individual will own the end-to-end production process and the logistics and inventory organization, driving continuous improvement and ensuring our products and materials meet the highest standards from supplier to customer.

  

***This role will be spending time at both our Thomas Rd, Santa Clara and Borregas Ave, Sunnyvale locations and you will be expected to be in-office 5 days per week.***

  

**What You Will Do**

  

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Recruit, hire, onboard, and develop a team of manufacturing technicians and logistics and inventory staff, building a culture rooted in accountability, pride in craftsmanship, and continuous learning.
* Set clear performance expectations and conduct regular coaching sessions, performance reviews, and skills assessments to elevate individual and team capabilities across production and logistics/inventory functions.
* Foster a positive, motivated work environment where team members feel valued and engaged, resulting in strong retention and morale.
Create training programs and cross-training plans to ensure workforce flexibility and depth across all production stations and logistics/inventory operations.  

  

**Safety**

* Champion a safety-first culture across the production floor and logistics and warehouse operations, ensuring compliance with all OSHA regulations and company safety policies.
* Conduct regular safety audits, risk assessments, and incident investigations; implement corrective and preventive actions promptly.
* Develop, maintain, and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs) that prioritize operator and warehouse safety in every task.
Track and report safety metrics, driving toward zero-incident goals through proactive hazard identification and mitigation.  

  

**Quality**

* Own product quality throughout the manufacturing and assembly process, ensuring every product meets rigorous quality standards before shipment.
* Implement and manage quality control checkpoints, inspection protocols, and testing procedures at critical stages of production.
* Collaborate with Ops Engineering and Quality teams to resolve defects, perform root cause analysis, and drive corrective actions.
Monitor yield rates and first-pass quality metrics, using data to drive continuous improvement initiatives.  

  

**Cost & Operational Efficiency**

* Manage production budgets, labor costs, and material utilization to meet or exceed cost targets without compromising safety or quality.
* Own budget and cost outcomes for Carbon’s freight, logistics, and inventory programs.
* Identify and implement process improvements using Lean manufacturing principles to reduce waste, improve throughput, and increase efficiency.
* Plan and manage production schedules, capacity, and resource allocation to meet delivery commitments and customer demand.
Partner with Strategic Sourcing and Planning to optimize inventory levels and ensure timely availability of components and materials.  

  

**Logistics & Inventory Leadership**

* Own management accountability for the cost, service levels, and integrity of Carbon’s global goods flow, including all inbound and outbound freight and global inventory accuracy and compliance.
* Lead, mentor, and directly manage the team of inventory and logistics staff, setting priorities and building scalable processes as Carbon grows.
* Ensure full compliance with international trade regulations and dangerous goods/hazardous materials requirements.
Establish and track logistics and inventory KPIs (cost per shipment, on-time delivery, inventory accuracy, freight as a percentage of revenue) and drive continuous improvement against them.  

  

**Cross-Functional Collaboration & Reporting**

* Serve as the primary liaison between the production floor and the Engineering, Supply Chain, and Quality teams to ensure seamless product launches and design-for-manufacturability feedback.
* Serve as the primary management point of contact for Finance, Legal, EH&S, Sales, contract manufacturing partners, and 3PLs on logistics, inventory, and trade compliance matters.
* Participate in new product introduction processes, contributing manufacturing insights during design reviews and pilot builds.
Provide regular production, logistics, and inventory status reports, KPIs, and escalation updates to senior leadership.  

  

**Qualifications**

  

**Required:**

* 8+ years of experience in a manufacturing or production management role, with demonstrated success leading teams of technicians or production operators.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related field.
* Experience managing, overseeing, or working closely with logistics, freight, and inventory functions, including leading teams responsible for freight and inventory control.
* Proven ability to build, develop, and motivate high-performing teams in a hands-on manufacturing environment, with a track record of maintaining safe production environments.
* Strong technical aptitude with the ability to understand complex electromechanical assemblies and manufacturing processes.
* Demonstrated discipline and meticulous attention to detail in managing production operations, documentation, and quality systems.
* Experience managing budgets, schedules, and resource planning.
Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to partner effectively with a senior individual-contributor expert to translate strategy into team execution.  

  

**Nice to Have:**

* Understanding of workplace safety regulations (OSHA).
* Lean manufacturing certification (e.g., Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt).
* Experience with ISO 9001 or similar quality management systems.
* Background in 3D printing, additive manufacturing, or precision hardware production.
* Experience with ERP/MRP systems and production tracking tools.
* Familiarity with Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) principles.
Familiarity with international trade compliance and dangerous goods/hazardous materials regulations.  

  

*You do not need to match every listed expectation to apply for this position. Here at Carbon, we know that diverse perspectives foster the innovation we need to be successful, and we are committed to building a team that encompasses a variety of backgrounds, experiences, and skills.*

  

By clicking the “APPLY FOR THIS JOB” button and submitting your job application, you agree you have reviewed the complete Privacy Notice for Employees, Independent Contractors and Job Applicants , which explains the categories of personal information we collect about you, the purposes for which the categories of personal information shall be used and your rights with respect to our use of such personal Information.

  
  

At Carbon, we look at the person holistically and carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining salary. The compensation bracket for this position is $182,400 - $273,600 (per year). In order to maintain equitable internal pay practices, we aim to hire new employees near the midpoint of $228,000 taking into account your experience, work location, certifications, and the unique skills you bring to the role. If you are not based in our Sunnyvale office, the range above will be adjusted for the geographical differential associated with your actual work location.

  

For more information on how we modify your pay based on your location, please refer to our geographic differentials chart .

  
  

Carbon also offers to our eligible employees a comprehensive total rewards package that includes equity, benefits, and time off programs. For details on our total rewards package, visit https://www.carbon3d.com/about/life-at-carbon .

records.description:
**Director of Quality**

Job Type: Full time - Permanent

Location: Bethel, CT📍

A global, private equity backed medical device contract manufacturer is growing fast. With around 20 ISO 13485 certified sites, they make the precision components and sub-assemblies inside many of the world's leading medical devices, from laser-processed nitinol to thin-wall tubing. They're now looking for a Director of Quality to lead product quality and QMS compliance at one of their largest manufacturing sites.

**What you'll do:**

* Own manufacturing quality performance end to end, partnering with Operations to build quality into daily production
* Drive SPC, process capability and data-led problem solving directly on the manufacturing floor
* Lead validation strategy (IQ/OQ/PQ) and quality for New Product Introduction, from development into full-scale production
* Keep the QMS inspection-ready against ISO 13485 and 21 CFR 820, and host FDA inspections and ISO audits
* Be the senior quality contact for high-visibility customers and lead the supplier quality program
* Build, mentor and train a quality team in tools like pFMEA, Gage R&R, RCA and CAPA

**What you'll bring:**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering or management
* 7+ years in a medical device quality management role
* Hands-on manufacturing quality leadership in an ISO 13485 / 21 CFR 820 environment
* Experience hosting FDA inspections and ISO audits
* Lean and/or Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt
* Contract manufacturing, finished device assembly, sterilization oversight, eQMS / ERP and CQA (preferred)
* Willingness to travel around 25%

This is a chance to lead quality at a flagship site within a high-growth medtech manufacturer, with real influence on how quality scales across a global network.

records.title: Vice President of Quality
records.description:
**Vice President Quality**

**Global Product Distribution Quality**

**The Opportunity**

Our client is a leading global medical technology company looking to appoint a hands-on VP Global Product Distribution Quality. Reporting directly to the SVP of Corporate Quality, you will be responsible for developing and implementing business strategies to effectively manage all global product distribution quality. In this role, you will lead the global product distribution quality organization and processes, holding quality management accountability for all captive and outsourced distribution centres across every entity worldwide.

This is a genuine turnaround and organizational design mandate, rather than a caretaker or step-up role. You will step in to stabilize day-to-day operations, manage significant FDA and global regulatory scrutiny, and reshape the commercial quality infrastructure into a world-class function. For a seasoned executive who enjoys building progressive systems at scale, there is a clear path to expanded enterprise responsibility within 6 to 20 months.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Global Distribution Governance:**
 Own quality management systems/compliance performance across captive/3PL distribution centres globally - alongside full P&L, budget, and headcount accountability for the function.
* **Turnaround & Future-State Design:**
 Audit current teams, workflows, and systems to close compliance gaps, restructuring the global commercial quality organization into a streamlined, best-in-class model.
* **FDA & Global Regulatory Execution:**
 Act as the single accountable global executive for all distribution-related regulatory inspections, audit responses, and direct agency communications, including intensive FDA engagement.
* **Quality Systems & Digital Traceability:**
 Direct the IT partnership to optimize warehouse management systems (WMS), end-to-end product traceability, inventory controls, and nonconforming product containment.
* **Enterprise Leadership:**
 Serve as the global subject matter expert for distribution quality and contribute to enterprise-wide quality strategy as a senior member of the Global Corporate Quality leadership team.

**Candidate Profile**

* **Sitting or Recent Med-Tech VP:**
 Minimum 10 years of global organizational leadership at the Vice President level within medical devices, capital equipment, or adjacent life sciences—ready to deliver impact from day one.
* **Post-Manufacturing & 3PL Mastery:**
 Deep operational expertise in commercial, supply chain, and global distribution quality across multi-site networks (upstream supplier quality into manufacturing is out of scope).
* **Proven Remediation Track Record:**
 Demonstrated success leading quality turnarounds, organizational redesigns, and systemic remediation under active FDA scrutiny.
* **Global Trade & Customs Compliance:**
 Hands-on command of international medical device regulations, import/export laws, embargoes, import bans, and regional market-entry barriers.
* **Academic Foundation:**
 Bachelor of Science in a medical or applied science discipline

**What Sets You Apart**

You lead from the front with high energy and a clear appetite for complex turnarounds. You combine sharp analytical rigor with executive presence, enabling you to influence across commercial, supply chain, and regulatory stakeholders while building high-performing global teams.
